# Cox proportional-hazards models in Phase 3 trials: trial-level details

Companion to [`Cox_Models_Findings.md`](Cox_Models_Findings.md). One section per census entry whose `README.md` text mentions a Cox / proportional-hazards model, in README order. Each section lists every Cox model found in the entry's Phase 3 (or Phase 2/3) trials, from the README entry and from the FDA reviews, SAPs and publications it links to. Entries whose only Cox use is outside a Phase 3 trial are kept with a short exclusion note.

Each model ends with **Verbatim specification excerpts**: passages and SAS/R code copied from the source documents. Every excerpt was checked against the downloaded PDF text; excerpts that could only be matched in part (page breaks, tables, garbled text layers) are marked. Page numbers are PDF page indices and can differ from printed page numbers. `[...]` marks omitted text, usually running page headers or footers. Fields reading *Not stated* were not found in any source consulted.

## Oncology

### Pembrolizumab (Keytruda) — BLA 125514/S-012

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC. Approval year: 2016. Phase-3 trial(s): KEYNOTE-024 (MK-3475-024), NCT02142738, Phase 3

#### Model 1: KEYNOTE-024 (MK-3475-024), NCT02142738, Phase 3 — PFS per RECIST 1.1 by BICR (primary (also PFS sensitivity analyses 1-2 with alternative censoring))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Randomization factors (Section 5.4): geography (East Asia vs non-East Asia), ECOG PS (0 vs 1), histology (squamous vs non-squamous); IxRS vs CRF source not stated
- Covariates: Treatment only ("single treatment covariate")
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank test for hypothesis testing; HR and 95% CI from stratified Cox (CI method, Wald vs profile likelihood, not stated); one-sided alpha 2.5% (or 2.0% if ORR negative)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated for PFS; supportive Finkelstein interval-censored likelihood score test if assessment-schedule/censoring imbalance
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: PD dated at first documented PD regardless of drug discontinuation; censored at last disease assessment (before new anticancer therapy if started); sensitivity 1 censors PD/death after >=2 missed assessments; sensitivity 2 counts treatment discontinuation/new therapy as PD
- Interim/sample size: Single PFS analysis at ~175 events; ~98%/97% power for HR 0.55 at one-sided alpha 2.5%/2.0%; critical HR ~0.744/0.738; sample size in EAST and R gsDesign
- Software: Sample size: EAST and R gsDesign; analysis software not stated
- Result: HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.37, 0.68), stratified log-rank p<0.001; events 73/154 (47%) pembrolizumab vs 116/151 (77%) chemotherapy (label Table 9)
- FDA comments: No FDA statistical review publicly posted for this supplement; label states HR based on stratified Cox model
- Spec source: Protocol/SAP §8.1.1 Table 8, §8.2.5.1.1, §8.2.7, §8.2.9.1; USPI Table 9

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The non-parametric Kaplan-Meier method will be used to estimate the PFS curve in each treatment group. The treatment difference in PFS will be assessed by the stratified log-rank test. A stratified Cox proportional hazard model with Efron's method of tie handling will be used to assess the magnitude of the treatment difference (i.e., HR) between the treatment arms. The HR and its 95% CI from the stratified Cox model with Efron's method of tie handling and with a single treatment covariate will be reported. The same stratification factors used for randomization (see Section 5.4) willbe applied to both the stratified log-rank test and the stratified Cox model."
>
> — KEYNOTE-024 Protocol MK-3475-024-11 (incl. SAP Section 8), 20-Dec-2017, PDF p. 119 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/38/NCT02142738/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

> "In order to evaluate the robustness of the PFS endpoint, two sensitivity analyses will be performed with a different set of censoring rules. Sensitivity analysis 1 is the same as the primary analysis except that it censors at the last disease assessment without PD when PD or death is documented after more than one missed disease assessment. Sensitivity analysis 2 is the same as the primary analysis except that it considers discontinuation of treatment or initiation of new anticancer treatment, whichever occurs later, to be a PD event for subjects without documented PD or death."
>
> — KEYNOTE-024 Protocol MK-3475-024-11 (incl. SAP Section 8), 20-Dec-2017, PDF p. 119 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/38/NCT02142738/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

> "The pembrolizumab arm will be compared to the SOC arm. An observed HR of ~0.738 or less would demonstrate PFS superiority at α = 2% (one-sided) assuming ORR is negative at the first interim analysis, or an observed HR of ~0.744 or less if α = 2.5 % (one-sided) assuming ORR is positive at the first interim analysis. This HR approximately corresponds to at least 1.9-2.0 month improvement of the median PFS from 5.5 months in the SOC arm."
>
> — KEYNOTE-024 Protocol MK-3475-024-11 (incl. SAP Section 8), 20-Dec-2017, PDF p. 126 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/38/NCT02142738/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

> "Based on the stratified Cox proportional hazard model † P-value is compared with 0.0118 of the allocated alpha for this interim analysis."
>
> — Keytruda USPI (2016, S-012), PDF p. 21 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/125514s012lbl.pdf)

#### Model 2: KEYNOTE-024 (MK-3475-024), NCT02142738, Phase 3 — Overall survival (secondary (alpha-controlled, step-down after PFS); includes crossover sensitivity analyses)

- Model type: stratified Cox; sensitivity analysis treating new-therapy initiation as a time-dependent binary covariate (model class not named); RPSFT crossover adjustment
- Stratification: Same randomization factors as PFS (geography, ECOG PS, histology)
- Covariates: Treatment only; time-dependent new-therapy indicator in one sensitivity analysis
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank test; HR/95% CI from stratified Cox; Hwang-Shih-DeCani alpha spending (gamma -0.4)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / "In case the proportional hazards assumption doesn’t hold, Fleming and Harrington’s weighted log-rank test or other methods" after crossover adjustment
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Sensitivity analysis censoring at initiation of new therapy
- Interim/sample size: Interim OS at the PFS analysis (~110 deaths; tested at ~1.5% one-sided, empirical HR <~0.661); final ~170 deaths dropped after Amendment 08; actual interim at 108 deaths vs allocated alpha 0.0118
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.41, 0.89), stratified log-rank p=0.005; deaths 44/154 (29%) vs 64/151 (42%) (label Table 9)
- FDA comments: No FDA statistical review publicly posted
- Spec source: Protocol/SAP §8.2.5.1.2, §8.2.9.1; USPI Table 9

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The Kaplan-Meier method will be used to estimate the survival curves. The treatment difference in survival will be assessed by the stratified log-rank test. A stratified Cox proportional hazard model with Efron's method of tie handling will be used to assess the magnitude of the treatment difference (i.e., the HR). The HR and its 95% CI from the stratified Cox model with a single treatment covariate will be reported. The same stratification factors used for randomization (see Section 5.4) will be applied to both the stratified log-rank test and the stratified Cox model."
>
> — KEYNOTE-024 Protocol MK-3475-024-11 (incl. SAP Section 8), 20-Dec-2017, PDF p. 120 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/38/NCT02142738/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

> "To further account for the possible confounding effect, a sensitivity analysis of OS that censors subjects at the time of initiation of new therapy will be performed and an OS analysis that treats initiation of new therapy as a time-dependent binary covariate will also be conducted. In case the proportional hazards assumption doesn’t hold, Fleming and Harrington’s weighted log-rank test or other methods, as appropriate, willbe conducted, after proper adjustment of the crossover effect over time."
>
> — KEYNOTE-024 Protocol MK-3475-024-11 (incl. SAP Section 8), 20-Dec-2017, PDF p. 121 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/38/NCT02142738/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

> "Via the group sequentialapproach with the predefined alpha-spending function (assuming that PFS is statistically significant), the superiority hypothesis will be tested at the type I error of 1.5% with ~110 deaths. An empirical HR < ~0.661, i.e., at least 6.7-month improvement in median OS, would demonstrate OS superiority."
>
> — KEYNOTE-024 Protocol MK-3475-024-11 (incl. SAP Section 8), 20-Dec-2017, PDF p. 126 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/38/NCT02142738/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

### Osimertinib (Tagrisso) — NDA 208065/S-008

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP. Approval year: 2018. Phase-3 trial(s): FLAURA (D5160C00007), NCT02296125, Phase 3

Note: the primary PFS HR is NOT from a Cox model. SAP Ed. 3.0 (amendment 22-Feb-2017) reverted to HR/CI "obtained directly from the U and V statistics" of the stratified log-rank test (Breslow ties), after the 16-Dec-2016 amendment had switched to a Cox model; the label footnotes the HR as a "Pike estimator". Cox models are used for subgroup/interaction analyses and the PH check. OS uses "the same methodology and model as for the analysis of PFS" (i.e., U/V), so OS is not listed as a Cox model.

#### Model 1: FLAURA (D5160C00007), NCT02296125, Phase 3 — PFS (investigator, RECIST 1.1) by prespecified subgroups (sex, race, age, brain mets, smoking, WHO PS, T790M, EGFR mutation, ctDNA, central EGFR) plus an overall treatment-only Cox HR for the forest plot (subgroup (supportive))

- Model type: standard Cox (unstratified) with treatment-by-subgroup interaction
- Stratification: None stated for the subgroup models
- Covariates: Treatment, subgroup covariate, treatment-by-subgroup interaction; separate treatment-only Cox model also fitted
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: HR and two-sided 95% CI per subgroup level from the interaction model; no multiplicity adjustment
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Subgroups with <20 events per level not formally analysed
- Interim/sample size: Primary PFS at ~359 events, 90% power for HR 0.71 (2-sided 5%); not specific to subgroup models
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG
- Result: Not stated in retrieved documents
- FDA comments: No FDA review publicly posted
- Spec source: SAP Ed. 3.0 §4.3.8.1 "Subgroup analysis"

> "For each subgroup, the HR and 95% CI will be calculated from a single Cox proportional hazards model that contains a term for treatment, the subgroup covariate of interest and the treatment by subgroup interaction term. The treatment effect HR will be obtained for each level of the subgroup from this model. The Cox models will be fitted using SAS® PROC PHREG with the Efron method to control for ties."

This will be performed in the overall population by comparing the fit of a Cox proportional hazards model including treatment, covariates for race (Asian versus Non-Asian) and mutation type (Ex19del versus L858R), and all covariate by treatment interaction terms, with one that excludes the interaction terms and will be assessed at the two-sided 10% significance level. #### Model 4: FLAURA (D5160C00007), NCT02296125, Phase 3 — PFS (investigator) — primary analysis PH check (PH assumption diagnostic for primary (non-Cox) analysis)

- Model type: time-dependent covariate Cox (treatment-by-time or treatment-by-ln(time) interaction), fitted only if complementary log-log plots raise concerns
- Stratification: Primary analysis stratified by race and mutation type (IVRS values)
- Covariates: Treatment plus treatment-by-time or treatment-by-ln(time)
- Ties: Breslow for primary stratified log-rank test

- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Complementary log-log vs log(time) plots, then time-dependent covariate / Piecewise HRs over time periods (0-6m, 6-12m, ...); average-HR interpretation unless extensive crossing
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: ~359 PFS events, 90% power for HR 0.71, 2-sided alpha 5%, minimum critical HR 0.81; OS interim + final (~318 deaths) with Lan-DeMets O’Brien-Fleming-type spending
- Software: SAS PROC LIFETEST with STRATA (for U/V); PHREG for Cox models
- Result: Primary PFS HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.37, 0.57), p<0.0001; events 136/279 vs 206/277 (label Table 6; Pike estimator, not Cox)
- FDA comments: No FDA review publicly posted
- Spec source: SAP Ed. 3.0 §4.3.8.1 and amendment history; Protocol §8.5; USPI Table 6

If a lack of proportionality is evident, the variation in treatment effect can be described by presenting piecewise HR calculated over distinct time-periods for example 0-6m, 6-12m etc. In such circumstances, the HR from the primary analysis can still be meaningfully interpreted as an average HR over time unless there is extensive crossing of the survival curves. If lack of proportionality is found this may be a result of a treatment-by-covariate interaction, which will be investigated."

### Venetoclax (Venclexta) — NDA 208573/S-013

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: AbbVie Inc. (with Genentech/Roche). Approval year: 2019. Phase-3 trial(s): CLL14 (BO25323), NCT02242942, Phase 3

README discrepancy: README (from Protocol v7) says the stratified log-rank/Cox use Binet stage only. The posted SAP (v2, 08-Nov-2018; not listed in README) stratifies the log-rank test and Cox model by Binet stage AND geographic region, and the label footnote confirms the HR came from a Cox model stratified by Binet stage and geographic region. Parts of the FDA Multi-Discipline Review have a garbled text layer (digits/Greek letters); only clean passages are quoted.

#### Model 1: CLL14 (BO25323), NCT02242942, Phase 3 — Investigator-assessed PFS (iwCLL 2008) (primary (protocol); sensitivity analyses: unstratified log-rank, censoring at new anti-CLL therapy, censoring after >1 missed visit)

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: SAP: Binet stage (A/B/C) and geographic region (IxRS); Protocol v7 text: Binet stage only
- Covariates: Treatment only (implied; not explicitly stated)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided stratified log-rank test at 0.05 adjusted for interim (gamma-family spending, gamma -9.21; boundary 0.0019 at IA with 110 events); HR with 95% CI from stratified Cox
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last disease assessment; no post-baseline assessment censored at randomization + 1 day
- Interim/sample size: 170 PFS events for 80% power to detect HR 0.65 (27 vs 41.5 months), exponential, 10% annual dropout; interim at 110 events crossed boundary 0.0019 and became the primary analysis
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.35 (95% CI 0.23, 0.53), stratified log-rank p<0.0001 (FDA MDR Table 4; event counts garbled in text layer)
- FDA comments: FDA considers IRC-assessed PFS the primary outcome; FDA agrees with applicant for the majority of analyses
- Spec source: SAP §4.4.1, §4.4.3, §4.4.5; Protocol v7 §6.4.1; FDA MDR

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Treatment comparisons will be made using a two-sided log-rank test (at 0.05 significance-level, adjusted for the interim analysis), stratified by Binet stage and Geographic Region. If the null hypothesis is rejected and the observed stratified HR is favorable for the obinutuzumab  venetoclax experimental arm, then it is concluded that obinutuzumab  venetoclax significantly lowers the risk of PFS events more than GClb. Median PFS and the 95% confidence limits will be estimated using Brookmeyer Crowley method, with the Kaplan-Meier survival curve presented to provide a visual description. PFS rates for 1, 2, and 3 years after randomization with 95% CIs using Brookmeyer Crowley method will be reported. Estimates of the treatment effect will be expressed as HR including 95% confidence limits estimated through a Cox proportional-hazards analysis stratified by Binet stage and Geographic Region. Primary analysis for FDA submission will be based on assessment of PFS by an IRC."
>
> — CLL14 SAP BO25323 (v2, 08-Nov-2018), PDF p. 19 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/42/NCT02242942/SAP_000.pdf)

Stopping only one component of the randomized study treatment will not be considered a reason for censoring patients.  To assess the impact of missing assessments on PFS, an analysis on PFS will be performed by censoring those patients who progressed, relapsed or died after missing more than one visit consecutively at their last adequate response assessment date before the missed visits."

### Ipilimumab (Yervoy) — BLA 125377

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Bristol-Myers Squibb Company. Approval year: 2011. Phase-3 trial(s): MDX010-20 (CA184-002), NCT00094653, Phase 3

The FDA Statistical Review PDF has no text layer; it was OCR’d with tesseract (200 dpi). Quotes from it are verbatim OCR output, OCR artifacts retained (e.g., "Mla" for M1a, "Mic" for M1c).

#### Model 1: MDX010-20 (CA184-002), NCT00094653, Phase 3 — Overall survival: ipi+gp100 vs gp100 (primary), ipi vs gp100 and ipi+gp100 vs ipi (secondary) (primary + secondary comparisons)

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Baseline M-stage (M0, M1a or M1b vs M1c) and prior IL-2 (yes/no), from randomization data
- Covariates: Treatment only (implied)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank test for p-value; 2-sided CI from stratified Cox; secondary comparisons not multiplicity-adjusted. Publication says Cox models were also used "to test for significance"
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Delayed-effect assumption used only in sample-size simulation
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Alive patients censored at last contact (last known alive date)
- Interim/sample size: After Amendment 6 (BORR->OS): simulation assuming delayed effect (HR 1 before month 8); 385 deaths in ipi+gp100 vs gp100 for 90% power (~481 total)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: ipi+gp100 vs gp100 HR 0.68 (0.55, 0.85), p=0.0004; ipi vs gp100 0.66 (0.51, 0.87), p=0.0026; ipi+gp100 vs ipi 1.04 (0.83, 1.3), p=0.7575; deaths 306/403, 100/137, 119/136
- FDA comments: Reviewer checked censoring balance via reverse-censoring stratified log-rank (p>0.8); secondary p-values unadjusted
- Spec source: FDA StatR §3.2.4, Table 4 (OCR); Hodi et al. 2010 Methods

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary analysis for all time-to-event endpoints was based on a stratified log-rank test stratified by the baseline stratification factors (i.e. baseline M-stage [M0, Mla or Mlb vs. Mlc] and prior treatment with IL-2 or not). The Kaplan-Meier method was used to plot the survival estimates for OS. The median OS and its 95% confidence interval were calculated using the method of Brookmeyer and Crowley. The hazard ratio and the corresponding 2-sided confidence intervals were estimated using the Cox’s proportional hazards model stratified by baseline M-stage and prior treatment IL-2."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125377 [OCR of scanned PDF, tesseract], PDF p. 20 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125377Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Cox model for Hazard ratios (HR) and log-rank test p-values were stratified by baseline M-stage at randomization (M0, Mla, M1b vs. Mic) and prior treatment with IL-2 (Yes vs. No) using the data from the randomization. 95% confidence intervals (CI) for HR were computed using Cox model."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125377 [OCR of scanned PDF, tesseract], PDF p. 27 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125377Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Based on the simulation, it shows that a total of 385 deaths in ipilimumab+gp100 vs. gp100 arm can achieve a 90% power. It is estimated that approximately a total of 481 events are required in all 3 groups (assuming events are evenly distributed among the 3 arms according to the randomization ratio) to observe 385 events in the ipilimumab+gp100 and gp100 treated arms."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125377 [OCR of scanned PDF, tesseract], PDF p. 20 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125377Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "To evaluate the censoring distribution among treatment arms, stratified log rank tests were performed for all paired comparisons by switching the censoring indicator, The results show that the censoring distribution appears to be compatible between arms (the nominal p-values for all pair-wise comparisons are >0.8)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, BLA 125377 [OCR of scanned PDF, tesseract], PDF p. 27 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/125377Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Cox proportional-hazards models, stratified according to metastasis status and receipt or nonreceipt of previous interleukin therapy, were used to estimate hazard ratios and to test for significance of the timing of events."
>
> — Hodi et al. NEJM 2010 (PMC author manuscript, BioC text; no PDF pagination) (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3549297/)

### Vandetanib (Caprelsa) — NDA 022405

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP. Approval year: 2011. Phase-3 trial(s): ZETA (D4200C00058, Study 58), NCT00410761, Phase 3

The applicant derived the PFS HR from the log-rank test (not Cox); the Cox models below are FDA reviewer analyses (and the labeled HR 0.35 is FDA’s Cox estimate). Randomization was stratified only by site (blocks of 3), so the models are unstratified.

#### Model 1: ZETA (D4200C00058, Study 58), NCT00410761, Phase 3 — PFS by independent (central) review, FAS (primary (FDA analysis))

- Model type: standard Cox (unstratified)
- Stratification: None (randomization stratified by site in blocks of 3)
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided log-rank p-value; HR/95% CI from Cox (FDA). Applicant: HR/CI derived from log-rank results
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: FDA: investigator-only progression censored at last RECIST assessment before study-drug discontinuation; censored before on-study radiotherapy; no measurable baseline disease censored at Day 1. Applicant did not apply these
- Interim/sample size: 90 events for >80% power to detect doubling of median PFS (12-month control), 2-sided 0.05; no PFS interim
- Software: Not stated
- Result: FDA: HR 0.352 (0.235, 0.527), p<0.0001; events 59/231 vs 41/100. Applicant (log-rank based): 0.46 (0.31, 0.69). Label: 0.35 (0.24-0.53)
- FDA comments: Statistical issue #8: applicant used log-rank-derived HR whereas FDA used Cox; issue #2: censoring-rule differences
- Spec source: FDA StatR §1.3, §3.1.7.2, §3.1.8.3 Table 5; USPI Table 3

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "A log-rank test was performed for the primary analysis of PFS based on the ITT population. Results are presented in terms of an estimate of the hazard ratio (vandetanib:placebo) associated confidence interval, and p-value."

> "Reviewer’s comment: The applicant derived the hazard ratio estimate and its confidence interval based on the results from the log-rank test whereas FDA used the Cox proportional hazards model to derive these numbers."

> "The hazard ratios of vandetanib over placebo and 95% confidence intervals for PFS were 0.352 [95% CI: (0.235, 0.527)] and 0.46 [95% CI: (0.31, 0.69)] in FDA’s and applicant’s analyses, respectively."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 022405, PDF p. 27 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022405Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The censoring rules of FDA and the applicant were different for primary PFS analysis based on IRC review. Following is a list of censoring rules that are different for FDA’s and the applicant’s analyses. • PFS for the patients with investigator-determined, but without IRC determined progression have been censored at their last RECIST assessment prior to discontinuation of study drug for FDA’s analysis. While the sponsor’s analysis may address informative censoring and conform to ITT analysis, this analysis includes effect of non-protocol treatment beyond investigator determined progression. • For the patients who received radiation during the study period, FDA’s analysis censored PFS at the last RECIST assessment prior to radiation therapy."

> "In this study, randomization was stratified by site in blocks of 3. If a site did not use all the randomization numbers in a given block, it would be expected that the ratio of patients assigned to the vandetanib group relative to those assigned to the placebo group would not be equal to 2."

> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 022405, PDF p. 10 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022405Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "statistically significant improvement in PFS for patients randomized to vandetanib (Hazard Ratio = 0.35; 95% Confidence Interval (CI) = 0.24-0.53; p<0.0001)."

> "OS was compared between the two treatment groups in the ITT population using the stratified log-rank test with stratification factors at randomization from IWRS: baseline ECOG performance status, baseline pain, number of prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens, and documented type of prostate cancer progression at entry. Survival curves were generated using Kaplan-Meier estimates. The following sensitivity analyses were conducted by the applicant to evaluate the robustness of the primary analysis: a stratified log-rank test using stratification factors based on eCRF data, a non-stratified log-rank test, and an analysis excluding subjects with major protocol deviations. The reviewer also performed a worst-case analysis to further evaluate the OS benefit of abiraterone acetate."

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals, Inc.. Approval year: 2012. Phase-3 trial(s): CORRECT (Study 14387), NCT01103323, Phase 3

FDA StatR internal inconsistency: Executive summary reports OS stratified HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.64, 0.93); Table 8 and the label report (0.64, 0.94). The CSR primary analysis used strata reclassified from source documents; IVRS strata were a sensitivity analysis.

#### Model 1: CORRECT (Study 14387), NCT01103323, Phase 3 — Overall survival (primary + sensitivity (IVRS strata; unstratified; FDA alternative strata))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Planned: prior VEGF therapy, time from diagnosis of metastatic disease (>=18 vs <18 months), region (1/2/3). Prior VEGF dropped by FDA (all patients yes). FDA sensitivity: region 1 vs 2+3 + TFDMD; TFDMD only
- Covariates: Treatment only (implied)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank; HR/95% CI from stratified Cox
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: Lan-DeMets O’Brien-Fleming; interim at 432 deaths (74%) with alpha 0.018, crossed (p=0.0102)
- Software: SAS programs provided on FDA request
- Result: HR 0.77 (0.64, 0.94), p=0.0102; deaths 275/505 vs 157/255. IVRS strata 0.77 (0.63, 0.94); unstratified 0.77 (0.63, 0.93)
- FDA comments: 4% IVRS/CRF discordance; degenerate VEGF stratum excluded; programs initially missing
- Spec source: FDA StatR §3.1, §3.2.5, Tables 8-9

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The analysis for OS was performed using a stratified log-rank test, stratified by the same stratification factors as used for randomization: prior treatment with VEGF targeting drugs (yes/no), time from diagnosis of metastatic disease (TFDMD) (≥ 18 months vs. <18 months), and geographical region 1 (North America, Western EU, Israel and Australia) versus region 2 (Asia) versus region 3 (South America, Turkey and Eastern EU). The median OS and survival curves were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier (KM) method. The KM estimates at different time points with corresponding 95% confidence intervals as well as the differences of these estimates were calculated. The hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) of REG/BSC over the PBO/BSC were estimated by a stratified Cox regression procedure."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 203085, PDF p. 12 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203085Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Because all patients received prior VEGF therapy, this reviewer excluded prior VEGF therapy from the stratification log-rank test and stratified CMH test."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 203085, PDF p. 12 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203085Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Overall, the discordance rate between IVRS and CRFs was 4% (33). As part of the applicant’s data collection and monitoring, patients were reclassified based on the source documents. These reclassified strata were used for statistical analyses in the CSR. In the section 3.2.3.6.3, the impact of stratification misclassification is discussed."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 203085, PDF p. 14 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203085Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "This reviewer also conducted two sensitivity analyses using different stratification factors (see Table 9). The first sensitivity analysis used combined region (1 vs. 2+3) and time from diagnosis of metastatic disease (p-value=0.0085). The second sensitivity analysis only used time from diagnosis of metastatic disease (p-value=0.0093). Both sensitivity analysis results were similar to the primary OS analysis."

> "The stratified log-rank test p-value for OS comparison was 0.0102 compared with the allocated alpha of 0.018 at the second interim analysis. The median OS was 6.4 (95% CI: 5.8, 7.3) months for the REG/BSC arm and 5.0 (95% CI: 4.4, 5.8) months for the PBO/BSC arm. The stratified Cox proportional HR was 0.77 with 95% CI (0.64, 0.93)."

> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 203085, PDF p. 6 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203085Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

In addition, some important disease characteristics were not included in the derived demographic dataset. Upon this reviewer’s request, the applicant resubmitted the adequate documentations, derived datasets, and analysis programs. This reviewer was able to duplicate the analysis variable derivation and reproduce applicant’s summary statistics."

#### Model 4: EXAM (XL184-301), NCT00704730 — OS (key secondary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (HR estimation; inference by stratified log-rank test)
- Stratification: Age (≤65 vs >65) and prior TKI (yes/no) (IVRS)
- Covariates: Treatment arm only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank test at two-sided 0.04 (parallel with ORR at 0.01, gated by PFS); 95% and 96% CIs for medians
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last date known alive (alive at cutoff or lost to follow-up)
- Interim/sample size: 217 deaths for 80% power to detect HR 0.667 (two-sided 4%); interim at ~31% information with Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming boundary (expected 0.00006; actual boundary 0.0009 at 44% information)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Interim (6/15/2011 cutoff; 44% info): HR 0.997 (0.644, 1.542), p=0.989, deaths 66/219 vs 30/111. 120-day update (75% info): HR 0.825 (0.598, 1.14), stratified log-rank p=0.2432 in table (text says 0.2993), deaths 103 vs 59
- FDA comments: OS did not cross boundary; reviewer attributed failure to optimistic design assumption (33 vs ~26 months); OS excluded from labeling claims. Internal p-value inconsistency (0.2993 text vs 0.2432/0.2434 tables)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1 and §3.2.3

### Pomalidomide (Pomalyst) — NDA 204026

Therapeutic area: Oncology Sponsor: Celgene Corporation Approval year: 2013 Phase-3 trial(s): None reviewed in the approval package (MM-003/NIMBUS, NCT01311687, Phase 3 confirmatory, not part of the 2013 FDA reviews)

Excluded. The accelerated approval rested on CC-4047-MM-002 (NCT00833833), a randomized Phase 1/2 trial; its SAP specified an unstratified Cox model for the PFS HR, but FDA did not compute HRs because the trial was uncontrolled for the pomalidomide effect. #### Model 1: EMILIA (TDM4370g/BO21977), NCT00829166 — PFS (IRC, modified RECIST 1.0) (co-primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (HR estimation; inference by stratified log-rank test)
- Stratification: World region (US, Western Europe, other), number of prior chemotherapy regimens for advanced disease (0-1 vs >1), visceral vs non-visceral disease (investigator-assessed at randomization)
- Covariates: Treatment arm only
- Ties: Not stated

- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last evaluable tumor assessment; no post-baseline assessment censored at randomization + 1 day; not censored at start of non-protocol therapy (ITT follow-up); publication sensitivity analysis censoring at non-protocol therapy

- Software: Not stated

### Radium Ra 223 dichloride (Xofigo) — NDA 203971

Therapeutic area: Oncology Sponsor: Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc. Approval year: 2013 Phase-3 trial(s): ALSYMPCA (BC1-06), NCT00699751 (Phase 3, randomized 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled)

#### Model 1: ALSYMPCA (BC1-06), NCT00699751 — OS (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (HR estimation; inference by stratified log-rank test)
- Stratification: Total ALP (<220 vs ≥220 U/L), current bisphosphonate use (yes/no), prior docetaxel (yes/no); actual (source-verified) values used in primary analysis, IVRS values in sensitivity
- Covariates: Treatment arm only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank test (two-sided); 95% CI for HR
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Design assumed non-proportional (piecewise) hazards: common hazard first 4 months, then arm- and docetaxel-specific hazards; sample size by simulation
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not deceased censored at last date known alive or lost to follow-up
- Interim/sample size: 640 deaths, 90% power, two-sided 5%; sample size via Cox regression stratified by prior docetaxel with piecewise hazards, simulated in R; interim at 320 deaths (nominal 0.0031, Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming); blinded sample-size re-estimation (Bolland)
- Software: Not stated for analysis (sample-size simulations in R)
- Result: Interim (314 deaths): HR 0.695 (0.552, 0.875), p=0.00185; deaths 191/541 vs 123/268. Updated (528 deaths): HR 0.695 (0.581, 0.832), p=0.00007
- FDA comments: 83 patients (10.3%) had IVRS vs actual stratification discrepancies; FDA confirmed robustness with IVRS-strata sensitivity analysis
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1-3.2.4 (summarizing SAP)

The hazard ratio and corresponding 95% confidence interval were estimated using the Cox proportional hazards model stratified by the same stratification factors."

#### Model 1: METRIC (MEK114267), NCT01245062 — PFS (investigator) (primary — FDA analysis (unstratified Cox) vs SAP (stratified log-rank + Pike))

- Model type: Standard (unstratified) Cox as FDA primary; stratified Cox per CRF and per IVRS as sensitivity

- Software: Not stated (applicant SAS programs judged unexecutable)

### Ramucirumab (Cyramza) — BLA 125477

Therapeutic area: Oncology Sponsor: Eli Lilly and Company (ImClone) Approval year: 2014 Phase-3 trial(s): REGARD (I4T-IE-JVBD), NCT00917384 (Phase 3, randomized 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled)

#### Model 1: REGARD (I4T-IE-JVBD), NCT00917384 — OS (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (HR estimation; inference by stratified log-rank test)
- Stratification: Weight loss over prior 3 months (≥10% vs <10%), geographic region, primary tumor location (gastric vs GEJ), per IVRS/IWRS
- Covariates: Treatment arm only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank test (one-sided α=0.025 in design); 95% CI

- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not dead at study completion or lost to follow-up censored at last date known alive
- Interim/sample size: 268 deaths for 80% power to detect HR 0.69 (one-sided 0.025, 2:1); interim futility at 94 deaths (35%), non-binding Gamma(-1) beta-spending; sample size amended 3 times
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.776 (0.603, 0.998); stratified log-rank p=0.0473; deaths 179/238 vs 99/117; median 5.2 vs 3.8 months
- FDA comments: Reviewer: OS result 'may not be robust'; sample size amended 3 times without Agency statistical review; 27 patients (7.6%) IVRS vs eCRF stratification discrepancies

### panobinostat (Farydak) — NDA 205353

Therapeutic area: Oncology Sponsor: Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation Approval year: 2015 Phase-3 trial(s): PANORAMA-1 (D2308), NCT01023308 (Phase 3, randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled)

#### Model 1: PANORAMA-1 (D2308), NCT01023308 — PFS (investigator, mEBMT) (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox per table footnotes; methods text says PH model 'including treatment arm and the randomization factors' (covariate-adjusted)
- Stratification: Number of prior lines of anti-myeloma therapy (1 vs 2 or 3) and prior bortezomib (yes/no)
- Covariates: Methods text: treatment arm and randomization factors (as covariates); footnotes: stratified
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided stratified log-rank test; 95% CI; O'Brien-Fleming alpha spending
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last adequate assessment before cutoff or new antineoplastic therapy; events after >2 missing assessments censored
- Interim/sample size: ~460 events; 90% power for HR 0.74 (two-sided 5%); interims at 33% (futility) and 80% (efficacy)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.63 (0.52, 0.76); p<0.0001; events 207/387 vs 260/381; median 12.0 vs 8.1 months
- FDA comments: Large censoring limited FDA confidence in primary analysis; IRC PFS showed smaller benefit (HR 0.69, Δ2.2 months)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2 and Table 4

### Dinutuximab (Unituxin) — BLA 125516

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: United Therapeutics Corporation. Approval year: 2015. Phase-3 trial(s): ANBL0032 (COG; DIV-NB-301), NCT00026312, Phase III

The only Cox models are FDA-reviewer hazard-ratio estimates added to the applicant's unstratified log-rank analyses; the protocol-specified primary test was a stratified log-rank test (24 strata), abandoned because of empty strata. The 2021 long-term follow-up publication uses Cox models only for associations of EFS with dinutuximab plasma levels (exposure-response; out of scope).

#### Model 1: ANBL0032 (NCT00026312) — Event-free survival (EFS) (primary; FDA-reviewer HR estimate)

- Model type: Standard (unstratified) Cox PH model, added by FDA reviewer to accompany the applicant's unstratified log-rank test
- Stratification: None in the Cox model. Randomization stratified by pre-ASCT response (CR/VGPR/PR) x pre-ANBL0032 treatment protocol = 24 strata; protocol-specified stratified log-rank replaced by unstratified log-rank because of empty strata
- Covariates: Treatment only (unadjusted)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI from Cox model; test = unstratified log-rank (planned: stratified log-rank, one-sided alpha 0.025)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last contact; 4 RA-alone patients who crossed over to immunotherapy censored at crossover
- Interim/sample size: 137 EFS events for 80% power, one-sided alpha 0.025 stratified log-rank (FDA review states HR 0.25 / 3-yr EFS 65% vs 50%); 7 interim looks every 6 months (FHO boundaries, then Lan-DeMets rho-family at 7th look, boundary p=0.0108); randomization halted after 7th look (p=0.0115)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Jan 13, 2009 cutoff: HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.37, 0.89); unstratified log-rank p=0.0115; events 33/113 vs 50/113. Supportive: June 30, 2009 HR 0.64 (0.43, 0.97), p=0.033, 40/113 vs 54/113; June 30, 2012 HR 0.73 (0.50, 1.06), p=0.099, 49/114 vs 58/114
- FDA comments: Reviewer computed HRs (applicant reported only log-rank p-values); concerns about stopping randomization when p=0.0115 did not cross boundary 0.0108, too many strata, frequent interim looks; Jan 2009 raw dataset corrupted (June 2009 soft lock used)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review only (protocol/SAP not public)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "In addition to the applicant's summary, this reviewer included in the review the medians, the proportion of subjects with events, hazard ratios and corresponding 95% CIs (as calculated using a Cox proportional hazards regression model)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (BLA 125516, Ref ID 3627251), PDF p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125516Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "An unstratified log-rank test was used to perform the analysis since there were a large number of strata (24 strata) and there were no subjects associated to some of these strata."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (BLA 125516, Ref ID 3627251), PDF p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125516Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "the hazard ratio estimate was 0.57 with 95% confidence interval of (0.37, 0.89) obtained from unstratified Cox proportional hazards regression."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (BLA 125516, Ref ID 3627251), PDF p. 5 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125516Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "There were 4 subjects who were in the RA alone arm and crossed over to the Immunotherapy+RA arm and these subjects were censored at the point of crossover for all efficacy analyses."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (BLA 125516, Ref ID 3627251), PDF p. 21 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125516Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The main issue from this study is the concern of terminating the randomization to the RA alone arm by DSMC despite the fact that the observed p-value of 0.0115 (based on the interim analysis) did not cross the pre-specified alpha boundary of 0.0108."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (BLA 125516, Ref ID 3627251), PDF p. 5 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125516Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: ANBL0032 (NCT00026312) — Overall survival (OS) (key secondary; FDA-reviewer HR estimate)

- Model type: Standard (unstratified) Cox PH model (FDA reviewer)
- Stratification: None in the Cox model (planned OS analysis: stratified log-rank)
- Covariates: Treatment only (unadjusted)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI from Cox model; nominal unstratified log-rank p
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last contact; crossover patients censored at crossover
- Interim/sample size: OS analysis not pre-specified (no HR, power, events or timing); no alpha allocated to OS interim test
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Jan 13, 2009 cutoff: HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.30, 0.92); nominal p=0.0223; deaths 19/113 vs 33/113
- FDA comments: OS p-value 'not interpretable'; recommended OS p-value be excluded from labeling
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review

>

### Cobimetinib (Cotellic) — NDA 206192

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Genentech, Inc.. Approval year: 2015. Phase-3 trial(s): coBRIM (GO28141), NCT01689519, Phase III

#### Model 1: coBRIM (NCT01689519) — PFS (investigator-assessed) (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox PH model (HR) with stratified log-rank test
- Stratification: Geographic region (North America, Europe, Australia/NZ/others) and metastatic classification (unresectable IIIc, M1a, M1b vs M1c). Source not pre-specified (IxRS vs CRF); FDA designated IxRS-based analysis as primary
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% CI; stratified log-rank two-sided alpha 0.05; unstratified log-rank and HR also presented
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: No PD/death: censored at last tumor assessment; no post-baseline assessment: censored at randomization; sensitivity censoring at non-protocol anticancer therapy
- Interim/sample size: 206 events for 95% power to detect HR 0.55 (6 vs 11 months), two-sided 0.05; ~500 patients
- Software: Not stated
- Result: IxRS-stratified HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.38, 0.67), p<0.0001; CRF-stratified HR 0.51 (0.39, 0.68); unstratified 0.51 (0.39, 0.68); IRF-assessed 0.60 (0.45, 0.79), p=0.0003; events 79/247 vs 128/248; FDA combined INV+IRF HR 0.55 (0.42, 0.71)
- FDA comments: Applicant did not pre-specify IxRS vs CRF strata; FDA disagreed with CRF-based stratification (not consistent with ITT) and took IxRS-based analysis as primary
- Spec source: Protocol v8 §6.4.1; FDA Statistical Review

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The hazard ratio for PFS will be estimated using a stratified Cox model. Two-sided 95% CIs for the hazard ratio will be provided. The stratified analyses will incorporate 2 stratification factors: geographic region (North America, Europe, Australia/New Zealand/others) and metastatic classification (unresectable Stage IIIc, M1a, and M1b; M1c). Results from an unstratified log-rank test and the unstratified hazard ratio will also be presented."
>
> — GO28141 Protocol v8 (ClinicalTrials.gov), PDF p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/19/NCT01689519/Prot_001.pdf)

> "Data from patients who have not experienced disease progression or death will be censored at the last tumor assessment date. Data from patients with no post-baseline tumor assessment will be censored at the randomization date."
>
> — GO28141 Protocol v8 (ClinicalTrials.gov), PDF p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/19/NCT01689519/Prot_001.pdf)

> "Hazard ratio and its 95% confidence intervals were estimated using the Cox proportional hazards model stratified by region and metastatic classification."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review + Addendum (NDA 206192, Ref ID 3748873/3841271), PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206192Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "FDA does not agree with the applicant's stratified analysis using strata derived from CRF data, because it is not consistent with the ITT principle. FDA considers the stratified PFS analysis using strata recorded from IxRS as the primary analysis and the PFS analysis using strata recorded from CRFs as a supportive analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review + Addendum (NDA 206192, Ref ID 3748873/3841271), PDF p. 16 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206192Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: coBRIM (NCT01689519) — Overall survival (OS) (key secondary (hierarchical after ORR))

- Model type: Stratified Cox PH model with stratified log-rank test
- Stratification: Same as PFS (region, metastatic classification); IxRS primary per FDA, CRF sensitivity
- Covariates: Treatment only

- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Alive at cutoff: censored at last date known alive; no post-baseline survival information: censored at randomization
- Interim/sample size: Two interim OS analyses (at final PFS; at 256/67% events); final at 385 events per FDA review (protocol v8 states ~250 deaths, 80% power, HR 0.70)

- Interim/sample size: Interim ~262 events, final (2nd IA) ~365 events; 365 events for 85% power at HR 0.728 two-sided 0.05; FDA: IA1 boundary 0.023 two-sided at 286 events

### Necitumumab (Portrazza) — BLA 125547

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Eli Lilly and Company. Approval year: 2015. Phase-3 trial(s): SQUIRE, NCT00981058, Phase 3; INSPIRE (I4X-IE-JFCB), NCT00982111, Phase 3 (ClinicalTrials.gov: PHASE3; non-squamous, safety-supportive)

#### Model 1: SQUIRE (I4X-IE-JFCC, NCT00981058) — Overall survival (OS) (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox PH model with stratified log-rank test
- Stratification: ECOG PS (0-1 vs 2) and geographic region (NA/Europe/Australia vs S America/S Africa/India vs E Asia), IVRS/IWRS-recorded (CRF-based sensitivity)

### Olaratumab (Lartruvo) — BLA 761038

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Eli Lilly and Company. Approval year: 2016. Phase-3 trial(s): ANNOUNCE (JGDJ), NCT02451943, Phase 3 confirmatory (post-approval); approval trial JGDG (NCT01185964) was Phase 1b/2

JGDG (stratified Cox for PFS, unstratified Cox for OS) is Phase 1b/2 (ClinicalTrials.gov PHASE1/PHASE2) and is not counted. Models below are from the Phase 3 confirmatory ANNOUNCE SAP v3 and JAMA 2020 publication.

#### Model 1: ANNOUNCE (I5B-MC-JGDJ, NCT02451943) — Overall survival (OS), ITT and LMS populations (dual primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox PH model ('primary Cox PH model') with stratified log-rank test
- Stratification: IWRS randomization factors: prior systemic therapies for advanced disease (0 vs >=1), histology (LMS vs liposarcoma vs pleomorphic vs other), ECOG PS (0 vs 1)
- Covariates: Assigned treatment as the only covariate
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-tailed 95% CI and Wald test p-value; primary test stratified log-rank, one-sided; graphical procedure alpha 0.02 (ITT) / 0.005 (LMS)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Graphical diagnostics using Schoenfeld residuals and log-negative-log survival vs log time (JAMA 2020) / Restricted mean difference in OS up to minimum of the arms' maximum observed times (SAP)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Alive at cutoff or lost to follow-up: censored at last date known alive
- Interim/sample size: 460 patients; final at >=322 ITT and >=131 LMS events; HR 0.723, 80% power at one-sided 0.02 (ITT); interim at 194 ITT events using unstratified Cox HR (many small cells)
- Software: SAS version 9.1.2 (JAMA 2020)
- Result: Total STS HR 1.05 (95% CI 0.84, 1.30), P=.69 (n=258 vs 251); LMS HR 0.95 (0.69, 1.31), P=.76 (n=119 vs 115)
- FDA comments: Not in FDA review (trial ongoing at 2016 approval); failed confirmation led to BLA revocation
- Spec source: ANNOUNCE SAP v3 §5.11.2; JAMA 2020

### Niraparib (Zejula) — NDA 208447

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Tesaro, Inc.. Approval year: 2017. Phase-3 trial(s): NOVA (ENGOT-OV16), NCT01847274, Phase 3

The posted SAP PDF bundles a population PK/exposure-response modeling plan (stratified Cox for PFS vs exposure, cox.zph PH checks) ahead of SAP v3.0; those E-R models are out of scope. The SAP's covariate section is internally ambiguous: stratification factors as PHREG 'strata' but also 'included as covariates'.

#### Model 1: NOVA (PR-30-5011-C, NCT01847274) — PFS per IRC (gBRCAmut cohort; non-gBRCAmut HRD+ subgroup; overall non-gBRCAmut cohort) (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox PH model (baseline hazard varies by strata) with stratified log-rank test
- Stratification: Time to progression after penultimate platinum (6-<12 vs >=12 months), bevacizumab with penultimate/last platinum (yes/no), best response to last platinum (CR vs PR); IVRS-recorded; separate randomization per cohort
- Covariates: Treatment group as the only covariate
- Ties: Exact (PROC PHREG ties=EXACT)
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% CI from stratified Cox; stratified log-rank (PROC LIFETEST), one-sided 0.025 per cohort; hierarchical HRD+ then overall non-gBRCAmut
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: No adequate post-baseline scan: censored at randomization unless death within 17 weeks; new anticancer therapy, events after >17-week gap, or IRC-overturned PD: censored at last adequate assessment
- Interim/sample size: gBRCAmut originally 140 events (>95% power, HR 0.50), reduced to ~100 events (90%) after FDA Type C comment; HRD+ 98 events (90%); overall non-gBRCAmut 140 events (>95%); planned interim at 85 events not conducted per FDA advice
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG / PROC LIFETEST
- Result: gBRCAmut HR 0.26 (0.17, 0.41), events 58/138 vs 44/65; HRD+ HR 0.37 (0.24, 0.58), 56/106 vs 45/56; non-gBRCAmut HR 0.45 (0.34, 0.61), 125/234 vs 88/116; all p<0.0001 (label: 0.27/0.38/0.45). Sensitivity S2 unstratified 0.30/0.37/0.50; S5 limited censoring 0.35/0.42/0.66
- FDA comments: FDA considered gBRCAmut cohort overpowered; ~12% censored for investigator PD not confirmed by IRC (possible informative censoring) addressed in FDA SA2; FDA sensitivity HRs consistent; median in gBRCAmut niraparib arm not robust
- Spec source: NOVA SAP v3.0 §6.6.1; FDA Multi-Discipline Review

### Midostaurin (Rydapt) — NDA 207997

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation. Approval year: 2017. Phase-3 trial(s): RATIFY (A2301), NCT00651261, Phase III

#### Model 1: RATIFY (CALGB 10603 / A2301, NCT00651261) — Overall survival (OS) (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox PH model with stratified log-rank test
- Stratification: FLT3 mutation status at randomization (ITD allelic ratio <0.7, ITD >=0.7, TKD)
- Covariates: Treatment only (implied)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; stratified log-rank (FDA: 2-sided p; NEJM: one-sided P by stratified log-rank and stratified score test for HR)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: No formal test reported; FDA noted the median difference (74.4 vs 25.6 months) is inconsistent with a PH model (HR 0.77 implies ~7.6-month median difference) / FDA reviewer: survival percentiles and restricted mean survival time (ratio ~0.90 at 3-6 years) as alternatives to medians
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not censored at SCT; censored at last contact; missing last-contact dates imputed as end of reporting period (FDA clinical reviewer concern)
- Interim/sample size: 509 deaths, 714 patients, ~85% power for HR 0.78, 2-sided 0.05; interim at 50% events; final moved to fixed date (Apr 1, 2015) with 357 deaths, critical 2-sided p 0.047
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.63, 0.95); 2-sided p=0.016; deaths 171/360 vs 186/357 (NEJM: HR 0.78, 0.63-0.96, one-sided P=0.009). Interim at 255 events not significant (p=0.0252)
- FDA comments: Medians unreliable (plateau); RMST did not support a significant benefit; gender interaction concern
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review; FDA Clinical Review; NEJM 2017

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary comparison between treatment arms in OS was based on log-rank test and Cox regression model stratified for FLT3 mutation status used in the randomization. OS was not censored at the time of SCT in the primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (NDA 207997, Ref ID 4049883), PDF p. 27 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/207997Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

> "A hazard ratio of 0.77 with an estimated median OS of 25.6 months in the control arm and a proportional hazards assumption would correspond to a 7.6 months (7.6= (25.6/0.77 – 25.6)) difference in median OS."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (NDA 207997, Ref ID 4049883), PDF p. 30 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/207997Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

> "With the ratio of restricted means between treatment arms to be about 0.90 regardless of duration of follow-up, a significant benefit of midostaurin was not supported by the results of restricted means."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (NDA 207997, Ref ID 4049883), PDF p. 36 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/207997Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

> "Stratified Cox regression models were used to provide estimates of the hazard ratios and associated 95% confidence intervals."
>
> — FDA Clinical Review (NDA 207997, Ref ID 4051527), PDF p. 133 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/207997Orig1Orig2s000MedR.pdf)

> "the corresponding hazard ratio for death of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.63 to 0.96; one-sided P = 0.009 by stratified score test) more accurately reflects the magnitude of benefit"
>
> — Stone et al., N Engl J Med 2017 (PMC full text), HTML full text (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5754190/)

### Neratinib (Nerlynx) — NDA 208051

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Puma Biotechnology, Inc.. Approval year: 2017. Phase-3 trial(s): ExteNET (Study 3004), NCT00878709, Phase 3

CNS recurrence was analyzed with stratified cumulative incidence and Gray's test (no Fine-Gray model); not counted as a Cox model.

#### Model 1: ExteNET (Study 3004, NCT00878709) — Invasive disease-free survival (iDFS), 2-year (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox PH model with stratified log-rank test
- Stratification: ER/PgR (positive vs negative), nodal status (negative, 1-3, >=4 positive nodes), trastuzumab sequential vs concurrent with chemotherapy
- Covariates: Treatment only (implied)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; stratified log-rank, one-sided 0.025
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Events up to 2 years + 28 days; no event: censored at last physical exam within 2 years, 4 months, 28 days; event after >=2 missed exams: censored at last exam before event
- Interim/sample size: Time-driven after Amendment 9 (interim analyses removed); Amendment 13 expected 241 events, ~88% power for HR 0.667 one-sided 0.025
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Stratified HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.49, 0.90); unstratified 0.67 (0.49, 0.90); stratified log-rank 2-sided p=0.008; events 67/1420 vs 106/1420
- FDA comments: Post-database-lock SAP changes to censoring rules (per FDA request); differential early dropout
- Spec source: FDA Multi-Discipline Review (SAP April 6, 2016 not public)

### Inotuzumab ozogamicin (Besponsa) — BLA 761040

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Pfizer Inc. (Wyeth Pharmaceuticals). Approval year: 2017. Phase-3 trial(s): INO-VATE ALL (Study B1931022), NCT01564784, Phase 3

#### Model 1: INO-VATE ALL (Study B1931022), NCT01564784, Phase 3 — Overall survival (ITT, N=326) (co-primary)

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Randomization stratification factors: duration of first remission (<12 vs >=12 months), salvage treatment line (1 vs 2), age (<55 vs >=55 years); IxRS vs CRF source Not stated
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 2-sided 97.5% CI; inference by stratified log-rank test at 1-sided alpha 0.0125 (final boundary 1-sided p=0.0104)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA reviewer: KM curves crossed at ~13 months; Schoenfeld residual plot showed non-zero slope (PH violated) / None pre-specified; publication reports an exploratory post hoc RMST analysis (truncation 37.7 months)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Patients without death censored at date last known alive; FDA noted unexplained imbalance in censoring distributions between arms
- Interim/sample size: 248 OS events / 325 patients for 80% power to detect HR 0.67 (median 4.30 to 6.45 months) at 1-sided alpha 0.0125; group-sequential with 2 interim analyses
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Stratified HR 0.77 (97.5% CI 0.58-1.03), 1-sided p=0.0203 (stratified log-rank), not significant vs boundary 0.0104; deaths 122/164 vs 130/162; unstratified HR 0.75 (97.5% CI 0.56-0.99), 1-sided p=0.01
- FDA comments: OS co-primary missed; non-proportional hazards make log-rank/median-based summaries hard to interpret; OS confounded by post-study HSCT (43% vs 11%) and by imbalanced subsequent therapy
- Spec source: FDA Multi-Discipline Review (SAP summary, §Statistical Analysis Plan); publication

### Abemaciclib (Verzenio) — NDA 208716

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Eli Lilly and Company. Approval year: 2017. Phase-3 trial(s): MONARCH 2 (I3Y-MC-JPBL), NCT02107703, Phase 3 (MONARCH 1 single-arm Phase 2 not in scope)

#### Model 1: MONARCH 2 (I3Y-MC-JPBL), NCT02107703, Phase 3 — Investigator-assessed PFS (EP population N=669) (primary)

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Nature of disease (visceral vs bone-only vs other) and sensitivity to endocrine therapy (primary vs secondary resistance), per IWRS
- Covariates: Treatment (as factor)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Wald CI and Wald p-value for HR; hypothesis test = 1-sided stratified log-rank (cumulative alpha 0.025)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Pre-specified restricted mean difference in PFS (Irwin/Karrison; restriction time where SE of S(t) <= 0.075) as supportive time-scale summary
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Standard PFS table; events after >=2 consecutive missed assessments censored at last adequate assessment
- Interim/sample size: 378 events for ~90% power at HR 0.703 (1-sided 0.025); interim at 265 events with nominal alpha 0.00001 (Slud-Wei)
- Software: Not stated for Cox (ADDPLAN 6.0 or SAS 9.2 for boundaries; SAS PROC LIFETEST for RMST)
- Result: HR 0.553 (95% CI 0.449-0.681), p<0.0001; events 222/446 vs 157/223; median 16.4 vs 9.3 months. BICR: HR 0.460 (0.36-0.58), events 164 vs 124
- FDA comments: 36.9% of patients had 'incorrect stratification factors for IWRS'; marked IWRS-vs-CRF discrepancy for endocrine sensitivity led FDA to an unstratified sensitivity analysis (HR 0.577, 95% CI 0.45-0.68); censoring at new therapy HR 0.53 (0.42-0.65); excluding 200 mg starting dose HR 0.598 (0.480-0.75)
- Spec source: SAP v4 §6.7.2.2-6.7.2.3; FDA Multi-Discipline Review

### Encorafenib (Braftovi) — NDA 210496

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Array BioPharma Inc.. Approval year: 2018. Phase-3 trial(s): COLUMBUS (CMEK162B2301), NCT01909453, Phase 3

#### Model 1: COLUMBUS (CMEK162B2301), NCT01909453, Phase 3 — PFS per BIRC, Combo 450 vs vemurafenib (Test 1) (primary)

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: AJCC cancer stage (IIIB+IIIC+IVM1a+IVM1b vs IVM1c) and ECOG PS (0 vs 1); prior first-line immunotherapy stratum (randomization factor from protocol v2) combined/dropped for analysis per protocol v3
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI; test = 2-sided stratified log-rank, fixed-sequence Tests 1-4 at 0.05
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last adequate assessment; events after >=2 missed assessments censored (backdating sensitivity pre-specified)
- Interim/sample size: Part 1 N=577 (1:1:1): 90% power for HR 0.58 (Combo 450 vs vemurafenib), 2-sided 0.05; no PFS interim
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Stratified HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71), p<0.0001; events 98/192 vs 106/191; median 14.9 vs 7.3 months
- FDA comments: At EOP2 FDA recommended an unstratified primary analysis given the proposal to ignore/group strata; executed SAP remained stratified (stage, ECOG) — review does not reconcile
- Spec source: FDA Multi-Discipline Review §8.1.1 (SAP v4 summary), Table 35

### Mogamulizumab-kpkc (Poteligeo) — BLA 761051

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Kyowa Kirin, Inc.. Approval year: 2018. Phase-3 trial(s): MAVORIC (Study 0761-010), NCT01728805, Phase 3

#### Model 1: MAVORIC (Study 0761-010), NCT01728805, Phase 3 — PFS by investigator (PFS-INV), ITT (primary)

- Model type: standard Cox (covariate-adjusted; log-rank test stratified)
- Stratification: None in Cox model (log-rank test stratified by disease type, stage, region)
- Covariates: Treatment, disease type (MF vs SS), disease stage (IB/II vs III/IV), region (US, Japan, rest of world) — entered as covariates, not strata
- Ties: Efron (SAS ties=efron)
- CI/test: Wald (PROC PHREG risklimits) 95% CI; test = stratified log-rank, 1-sided 2.5%
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at new anti-lymphoma therapy incl. crossover absent PD; clinical progression not meeting formal PD censored
- Interim/sample size: 255 PFS events for 90% power (median 169 to 254 days), 1-sided 0.025; no interim; early cutoff 31 Dec 2016 at 241 events (>85% power)
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG
- Result: HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.41-0.69), 2-sided p<0.0001; events 110/186 vs 131/186; median 7.6 vs 3.1 months (FDA, 30.4375 days/month)
- FDA comments: 41% of mogamulizumab patients censored (47% of those before 6 months) — imbalanced/possibly informative censoring; FDA ran 6 additional sensitivity analyses (HR range 0.53-0.74). README describes the Cox model as 'stratified'; the SAP specifies a covariate-adjusted (unstratified) Cox model
- Spec source: SAP §6.11.2.1 and §8.2.5 (SAS code); FDA Multi-Discipline Review Table 9

### Duvelisib (Copiktra) — NDA 211155

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Verastem, Inc.. Approval year: 2018. Phase-3 trial(s): DUO (Study IPI-145-07), NCT02004522, Phase 3 (DYNAMO single-arm Phase 2 not in scope)

#### Model 1: DUO (Study IPI-145-07), NCT02004522, Phase 3 — PFS per IRC (ITT) (primary)

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: IRT randomization strata: del(17p), refractory/early relapse to purine analog, Grade 4 cytopenias — with pre-specified algorithmic pooling of sparse strata (<6 subjects or no events)
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 2-sided 95% CI for HR; test = 1-sided stratified log-rank (overall 0.025)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA: KM separation pattern and non-zero Schoenfeld residual slope indicate potential PH violation / FDA computed RMST (max difference 2.3 months at 29 months); interval-censored sensitivity (stratified generalized log-rank, HR 0.49) requested by FDA
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Right-censoring at last adequate disease assessment
- Interim/sample size: 185 events: ~93% power for HR 0.6, 1-sided 2.5%; interim at 93 events; Lan-DeMets OBF alpha spending, HSD gamma(-4) non-binding futility; boundaries 0.0015/0.0245
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.39-0.69), 1-sided p<0.0001; events 93/160 vs 110/159; median 13.3 vs 9.9 months
- FDA comments: Death before progression 12% vs 6%; HR 'may not be a clear comparison' given non-PH; imbalanced/early censoring may cause non-PH
- Spec source: SAP v4.0 §7.2, §7.2.1.1; FDA Multi-Discipline Review Table 28

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Pfizer Inc.. Approval year: 2018. Phase-3 trial(s): ARCHER 1050 (A7471050), NCT01774721, Phase 3; supportive ARCHER 1009 (NCT01360554, Phase 3) and Study A7471011 (NCT01000025, Phase 3 per ClinicalTrials.gov)

### gilteritinib (Xospata) — NDA 211349

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Astellas Pharma US, Inc. Approval year: 2018. Phase-3 trial(s): ADMIRAL (2215-CL-0301), NCT02421939, Phase 3

#### Model 1: ADMIRAL (2215-CL-0301), NCT02421939 — Overall survival (co-primary (HR estimation; Cox also a sensitivity test of H01))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Response to first-line AML therapy and preselected salvage chemotherapy (intensity), per IRT; SAP §7.11.4 pre-specifies stepwise pooling of strata if a stratum has all events in one arm or the Cox model fails to converge
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank test is the primary (one-sided) test; HR and 95% CI from stratified Cox (PROC PHREG option RL, i.e., Wald CI); Wald p-value reported in tables; one-sided alpha 0.0245 for OS
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not pre-specified in SAP. FDA reviewer (S-001): KM curves crossed after 25 months, 'indicating a violation of the assumption of proportional hazard' / Pre-specified RMST sensitivity analysis (Uno et al. 2015, 18-month cutoff); FDA used RMST as 'assumption free' support (RMST 10 vs 7.2 months, one-sided p<0.0001)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: OS censored at last contact date (or cutoff); sensitivity analyses censor at HSCT and at first new anti-leukemia therapy
- Interim/sample size: 258 deaths for ~90% power to detect HR 0.65 (median 7.7 vs 5.0 months) at overall one-sided 0.0245; second interim at ~129 deaths and final at 258; OBF-type boundaries via Lan-DeMets
- Software: SAS Version 9.3 or higher (PROC PHREG)
- Result: Final analysis: HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.49-0.83), stratified log-rank one-sided p=0.0004; deaths 171/247 vs 90/124; median OS 9.3 vs 5.6 months. Unstratified HR 0.636 (0.491-0.823). Censored-at-HSCT sensitivity HR 0.575 (0.434-0.762)
- FDA comments: FDA reproduced HR 0.64; noted non-proportional hazards (KM crossing after 25 months) and that log-rank/median 'may not be the optimal statistics'; FDA PPS sensitivity stratified Cox HR 0.84 (0.60-1.18), safety-set HR 0.68 (0.52-0.89); FDA assessed OS by chemotherapy-intensity stratum (HR 0.66 high, 0.56 low)
- Spec source: SAP v4.0 §7.4.1 and §7.11.4; Protocol statistical section; FDA S-001 review

The same stratification factors will be applied to both the stratified log-rank test and the stratified Cox proportional hazard model. The same Cox proportional hazard model will be included as a sensitivity analysis for testing H01."

 RUN;

### alpelisib (Piqray) — NDA 212526

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation. Approval year: 2019. Phase-3 trial(s): SOLAR-1 (CBYL719C2301), NCT02437318, Phase 3

#### Model 1: SOLAR-1 (CBYL719C2301), NCT02437318 — PFS (local assessment), PIK3CA-mutant cohort (primary (HR estimation; test is stratified log-rank))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Presence of lung and/or liver metastases (yes/no) and prior CDK4/6 inhibitor (yes/no), from IRT; CRF-derived strata used in a supportive analysis if IRT/CRF discrepancy >10%
- Covariates: Treatment arm only
- Ties: Exact (PROC PHREG TIES=EXACT)
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% Wald CI; SAP notes score-based CIs would be consistent with the log-rank test but are 'not available in SAS procedure PHREG'; hypothesis test = stratified log-rank, one-sided 2.0%
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated (hypotheses framed 'Assuming proportional hazards model') / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Per SAP event/censoring table; primary ignores new antineoplastic therapy; sensitivity censors at new antineoplastic therapy; actual-event and backdating sensitivity analyses for >=2 missing assessments
- Interim/sample size: 243 PFS events, ~84% power for HR 0.60 (11.7 vs 7.0 months); Haybittle-Peto with futility interim (~97 events) and efficacy interim (~185 events)
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG
- Result: HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.50-0.85); one-sided stratified log-rank p=0.00065 (two-sided 0.0013); events 103/169 vs 129/172; median 11.0 vs 5.7 months
- FDA comments: FDA agreed with the primary result; corrected the applicant's stated range of sensitivity-analysis HRs from 0.64-0.66 to 0.64-0.73 (PPS HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.55-0.96); called the 12-month landmark comparison arbitrary and not pre-specified
- Spec source: SAP Amendment 6 (08-May-2023) §3.8.1.2, §3.8.1.4, §4.4.1, §4.4.4; FDA MDR

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The PFS hazard ratio with two-sided 95% confidence interval will be derived from the stratified Cox proportional hazards model for each cohort. In this analysis the baseline hazard function will be allowed to vary across strata. SAS PHREG procedure with ties=EXACT option will be used to carry out this analysis in which the model statement will include treatment arm variable as the only covariate and the STRATA statement will include the stratum information as obtained via IRT."
>
> — Sponsor SAP Amendment 6 §3.8.1.4, PDF p. 44 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/18/NCT02437318/SAP_003.pdf)

```sas
PROC PHREG data=dataset;
MODEL survtime*censor(1)=trt / TIES=EXACT;
STRATA stratum 1 stratum 2;
RUN;
/* survtime represents variable containing event/censor times;
censor represents censoring variable (1=censored, 0=event);
trt represents treatment arm variable;
stratum 1 and stratum 2 represent IRT stratification variables */
```
— Sponsor SAP Amendment 6 §4.4.4 (General SAS code for the stratified Cox model), PDF p. 89 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/18/NCT02437318/SAP_003.pdf)

> "Hazard ratio with two-sided 95% confidence interval will be based on Wald test. Note: Ideally, the hazard ratio and the confidence interval should be derived by a method consistent with the p-value calculation, i.e. in this case with log-rank test. This requirement would lead to the score test based intervals. However, score test-based confidence intervals are not available in SAS procedure PHREG therefore Wald test based intervals will be used instead."
>
> — Sponsor SAP Amendment 6 §4.4.4, PDF p. 89 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/18/NCT02437318/SAP_003.pdf)

> "a: Both Log-rank test and Cox PH model were stratified by Prior CDK4/6 inhibitor usage and presence of lung/liver metastases."

#### Model 4: SOLAR-1 (CBYL719C2301), NCT02437318 — PFS by BIRC (50% audit sample), PIK3CA-mutant cohort (supportive (BIRC audit; NCI auxiliary-variable method))

- Software: SAS
- Result: BIRC audit HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.32-0.71), n=173; NCI auxiliary estimator 0.57 (95% CI 0.40-0.82), full BIRC review not triggered
- FDA comments: FDA: audit-sample point estimates overestimated the treatment effect; supportive only; audit strategy reasonable
- Spec source: SAP Amendment 6 §3.8.1.6 and §4.8; FDA MDR

- Covariates: Treatment only

- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated

#### Model 6: SOLAR-1 (CBYL719C2301), NCT02437318 — PFS, PIK3CA non-mutant cohort (secondary (Bayesian proof-of-concept gate on the Cox HR))

- Model type: stratified Cox (HR feeds Bayesian decision rule)
- Stratification: Lung and/or liver metastasis and prior CDK4/6 inhibitor
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Exact (general SAP rule)
- CI/test: PoC: estimated HR <= 0.60 and posterior P(HR<1) >= 90% using normal approximation Y~N(theta,4/m) with conjugate normal prior; formal test only if PoC met (stratified log-rank one-sided 0.5%)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: As primary PFS
- Interim/sample size: 102 events derived via Schoenfeld formula for PoC criterion
- Software: SAS
- Result: HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.58-1.25); posterior probability 79.4%; PoC not met, no formal test
- FDA comments: FDA reported PoC criteria not met
- Spec source: SAP Amendment 6 §3.8.2.2, §4.7; FDA MDR

### darolutamide (Nubeqa) — NDA 212099

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc. Approval year: 2019. Phase-3 trial(s): ARAMIS (Study 17712), NCT02200614, Phase 3

#### Model 1: ARAMIS (Study 17712), NCT02200614 — Metastasis-free survival (BICR) (primary (HR estimation; test is stratified log-rank))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: PSA doubling time (<=6 vs >6 months) and use of osteoclast-targeted therapy (yes vs no) at randomization, as recorded in IVRS (CRF values used for sensitivity analysis)
- Covariates: Treatment only (as factor)
- Ties: Not stated (SAS code uses PROC PHREG default)
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% CI (method not stated); test = two-sided stratified log-rank at alpha 0.05
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA reviewer: scaled (Schoenfeld-type) residual test, p=0.178 stratified and p=0.184 unstratified; PH 'appears acceptable' / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Death counted only if within 32(+1) weeks of last evaluable scan; censored at last tumor assessment before prohibited new anticancer treatment; patients with baseline metastasis handled by two primary-analysis variants (non-censored vs censored)
- Interim/sample size: 385 MFS events, ~91% power for HR 0.65 (diluted 0.71), two-sided 0.05; no interim for MFS; targets revised via SPA amendments (572 -> 370 -> 385 events)
- Software: SAS release 9.2 or higher (PROC PHREG)
- Result: Stratified HR 0.413 (95% CI 0.341-0.500), two-sided stratified log-rank p<0.0001; events 221/955 vs 216/554; median 40.4 vs 18.4 months
- FDA comments: PH acceptable by residual test; FDA Bayesian reanalysis of the stratified HR (non-informative prior posterior mean 0.413, HPD 0.344-0.504; sceptical prior 0.510); design flaw in imaging charter produced 89 patients with baseline metastasis, addressed by sensitivity analyses
- Spec source: SAP v4.2 §6.2 (MFS) and §4.1; FDA MDR §8

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "MFS will be compared between the treatment arms using a two-sided stratified log-rank test, stratified by PSADT (≤6 vs. >6 months) and use of osteoclast-targeted therapy (yes vs. no) at randomization. A two-sided overall alpha of 0.05 will be used for the efficacy analysis of MFS. The analysis will be performed according to treatment groups as randomized, with stratification as recorded in the IVRS data."
>
> — Sponsor SAP v4.2 (12-Mar-2021) §6.2.1, PDF p. 38 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/14/NCT02200614/SAP_003.pdf)

> "The hazard ratio as well as its 95% confidence interval (CI) will be presented based on fitting a Cox regression model with treatment as factor and stratified by PSA doubling time (≤6 vs. >6 months) and use of osteoclast-targeted therapy (yes vs. no) at randomization."
>
> — Sponsor SAP v4.2 (12-Mar-2021) §6.2.1, PDF p. 39 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/14/NCT02200614/SAP_003.pdf)

```sas
proc phreg data=data;
         model prog_time *cnsr(1) = trtpn;
         strata psa_double ot_therapy / missing;
         run;
```
— Sponsor SAP v4.2 (12-Mar-2021) §6.2.1 (Sample code to produce hazard ratio), PDF p. 39 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/14/NCT02200614/SAP_003.pdf)

> "The statistical evaluation will be performed by using the software package SAS release 9.2 or higher (SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC, USA)."
>
> — Sponsor SAP v4.2 (12-Mar-2021) §4.1, PDF p. 27 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/14/NCT02200614/SAP_003.pdf)

> "The proportional hazards (PH) assumption used in the MFS analysis appears acceptable. Using a scaled residual test, there was no evidence that the PH assumption did not hold (p-value=0.178 for the stratified Cox PH model and p-value=0.184 for the unstratified Cox PH model)."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review, NDA 212099 (Reference ID 4469844), Reviewer's comments, PDF p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212099Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "With a non-informative prior, the Bayesian posterior mean of the stratified hazard ratio was 0.413 with a 95% highest posterior density (HPD) interval of 0.344 to 0.504. With an informative prior centered around no effect, the Bayesian posterior mean of the stratified hazard ratio was 0.510 (95% HPD interval: 0.431, 0.600)."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review, NDA 212099 (Reference ID 4469844), Reviewer's comments, PDF p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212099Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)
