### Isatuximab-irfc (Sarclisa) — BLA 761113

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Sanofi-Aventis U.S., LLC. Approval year: 2020. Phase-3 trial(s): ICARIA-MM (EFC14335), NCT02990338, Phase 3

#### Model 1: ICARIA-MM (EFC14335), NCT02990338 — PFS (IRC) (primary (HR estimation; test is stratified log-rank))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Age (<75 vs >=75 years) and number of previous lines of therapy (2-3 vs >3) as entered in IRT; eCRF strata in a sensitivity analysis; '>=75 years and >3 lines' stratum collapsed if <20 patients
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; one-sided stratified log-rank test at 0.025; SAP gives the final-analysis critical value 'for the Wald test on PFS hazard ratio' as 0.734
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Graphical log-log plots pre-specified in SAP; results not reported in FDA review / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last valid assessment before further anti-myeloma treatment or cut-off; sensitivity variants ignore further therapy, use investigator assessment (with/without symptomatic deterioration), count further therapy as event, use nominal assessment dates
- Interim/sample size: 162 PFS events, 90% power for HR 0.60 (4.0 vs 6.67 months), one-sided 0.025; no PFS interim
- Software: SAS version 9.4 or higher
- Result: Stratified HR 0.596 (95% CI 0.436-0.814), one-sided stratified log-rank p=0.0010; events 73/154 IPd vs 89/153 Pd; median 11.53 vs 6.47 months
- FDA comments: FDA agrees sensitivity analyses (HR 0.568-0.602) show the primary result is robust; eCRF-strata analysis (HR 0.568) run because of small IRT/eCRF discrepancies in number of prior lines
- Spec source: SAP v3 §2.4.4, §2.4.4.1; Protocol statistical considerations; FDA MDR

### Tucatinib (Tukysa) — NDA 213411

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Seattle Genetics, Inc. Approval year: 2020. Phase-3 trial(s): None (HER2CLIMB is a randomized Phase 2 trial)

#### Excluded

Excluded on phase: HER2CLIMB, the sole pivotal trial, is a randomized double-blind Phase 2 trial (FDA: 'pivotal Phase 2 study'), not Phase 3, Phase 2/3 or Phase 3b. Note for the caller: it nevertheless used stratified Cox models extensively (PFS HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.42-0.71; OS HR 0.66; PFS-BrainMets HR 0.48), stratified by brain metastases, ECOG PS and region (US+Canada pooled), with p-values from a stratified log-rank re-randomization test (Rosenberger and Lachin 2002) because of dynamic hierarchical allocation. Re-include if the census scope is widened to randomized Phase 2 registration trials.

> "The primary evidence of effectiveness comes from the pivotal Phase 2 study"
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213411 (Reference ID 4593552), PDF p. 70 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213411Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The p-value for this test was calculated using a re-randomization procedure to reflect the dynamic hierarchical allocation scheme used in the study randomization. A Cox proportional-hazards model taking into account the stratification factors was used to estimate the treatment arm hazard ratio (HR) and its 95% CI."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 213411, statistical methods, PDF p. 115 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213411Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

### Ripretinib (Qinlock) — NDA 213973

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Deciphera Pharmaceuticals, LLC. Approval year: 2020. Phase-3 trial(s): INVICTUS (DCC-2618-03-001), NCT03353753, Phase 3

#### Model 1: INVICTUS (DCC-2618-03-001), NCT03353753 — PFS (independent radiologic review, double-blind period) (primary (HR estimation; test is stratified log-rank))

- Model type: Cox with stratification factors as covariates (covariate-adjusted, not stratified baseline hazards)
- Stratification: None in the Cox model (log-rank test stratified by prior lines and ECOG)
- Covariates: Treatment plus randomization stratification factors (prior lines 3 vs >=4; ECOG 0 vs 1-2) as fixed covariates — not a STRATA-statement stratified Cox
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% Wald CI; test = two-sided stratified log-rank at 0.05
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last evaluable assessment before >=2 consecutive missed assessments, before other anticancer therapy/surgery; analysis restricted to initially assigned (double-blind) treatment
- Interim/sample size: ~120 patients (2:1), 90 PFS events planned; >90% power for median 4.5 vs 1.0 months; analysis at 88 events, FDA/applicant applied O'Brien-Fleming adjustment to alpha 0.047
- Software: SAS version 9.4 or newer
- Result: HR 0.15 (95% CI 0.09-0.25), two-sided stratified log-rank p<0.0001; events 51/85 vs 37/44; median 6.3 vs 1.0 months
- FDA comments: Agreed with results; protocol amendment 5 switched PFS/OS from unstratified to 'stratified model' per ICH guidance; FDA examined age subgroups because of enrollment imbalance
- Spec source: SAP Final 2.0 §8.1; FDA MDR protocol amendment table and Table footnotes

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Analysis for PFS will be stratified by the randomization stratification factors [prior lines of therapy (3 versus ≥4) and ECOG (0 versus 1 or 2)] . The p-value will be from a 2-sided stratified Log-rank test at 0.05 significant level for evaluation of treatment difference. Point estimate of hazard ratio will be obtained from a Cox regression model with treatment and the randomization stratification factors as fixed factors and it’s 95% CI will be obtained using Wald method."
>
> — Sponsor SAP Final 2.0 (08-Aug-2019) §8.1, PDF p. 20 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/53/NCT03353753/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Statistical analysis will be performed using SAS® (version 9.4 or newer)."

> "[2] Cox regression model includes treatment and randomization stratification factors as fixed factors. [3] 95% CI is based on Wald Method."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review, NDA 213973 (Reference ID 4609309/4609640), footnote to PFS table, PDF p. 117 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213973Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "For the primary endpoint analysis (PFS) and the analysis of overall survival, changed the unstratified model to stratified model with stratification factors to comply to the ICH"

Point estimate of hazard ratio will be obtained from a Cox regression model and its 95% CI will be obtained using Wald method."

> "Since the number of PFS events included in the primary analysis (88 events) was less than the planned 90 events, an O’Brien‐Fleming method was considered to assess the robustness of the result. Using the O’Brien‐Fleming method, the alpha level was adjusted to be 0.047"

### Belantamab mafodotin-blmf (Blenrep) — BLA 761158 (original 2020 accelerated approval, revoked 2023); BLA 761440 (2025 re-approval, new application)

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: GlaxoSmithKline Intellectual Property Development Ltd. England (BLA 761158); GlaxoSmithKline LLC (BLA 761440). Approval year: 2020 (accelerated, revoked 2023); 2025 (re-approval). Phase-3 trial(s): DREAMM-7 (NCT04246047, Phase 3; basis of 2025 approval); DREAMM-3 (NCT04162210, Phase 3 confirmatory, failed); DREAMM-8 (NCT04484623, Phase 3, reviewed but not approved). DREAMM-2 (basis of 2020 approval) is Phase 2 and not included

#### Model 1: DREAMM-7 (207503), NCT04246047 — PFS (IRC) (primary (HR estimation; test is one-sided stratified log-rank))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Number of prior lines (1 vs 2/3 vs >=4), prior bortezomib (yes vs no), R-ISS (I vs II/III), as entered for randomization (IRT); clinical-database strata in a supplementary analysis if mis-stratification
- Covariates: Treatment arm as sole explanatory variable
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: 95% CI (method not stated); test = one-sided stratified log-rank with Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming boundaries
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Pre-specified: KM plot, log(time) vs log(-log(survival)) plot, Schoenfeld residual plot, treatment-by-time interaction in Cox model (violation if p<0.10) / If PH violated, RMST (Uno 2015; t* = smallest of the largest observed times across arms) via PROC LIFETEST RMST and PROC RMSTREG; Cox HR still reported
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Primary estimand with treatment-policy/while-on-treatment intercurrent-event strategies; supplementary estimands S1-S4 with alternative censoring rules
- Interim/sample size: Target PFS events redacted (CCI) in posted SAP; boundaries adjusted to observed events
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG; SAS/STAT 15.1 for RMST
- Result: Label (>=2 prior lines incl. PI and IMiD subgroup, 108 vs 109): HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.21-0.47), events 42 vs 73, stratified Cox. Full ITT per README/NEJM (not fetched): HR 0.41 (0.31-0.53)
- FDA comments: Not available (2025 FDA review not located); label restricts efficacy to >=2 prior lines subgroup
- Spec source: DREAMM-7 SAP §2/§4.2.3/§4.2.4.1; 2025 label §14

> "The stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox proportional hazards models will include the randomization stratification factors as “strata”. Unless otherwise specified, the stratification factors entered for randomization will be used in the primary analysis. If there is any mis-stratification, a supplementary analysis will be performed using the stratification data based on the clinical database."
>
> — DREAMM-7 SAP (dated 17-Nov-2023) §4.1, PDF p. 23 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT04246047/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Hazard ratio (HR) and its corresponding 95% CI will be estimated from Cox proportional hazard model stratified by randomization factors with treatment arm as the sole explanatory variable. The Cox models will be fitted using SAS PROC PHREG with the Efron method to control for ties."

> "The proportional hazards assumption will be assessed using the following methods: o Kaplan-Meier plot by treatment arm o Plot of log(time) against log(-log(survival)) by treatment arm o Plot of Schoenfeld residuals for treatment o Evaluation of time-dependency of treatment effect by adding an interaction term of treatment and time in the Cox model. If the interaction term is significant (p< [0.10]), it is considered that the proportional hazards assumption is violated."
>
> — DREAMM-7 SAP (dated 17-Nov-2023) §4.2.3 Model Checking & Diagnostics, PDF p. 29 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT04246047/SAP_001.pdf)

> — DREAMM-7 SAP (dated 17-Nov-2023) §4.2.4.1, PDF p. 30 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT04246047/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Remove piecewise constant Hazard ratio analysis according to protocol amendment 2. Non-proportional hazards will be handled by Restricted Mean Survival Time (RMST) method; specified analyses based on mITT population."

> "If there is possible non-proportional hazards effect in PFS, the Restricted Mean Survival Time (RMST) method [Uno, 2015] may be conducted as appropriate, while the hazard ratio (HR) and its corresponding 95% CI based on Cox proportional hazard model will still be reported."
>
> — DREAMM-3 SAP (dated 02-Sep-2022) §4.2.4.1, PDF p. 25 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/10/NCT04162210/SAP_001.pdf)

#### Model 5: DREAMM-8 (NCT04484623) — PFS (IRC) (primary (trial reviewed for BLA 761440; BPd indication not approved))

- Model type: stratified Cox (reduced strata) plus covariate-adjusted stratified Cox (supportive)
- Stratification: Only 2 of 4 randomization factors: number of prior lines of therapy and prior bortezomib (randomization used 24 strata across two cohorts); sensitivity analyses with pooled strata using all 4 factors
- Covariates: Primary: treatment only. Supportive: treatment, ISS status and prior anti-CD38 treatment
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: 95% CI; one-sided stratified log-rank
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Pre-specified: KM plot, log(time) vs log(-log(survival)) plot, Schoenfeld residual plot, treatment-by-time interaction in Cox model (violation if p<0.10) / RMST (Uno 2015) if non-PH
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not reviewed in detail
- Interim/sample size: Not stated in reviewed text
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG
- Result: Per README (publication not fetched): HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.37-0.73), p<0.001
- FDA comments: ODAC (July 2025) voted 7-1 unfavorable benefit-risk for BPd (per README)
- Spec source: DREAMM-8 SAP stratification rationale (general considerations), §4.2.3, §4.2.4.1

> "supportive analysis will be performed (HR and corresponding 95% CI will be estimated from Cox proportional hazard model stratified by number prior lines of therapy and prior bortezomib use with treatment, ISS status and prior anti-CD38 treatment as explanatory"
>
> — DREAMM-8 SAP (dated 02-Feb-2024), PDF p. 27 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/23/NCT04484623/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The hazard ratio (HR) and its corresponding 95% CI will be estimated from a Cox proportional hazard model stratified by applicable randomization factors with treatment arm as the sole explanatory variable. Cox models will be fitted using SAS PROC PHREG with the Efron method to control for ties."

### Margetuximab-cmkb (Margenza) — BLA 761150

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: MacroGenics, Inc. Approval year: 2020. Phase-3 trial(s): SOPHIA (CP-MGAH22-04), NCT02492711, Phase 3

#### Model 1: SOPHIA (CP-MGAH22-04), NCT02492711 — PFS (BICR) (sequential primary (HR estimation; test is stratified log-rank))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Backbone chemotherapy, number of metastatic sites (<=2 vs >2), number of prior lines in metastatic setting (<=2 vs >2); factors dropped in order (metastatic sites, prior lines, chemotherapy) if any stratum has <5 events
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Breslow
- CI/test: 95% CI (method not stated); two-sided stratified log-rank at 0.05
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Per SAP Table 1 censoring rules; sensitivity analyses with alternative censoring rules
- Interim/sample size: 257 PFS events, 90% power for HR 0.67 (4 vs 6 months), two-sided 0.05; futility look at ~100 events using conditional power with HR from stratified Cox
- Software: SAS Version 9.3 or higher; ADDPlan v6 for boundaries
- Result: HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.593-0.979), stratified log-rank p=0.0334; events 130/266 vs 135/270; median 5.8 vs 4.9 months. Unstratified HR 0.78 (0.61-0.99)
- FDA comments: Median PFS gain (0.9 months) smaller than 6-week imaging interval; FDA requested post-hoc interval-censored analysis (stratified HR 0.73, 0.57-0.94); accepted as regular approval vs active control
- Spec source: SAP v4.0 §6.3.1.1, §6.3.1.2.1, §6.1.1 (futility); FDA MDR

### melphalan flufenamide (Pepaxto) — NDA 214383

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Oncopeptides AB. Approval year: 2021 (accelerated; withdrawn 2024). Phase-3 trial(s): OCEAN (OP-103), NCT03151811, Phase 3 confirmatory (accelerated approval itself based on single-arm Phase 2 HORIZON, no Cox)

#### Model 1: OCEAN (OP-103), NCT03151811 — PFS (IRC) (primary (HR CI also used for superiority/non-inferiority decision))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Randomization strata from IRT: age (>=75 vs <75), number of prior lines (2 vs 3-4), ISS score (1 vs >=2)
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: 95% CI (method not stated); stratified log-rank test; superiority requires significant log-rank and upper 95% CI of HR < 1.0; non-inferiority margin 1.2 (non-FDA submissions only)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Pre-specified rules censor unconfirmed progression; the applicant's post hoc reassessment instead counted 29 unconfirmed PomDex progressions as events
- Interim/sample size: 339 PFS events, 90% power for HR 0.70, two-sided 0.05 (per README)
- Software: SAS version 9.4 or higher
- Result: Applicant ITT HR 0.817 (95% CI 0.659-1.012), p=0.0644 (not significant); FDA ITT HR 0.833 (0.665-1.044), p=0.1122; post hoc HRs 0.793-0.820
- FDA comments: FDA rejected post hoc reanalysis that departed from SAP censoring rules (FDA re-adjudication with its own censoring rules: HR 0.820, 0.654-1.027, nominal p=0.0837); approval withdrawn Feb 2024
- Spec source: OCEAN SAP §9.5.1, §5, §9.1; FDA Final Decision memo Table 1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The hazard ratio and 95% CI will be determined based on a semi parametric Cox proportional hazards regression model stratified by randomization strata to estimate the magnitude of the effect. Ties will be handled using the Efron methodology."
>
> — OCEAN (OP-103) SAP (dated 25-Oct-2021) §9.5.1, PDF p. 52 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT03151811/SAP_003.pdf)

> "In addition to a significant p-value for the treatment comparison based on the log rank test, the superiority of Melflufen + Dexamethasone versus Pomalidomide + Dexamethasone will be demonstrated if the upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the hazard ratio is < 1.0."
>
> — OCEAN (OP-103) SAP (dated 25-Oct-2021) §9.5.1, PDF p. 53 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT03151811/SAP_003.pdf)

> "Non-inferiority of Melflufen + Dexamethasone versus Pomalidomide + Dexamethasone will be demonstrated if the upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the hazard ratio is < 1.2. This assessment is relevant for non-FDA submissions."
>
> — OCEAN (OP-103) SAP (dated 25-Oct-2021) §9.5.1, PDF p. 53 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT03151811/SAP_003.pdf)

> "All statistical summaries and analyses will be performed in SAS® version 9.4 or higher (SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC, USA)."
>
> — OCEAN (OP-103) SAP (dated 25-Oct-2021) §9.1, PDF p. 45 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT03151811/SAP_003.pdf)

> "they submitted a post-hoc analysis, in which 29 individuals who had unconfirmed progression on the PomDex arm were included as having had their cancer progress while on study, rather than being censored as previously agreed upon in the statistical analysis plan"
>
> — FDA Final Decision on the Proposal to Withdraw Approval of Pepaxto (Feb 23, 2024), PDF p. 10 (https://www.fda.gov/media/176510/download)

> "FDA Re-adjudicated Post hoc Analysis 0.820 (0.654, 1.027) 1.8 0.0837 using FDA’s censoring rules"

### tivozanib (Fotivda) — NDA 212904

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Aveo Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Approval year: 2021. Phase-3 trial(s): TIVO-3 (AV-951-15-303), NCT02627963, Phase 3

#### Model 1: TIVO-3 (AV-951-15-303), NCT02627963 — PFS (BIRC) (primary (HR estimation; test is one-sided stratified log-rank))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: IMDC risk category (favorable/intermediate/poor) and prior therapy (two prior VEGFR TKIs / checkpoint inhibitor + VEGFR TKI / VEGFR TKI + other systemic agent), as collected in IWRS; 'randomized stratum' used if mis-stratified
- Covariates: Treatment only (sorafenib reference)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% CI (method not stated); one-sided stratified log-rank at alpha 0.025
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not pre-specified in SAP. FDA reviewer: Schoenfeld residual test p=0.01, departure from PH; curves separated around second scheduled assessment / FDA added landmark PFS rates at 6 and 12 months (45% vs 37%; 28% vs 11%) as supplementary
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at randomization if no post-baseline assessment; at last adequate assessment otherwise (FDA-described rules)
- Interim/sample size: 255 events, 90% power for median 6 vs 4 months, one-sided 0.025; cut-off fixed at 04-Oct-2018 with target 242 events
- Software: SAS version 9.2 or later
- Result: HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56-0.95), stratified log-rank p=0.016; events 123/175 vs 123/175; median 5.59 vs 3.88 months
- FDA comments: Non-PH flagged (Schoenfeld p=0.01); landmark analyses used as robustness check; PFS analysis plan acceptable
- Spec source: TIVO-3 SAP §4.7.1, §4.7.2; FDA MDR §8

### sotorasib (Lumakras) — NDA 214665

Therapeutic area: Oncology (KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC). Sponsor: Amgen Inc. Approval year: 2021 (accelerated). Phase-3 trial(s): CodeBreaK 200 (Study 20190009, NCT04303780; confirmatory, sotorasib vs docetaxel); also CodeBreaK 300 (mCRC, sotorasib + panitumumab; appears only in the 2025 label). The accelerated-approval basis, CodeBreaK 100 (NCT03600883), was a single-arm Phase 1/2 trial with no Cox model.

#### Model 1: CodeBreaK 200 (NCT04303780, Phase 3) — PFS by BICR (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (HR estimation alongside a stratified log-rank test). Planned extras: unstratified Cox sensitivity analysis, per-protocol and alternative-censoring sensitivity analyses, subgroup HRs with a treatment-by-subgroup interaction test in a stratified Cox model, and an exploratory piecewise Cox model if hazards are non-proportional.
- Stratification: Randomization factors per IXRS/IRT: number of prior lines of therapy for advanced disease (1 vs 2 vs >2), race (Asian vs non-Asian), and history of CNS involvement (present vs absent).
- Covariates: Treatment only (strata handle the stratification factors). SAP §4.1 lists additional covariates that "may be incorporated in selected models", but no covariate-adjusted Cox model is specified.
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: The p-value comes from a stratified log-rank test at one-sided 0.025. The Cox model gives the HR and 95% CI only. The CI method is not stated.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: No formal PH test is specified. "Piecewise Cox models may be explored given evidence of non-proportional hazards", with an overall weighted HR using Lu & Pajak weights.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: Rules are in SAP Appendix D. Sensitivity analyses: (a) new anticancer therapy counted as an event, (b) LTFU/consent withdrawal imputed as an event, (c) scheduled assessment dates used instead of actual dates. Crossover or post-progression treatment is not used after first progression.
- Interim/sample size: 230 PFS events give ~90% power for HR 0.65 at one-sided 2.5%. The IA was at ~160 events (70%), with an O'Brien-Fleming-type spending function and one-sided alpha 0.007 at the IA.
- Software: SAS version 9.4 or later (general SAP statement).
- Result: HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.51-0.86), p=0.0017 (README and ODAC briefing). Median PFS was 5.6 vs 4.5 months. 345 patients were randomized (171 sotorasib, 174 docetaxel). Events per arm: Not stated in the sources reviewed (the ODAC tables are images).
- FDA comments: The 2023 ODAC briefing (S-005) accepted that "the estimated HR is generally consistent" but argued that significance may not hold under informative censoring. Its points: (1) an FDA interval-censored analysis gave HR 0.71 (0.54-0.95) but only a ~5-day difference in medians; (2) multiple-imputation and tipping-point analyses for 20 docetaxel patients censored on day 1, and for 19 early crossovers, gave CIs that include 1; (3) the median PFS gain (~5 weeks) was shorter than the 6-week scan interval. FDA said the HR alone is insufficient and that medians, event rates and KM shape must be weighed. ODAC voted 10-2 that PFS per BICR could not be reliably interpreted.
- Spec source: SAP Amendment 3 (v5.0) §§3.2, 9.1, 9.5, 9.5.1; Protocol §9; FDA ODAC Briefing Document; ODAC minutes.

#### Model 2: CodeBreaK 200 (NCT04303780, Phase 3) — OS (key secondary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (same as PFS). Planned extras: unstratified Cox sensitivity analysis; crossover-adjusted analyses (RPSFT, an IPCW-weighted Cox model, and the two-stage method); a piecewise PH model if hazards are non-proportional.
- Stratification: Same randomization factors as PFS (prior lines, race, CNS involvement).
- Covariates: Treatment only. The IPCW weights come from logistic models with baseline and time-dependent covariates.
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: The p-value comes from a stratified log-rank test (one-sided). HR and 95% CI come from the stratified Cox model. Maurer-Bretz graphical multiplicity across PFS, ORR, OS and PROs. O'Brien-Fleming-type spending over an OS IA (≥175 events) and a primary analysis (≥198 events).
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Piecewise PH model "may be explored".
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated (no robust variance is specified for the IPCW-weighted Cox model).
- Censoring: Patients alive are censored at the date last known alive (capped at the data cutoff).
- Interim/sample size: OS IA at ≥175 events (~53% maturity), OS primary analysis at ≥198 events (~60% maturity, assumed HR 0.75). Nominal alpha 0.01% for the administrative OS summary at the PFS IA.
- Software: SAS 9.4 or later.
- Result: HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.77-1.33) at the primary analysis; HR 0.96 (0.74-1.24) at the 90-day safety update (ODAC briefing). 46 patients (26%) crossed over.
- FDA comments: FDA ran RPSFTM, IPCW and two-stage analyses, which were "generally consistent with the primary analysis". Tipping-point analyses suggested the HR "could be greater than 1" if docetaxel patients who were never treated had moderately longer survival.
- Spec source: SAP §§3.2, 9.5 table, 9.5.2.1; FDA ODAC briefing §§3.3.4, 4.5.

### mobocertinib (Exkivity) — NDA 215310

Therapeutic area: Oncology (EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC). Sponsor: Takeda. Approval year: 2021 (accelerated; withdrawn 2023). Phase-3 trial(s): EXCLAIM-2 (TAK-788-3001, NCT04129502; first-line mobocertinib vs platinum-pemetrexed). The accelerated-approval basis (Study 101, Phase 1/2, single-arm) had no Cox model. ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted protocol or SAP for NCT04129502, and the 2021 FDA review discusses EXCLAIM-2 only in its regulatory history, with no Cox specification. All specification text comes from the JCO 2025 publication.

#### Model 1: EXCLAIM-2 (NCT04129502, Phase 3) — PFS by BICR (primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (HR estimation alongside a stratified log-rank test).
- Stratification: Baseline intracranial CNS metastases (yes vs no) and race (Asian vs non-Asian). Randomization used block-stratified IRS. The publication does not say whether the analysis strata came from IRS or CRF.
- Covariates: Not stated (treatment only implied).
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: Two-sided stratified log-rank test; HR from the stratified Cox model; 95% CI method not stated. Overall two-sided alpha 0.05.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: Not stated (README notes PFS/DoR censoring in Study 101 followed FDA's 2015 NSCLC endpoints guidance; nothing specific for EXCLAIM-2).
- Interim/sample size: ~318 patients and 227 PFS events for 90% power at HR 0.65 (medians 6.5 vs 10 months). One IA at ~70% of events (159/227), O'Brien-Fleming Lan-DeMets spending, futility stop if the observed HR was >1. The paper also mentions an adaptive event-size reassessment.
- Software: SAS version 9.4 or higher.
- Result: At the IA (cutoff April 4, 2023; 354 randomized, 179 vs 175), median PFS was 9.6 vs 9.6 months, HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.77-1.39), p=0.803. The trial crossed the futility boundary and was discontinued. Events per arm: Not stated in the text extracted. In a related time-to-deterioration analysis, the lung-symptom HR was 0.68 (0.50-0.93); its model is not stated.
- FDA comments: None located for EXCLAIM-2. The 2021 review notes only that FDA "strongly recommended that an early futility analysis be implemented in Study TAK-788-3001".
- Spec source: Jänne et al., J Clin Oncol 2025;43:1553 (PMC12054980), Methods/Statistical analysis.

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Primary analysis of the primary end point was performed using a two-sided stratified log-rank test stratified by the presence of intracranial CNS metastases at baseline (yes v no) and race (Asian v non-Asian). The HR was estimated using a stratified Cox regression model."
>
> — Jänne et al., J Clin Oncol 2025 (EXCLAIM-2), PMC full text (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12054980/)

> "Per the statistical analysis plan, approximately 318 patients were to be enrolled to provide a 90% power to detect a 3.5-month improvement in median PFS (hazard ratio [HR] for disease progression or death, 0.65), after approximately 227 PFS events (PD or death) had occurred, assuming a median PFS of 6.5 months for platinum-doublet chemotherapy and 10 months for mobocertinib in treatment-naïve patients in the target population."
>

### tebentafusp-tebn (Kimmtrak) — BLA 761228

Therapeutic area: Oncology (HLA-A*02:01+ metastatic uveal melanoma). Sponsor: Immunocore Ltd. Approval year: 2022. Phase-3 trial(s): IMCgp100-202 (Study 202, NCT03070392). Phase note: the SAP title page says "A Phase II Randomized…", and ClinicalTrials.gov lists PHASE2. The README also calls it Phase 2. However, the FDA Multi-Discipline Review's Table 13 lists "IMCgp100‐202 Phase 3", and the review repeatedly calls it "the pivotal, Phase 3 Study 202" (and once "pivotal Phase 2"). It is included here as a pivotal randomized trial that FDA describes as Phase 3; the phase label is flagged as inconsistent across sources.

#### Model 1: IMCgp100-202 (NCT03070392, Phase 3 per FDA / Phase 2 per SAP and CT.gov) — OS (primary; ITT and RAS)

- Model type: Stratified Cox.
- Stratification: Baseline LDH (≤ULN vs >ULN, ULN=250 U/L; centrally measured). The analysis uses the IRT-recorded strata "even if it is subsequently discovered that these values were incorrect". A sensitivity analysis re-stratifying by central-lab LDH was triggered only if discrepancies exceeded 10%. It was not run because fewer than 10% of patients were discordant.
- Covariates: Treatment only.
- Ties: Efron.
- CI/test: Two-sided stratified log-rank test for the p-value; HR with profile-likelihood 95% CI. Supportive unstratified log-rank test. Alpha split: ITT 0.045, RAS (rash analysis set) 0.005, with Maurer-Bretz recycling.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: The SAP's subgroup section states that proportionality is assessed with the PROC PHREG ASSESS statement (Lin-Wei-Ying cumulative martingale residuals). No non-PH alternative is specified.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: Patients alive are censored at last known alive, or at the data cutoff if the death date falls after it. For the RAS, an immortal-time sensitivity analysis measures OS from Study Day 8 and excludes patients who died or were censored before Day 8.
- Interim/sample size: 250 deaths give 89% power for HR 0.645 at two-sided α=0.045 (369 patients, 2:1). RAS: 164 deaths for HR 0.531 at α=0.005. Two IAs at 150 (60%) and 200 (80%) events with O'Brien-Fleming boundaries via Lan-DeMets.
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG (named in the SAP for the ASSESS statement); version not stated.
- Result: At the first IA (150 deaths; 87/252 vs 63/126), ITT HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.37-0.71), p<0.0001. The stopping boundary was 0.006.
- FDA comments: FDA agreed with the SAP and the primary results. It noted the stopping boundary of 0.006 at 150 events, treated landmark OS rates as supportive only, and confirmed that the LDH re-stratification sensitivity analysis was not triggered.
- Spec source: SAP v3.0 §§1.2.3, 4.2.1, 4.2.3 (OCR); FDA MDR §8 (statistical assessment).

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary analysis of OS in all randomized patients will be analyzed using a 2-sided log rank test stratified by LDH status for generation of the p-value. The hazard ratio (HR) will be estimated using a Cox-proportional hazards model stratified by LDH using the Efron approach for handling ties (Efron 1977), together with the associated profile likelihood 95% confidence intervals for the HR."
>
> — IMCgp100-202 SAP v3.0 (28 Oct 2020) [OCR, tesseract; original text layer garbled], PDF p. 23 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/92/NCT03070392/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The LDH status in the statistical modelling will be based on the values entered into IRT at randomization, even if it is subsequently discovered that these values were incorrect."
>
> — IMCgp100-202 SAP v3.0 (28 Oct 2020) [OCR, tesseract; original text layer garbled], PDF p. 23 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/92/NCT03070392/SAP_001.pdf)

> "OS will also be analysed based on an unstratified log rank test as a supportive analysis. An additional sensitivity analysis will evaluate OS in the Safety Population. For the RAS OS analysis, in order to adjust for the potential immortal-time bias during the first week of treatment that determines eligibility into the RAS for tebentafusp patients, a sensitivity analysis will measure OS starting from Study Day 8 (7 days after the start of infusion) for all patients in the analysis set. Patients in the analysis set who die or who would otherwise be censored prior to Study Day 8 will be excluded from the analysis."
>
> — IMCgp100-202 SAP v3.0 (28 Oct 2020) [OCR, tesseract; original text layer garbled], PDF p. 24 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/92/NCT03070392/SAP_001.pdf)

> "reflect the central LDH value, then a sensitivity analysis will be done for OS if there are >10% discrepancies. For this sensitivity analysis patients will be stratified based on the strata determined by the central LDH results, not the strata recorded in IRT-."
>
> — IMCgp100-202 SAP v3.0 (28 Oct 2020) [OCR, tesseract; original text layer garbled], PDF p. 29 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/92/NCT03070392/SAP_001.pdf)

> "OS 1s the primary endpoint for this study. Assuming a 2:1 randomization ratio of tebentafusp vs. Investigator Choice, 250 events (deaths) are needed in the randomized trial to provide 89% power to detect a difference of survival distribution that can be characterized by a 0.645 hazard ratio (HR) for OS with a 2-sided significance level of 0.045. Assuming OS is exponentially distributed, this may translate to a median OS of 18.6 months in the tebentafusp treated arm and 12 months in the Investigator Choice arm. The smallest treatment effect that would be statistically significant is an OS HR of 0.75 (e.g. 16 vs 12mo)."
>
> — IMCgp100-202 SAP v3.0 (28 Oct 2020) [OCR, tesseract; original text layer garbled], PDF p. 12 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/92/NCT03070392/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The difference in OS between the treatment arms was tested using a 2‐sided log‐rank test stratified by LDH status (LDH > ULN versus LDH ≤ ULN; measured centrally). >
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, BLA 761228, PDF p. 90 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761228Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "FDA notes that with 150 OS events observed at this interim analysis (60% of the total 250 events required for final OS analysis), the corresponding stopping boundary was 0.006."
>

>

#### Model 2: IMCgp100-202 — PFS by investigator (key secondary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (same as OS).
- Stratification: Baseline LDH (IRT).
- Covariates: Treatment only.
- Ties: Efron (inherits the OS method: "The analysis method for PFS was the same as that of OS").
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank p-value; profile-likelihood CI (inherited from OS). Fixed-sequence testing OS → PFS → BOR. PFS was not tested at interim looks.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: As for OS (the ASSESS statement is described in the subgroup section).
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: Censored at the last evaluable tumor assessment. Events after two or more missed or NE assessments (>26 weeks) are censored at the last evaluable assessment. Sensitivity analyses: evaluation-time bias (midpoint imputation) and attrition bias (actual event times; censoring at subsequent therapy).
- Interim/sample size: Tested at the overall alpha (0.045, or 0.05 if the RAS alpha was recycled) only after OS was significant.
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG; version not stated.
- Result: Events 198/252 vs 97/126; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.58-0.94), p=0.0139.
- FDA comments: Results were consistent across the prespecified evaluation-time-bias and attrition-bias sensitivity analyses (Applicant statement, not disputed).
- Spec source: SAP §§4.2.2.1, 4.2.3 (OCR); FDA MDR.

#### Model 3: IMCgp100-202 — OS and PFS subgroup HRs (exploratory subgroup model)

- Model type: Standard Cox with treatment, factor and treatment-by-factor interaction. Subgroup-level HRs are derived from linear combinations of coefficients in a single model.
- Stratification: None stated for the subgroup model.
- Covariates: Treatment, the subgroup factor, and the treatment×factor interaction. Factors: ethnicity, gender, age (<65 vs ≥65), ECOG, alkaline phosphatase, LDH, prior adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy, size of largest metastatic lesion, region, and pre-selected investigator's-choice therapy.
- Ties: Efron.
- CI/test: Interaction tested at two-sided 10%; no multiplicity adjustment.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: PROC PHREG ASSESS statement (Lin, Wei and Ying 1993).
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: As for OS and PFS.
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable.
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG.
- Result: Forest plot (MDR Figure 39); values not extracted.
- FDA comments: FDA considered all subgroup analyses exploratory. In adequately sized subgroups, results were consistent with the overall OS result.
- Spec source: SAP §2.4 (OCR).

### nivolumab and relatlimab-rmbw (Opdualag) — BLA 761234

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Bristol-Myers Squibb Company. Approval year: 2022. Phase-3 trial(s): RELATIVITY-047 (CA224-047), NCT03470922, randomized double-blind Phase 2/3 (seamless Phase 2-to-3).

#### Model 1: RELATIVITY-047 (CA224-047), NCT03470922 — PFS per BICR (RECIST 1.1) (primary (HR estimation accompanying stratified log-rank test))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Planned: PD-L1 (>=1% vs <1%), LAG-3 (>=1% vs <1%), BRAF (mutant vs wild-type), AJCC v8 M stage (M0/M1any[0] vs M1any[1]); LAG-3 and BRAF from IRT, PD-L1 from LabCorp rescore, M stage derived from RAVE eCRF/LDH data. Final analysis: PD-L1 dropped from strata (strata <10 subjects) per pre-specified removal rule (SAP V2.1), so strata = LAG-3, BRAF, AJCC M stage
- Covariates: treatment group as single covariate
- Ties: exact
- CI/test: two-sided 95% CI for HR (method not stated); p-value from two-sided stratified log-rank test; overall two-sided alpha 0.05 (0.049 at PFS FA after 0.001 administrative penalty)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Sensitivity: time-dependent treatment-by-time covariate added to stratified Cox (Wald p<0.1 threshold); p=0.1497 (see Model 3); non-PH handling: Principal sensitivity analysis: stratified Fleming-Harrington G(0,1) weighted log-rank test; piecewise HR before/after 6 months via time-dependent Cox (Model 3)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Primary PFS definition censors at subsequent anticancer therapy; ITT definition (regardless of subsequent therapy) used for sensitivity; COVID-19 death censoring sensitivity if >=10% events COVID-related
- Interim/sample size: Phase 3: >=365 BICR PFS events, ~85% power for HR 0.73 (piecewise-hazard/cure-fraction simulation), two-sided alpha 0.05, ~700 randomized; blinded non-alpha-spending PFS IA (HR <=0.8 go criterion) with 0.001 administrative alpha penalty; Phase 2 alternative: 183 events, 80% power, HR 0.73, one-sided 0.1
- Software: Not stated (East v6 for alpha-spending boundaries)
- Result: HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.62, 0.92), stratified log-rank p=0.0055; events 180/355 (nivo+rela) vs 211/359 (nivo); median PFS 10.12 vs 4.63 mo
- FDA comments: FDA agreed with result; FDA confirmed missing-assessment sensitivity analysis with stratified Cox (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.62, 0.93) and performed its own re-stratified analysis using IRT instead of RAVE-derived AJCC M stage (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62, 0.92). Review documents M-stage stratification errors at sites (LDH not reliably incorporated into AJCC v8 M stage) and PD-L1 rescoring discrepancies
- Spec source: SAP v5.0 §7.5, §7.5.1; FDA Multi-Discipline Review §8.1.2

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The analysis of PFS (as determined by BICR) will be to compare the two treatment groups via a stratified log-rank test among all randomized subjects. The primary definition of PFS adjusting for subsequent anticancer therapy will be used in this analysis. The two-sided log-rank p-value will be reported. The estimate of the PFS hazard ratio between treatment groups will be calculated"
>
> — SAP CA224047 v5.0 (25-Oct-2021), PDF p. 49 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/22/NCT03470922/SAP_001.pdf)

> "using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model. Ties will be handled using the exact method. A two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio will also be presented."

>

#### Model 2: RELATIVITY-047 (CA224-047), NCT03470922 — OS (secondary (hierarchically tested; HR estimation accompanying stratified log-rank test))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Same as PFS (planned PD-L1, LAG-3, BRAF, AJCC M stage; OS IA1 analysis stratified by LAG-3, BRAF, AJCC M stage)
- Covariates: treatment arm as single covariate
- Ties: Not stated (exact method specified only for PFS)

#### Model 3: RELATIVITY-047 (CA224-047), NCT03470922 — PFS per BICR (sensitivity (non-PH; piecewise HR before/after 6 months) and PH check)

- Model type: time-dependent covariate Cox (stratified; treatment, period, period-by-treatment interaction)
- Stratification: Randomization stratification factors (as for primary)
- Covariates: treatment, period (pre vs post 6 months) and period-by-treatment interaction; Applicant PH check used treatment-by-time interaction covariate
- Ties: exact
- CI/test: two-sided 95% CI; Wald chi-square p-value for treatment-by-time interaction (<0.1 flags non-constant effect)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Time-dependent treatment-by-time interaction in stratified Cox; Wald p=0.1497 (no evidence of non-constant hazard); non-PH handling: Stratified FH G(0,1) weighted log-rank test as principal sensitivity analysis (falls back to stratified log-rank if not estimable); piecewise HR pre/post 6 months
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Primary and ITT PFS definitions
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Treatment-by-time interaction p=0.1497; piecewise HRs not reported in review
- FDA comments: FDA considers the Applicant sensitivity analyses exploratory but supportive of robustness
- Spec source: SAP v5.0 §7.5.2(1); FDA Multi-Discipline Review §8.1.2

### lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan (Pluvicto) — NDA 215833

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Advanced Accelerator Applications USA, Inc. (Novartis); trial sponsor Endocyte, Inc.. Approval year: 2022. Phase-3 trial(s): VISION (PSMA-617-01), NCT03511664, randomized open-label Phase 3.

#### Model 1: VISION (PSMA-617-01), NCT03511664 — rPFS per BICR (PFS-FAS, randomized on/after 5-Mar-2019) (alternate primary (supportive HR estimation; test = stratified log-rank))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: LDH (<=260 vs >260 IU/L), presence of liver metastases (yes/no), ECOG (0-1 vs 2), inclusion of NAAD in BSC/BSoC at randomization (yes/no); IRT values used for all efficacy analyses
- Covariates: randomized treatment arm (single covariate)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 99.2% CI for HR (alpha 0.004 one-sided for rPFS); one-sided stratified log-rank p-value. SAP v2.0 changed the primary test from the Wald chi-square test of the stratified Cox model to the stratified log-rank test
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Visual checks only: SAS LIFETEST plots (SURVIVAL LOGSURV LOGLOGS); no formal test; non-PH handling: If PH does not hold, additional methods per separate post-hoc analysis plan (not specified)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Events after >=2 missed assessments censored (sensitivity includes them); patients randomized before 5-Mar-2019 excluded from primary rPFS (dropout/withdrawal of consent remediation); supportive FAS analysis treating pre-March-2019 consent withdrawals as censored vs events
- Interim/sample size: 364 rPFS events, 84% power for HR 0.67, one-sided alpha 0.004
- Software: SAS version 9.4 or higher (LIFETEST for PH plots; Cox procedure not named)
- Result: HR 0.40 (99.2% CI 0.29, 0.57); one-sided stratified log-rank p<0.001; events 254/385 vs 93/196; median 8.7 vs 3.4 mo. FDA reports HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.31, 0.52)
- FDA comments: FDA concerned that asymmetric censoring from withdrawal of consent/informative censoring in the BSoC arm affected results; high degree of rPFS censoring limits interpretation of the magnitude of rPFS effect; conservative/worst-case/tipping-point sensitivity analyses supportive
- Spec source: SAP v3.0 §8.2.1; FDA Multi-Discipline Review Table 21 and statistical assessment

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "A supportive analysis will be performed in terms of a stratified Cox regression model with a single covariate for randomized treatment arm, stratifying again for the randomization stratification factors. The hazard ratio for rPFS will be calculated, along with its 99.2% confidence interval, from the stratified Cox model. The HR and CI from this model will be used as an adjunct to the primary stratified log-rank test p-value to provide the quantification of the treatment effect on rPFS."
>
> — SAP PSMA-617-01 v3.0 (18-Jan-2021), PDF p. 35 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/64/NCT03511664/SAP_001.pdf)

> "with a minimum of approximately 6 months follow-up, these patients are expected to yield 364 rPFS events which will be sufficient to provide 84% power to test the hypothesis that the HR of rPFS is 0.67 or better with a 1-sided alpha level of 0.004."
>
> — SAP PSMA-617-01 v3.0 (18-Jan-2021), PDF p. 12 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/64/NCT03511664/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Changed the statistical test to compare the primary endpoints (rPFS and OS) from the Wald chi-square test from the stratified Cox regression model to the stratified log-rank test (strata based on randomization stratification factors)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review NDA 215833, PDF p. 86 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215833Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Both Cox PH model and Log-rank test are stratified for LDH (≤ 260 IU/L vs. > 260 IU/L); presence of liver metastases (yes vs. no); ECOG score (0 or 1 vs. 2); and inclusion of NAAD in BSC/BSoC at time of randomization (yes vs. no). IRT data for stratification are used."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review NDA 215833, PDF p. 108 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215833Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The rPFS HR was 0.40 (95% CI: 0.31, 0.52) based on the PFS-FAS (N=581), which included all patients randomized on or after March 5, 2019."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review NDA 215833, PDF p. 115 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215833Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "FDA was concerned that asymmetric censoring due to withdrawal of consent and potential informative censoring would impact efficacy results. A variety of conservative and worst-case sensitivity analyses for OS and rPFS were performed to evaluate the disproportionate drop out in the BSoC arm compared to the 177Lu-PSMA-617. Interpretation of rPFS results was limited due to the high degree of censoring, which leads to uncertainty in the estimation of the magnitude of the rPFS treatment effect."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review NDA 215833, PDF p. 169 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215833Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 2: VISION (PSMA-617-01), NCT03511664 — OS (FAS, all 831 randomized) (alternate primary (supportive HR estimation; test = stratified log-rank))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: LDH (<=260 vs >260 IU/L), presence of liver metastases (yes/no), ECOG (0-1 vs 2), inclusion of NAAD in BSC/BSoC at randomization (yes/no); IRT values used for all efficacy analyses
- Covariates: randomized treatment arm (single covariate)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 99.8% CI at interim, 95% or 96% CI at final depending on rPFS/interim results; one-sided stratified log-rank p-value
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Visual checks only: SAS LIFETEST plots (SURVIVAL LOGSURV LOGLOGS); no formal test; non-PH handling: Additional methods in separate post-hoc analysis plan if PH violated (not specified)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last known alive; COVID-19 sensitivity censoring COVID-19 deaths at date of death; FDA sensitivity excluding consent withdrawals
- Interim/sample size: 508 deaths, >=90% power for HR 0.7306, one-sided alpha >=0.020 (0.020-0.025 depending on rPFS/interim results); interim OS at rPFS analysis (~341 deaths) at one-sided 0.001
- Software: SAS version 9.4 or higher
- Result: HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.52, 0.74); one-sided stratified log-rank p<0.001; deaths 343/551 vs 187/280; median 15.3 vs 11.3 mo
- FDA comments: FDA reviewer OS sensitivity analysis excluding patients who withdrew consent: HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.52, 0.75); statistical review concluded OS results not compromised by early dropout
- Spec source: SAP v3.0 §3.4, §8.2.1; FDA Multi-Discipline Review Table 22

### tremelimumab (Imjudo) — BLA 761289

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: AstraZeneca. Approval year: 2022. Phase-3 trial(s): HIMALAYA (D419CC00002), NCT03298451, randomized open-label Phase 3.

#### Model 1: HIMALAYA (D419CC00002), NCT03298451 — OS, T300+D (Arm C) vs sorafenib (Arm D) (primary (HR estimation; test = stratified log-rank))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Etiology of liver disease (confirmed HBV vs confirmed HCV vs others), ECOG (0 vs 1), macrovascular invasion (yes vs no); values from IWRS; CRF-based sensitivity if >10% IWRS/CRF discordance
- Covariates: treatment
- Ties: Efron for HR estimation (log-rank test described as equivalent to Cox score test with Breslow ties)
- CI/test: Profile likelihood CI (95%; alpha-adjusted 96.02% CI reported at final analysis); two-sided stratified log-rank p-value; Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming boundaries
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Complementary log-log vs log(time) plots; time-dependent covariate if concerns; Grambsch-Therneau test/Schoenfeld residuals may be used. FDA/Applicant: log(-log) plots showed delayed effect; post-hoc treatment-by-time linear interaction p=0.094 (T300+D vs S); non-PH handling: Piecewise HRs over distinct periods; three-component stratified MaxCombo (FH(0,0), FH(0,1), FH(1,1)) sensitivity; RMST (pseudovalues), Royston-Parmar; landmark OS rates
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last date known alive; COVID-19 sensitivity censors COVID-19 deaths; reverse-KM censoring check
- Interim/sample size: Average HR 0.70 assumed; IA2 at ~404 events (2-sided 0.0222), FA at ~515 events (2-sided 0.0425), >=97% power at FA; overall 2-sided alpha 4.9%
- Software: SAS (PROC PHREG named for subgroup Cox models)
- Result: HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.66, 0.92; 96.02% CI 0.65, 0.93), 2-sided stratified log-rank p=0.0035; deaths 262/393 vs 293/389; median 16.43 vs 13.77 mo
- FDA comments: FDA: delayed curve separation suggests non-proportional hazards, so OS HR should be interpreted as an average over the observed period, with landmark OS rates considered alongside; no major statistical issues; pre-BLA FDA flagged NI test method under PH violation as a review issue
- Spec source: SAP Edition 4.0 §4.2.2.1; FDA Multi-Discipline Review §8.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary OS endpoint will be analysed using a stratified log-rank tests adjusting for etiology of liver disease (confirmed HBV versus confirmed HCV versus others), ECOG (0 versus 1), and macrovascular invasion (yes versus no) for generation of the p-value and using rank tests for association as the testing approach, which corresponds to Cox regression with the Breslow approach for handling ties (Breslow, 1974). The effect of Arm C vs. Arm D treatment will be estimated by the HR from stratified Cox proportional hazards model (with ties=Efron and stratification variables as listed above) together with its corresponding 95% confidence interval (CI) calculated using a profile likelihood approach. The stratification variable will use the values recorded in the randomization system (IWRS). If there is >10% discordance in stratification factors as recorded in IWRS versus the Case Report Form (CRF), then a sensitivity analysis of the primary endpoint OS will be performed using CRF based stratification factors."
>
> — SAP D419CC00002 Edition 4.0 (30-Jul-2021), PDF p. 77 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/51/NCT03298451/SAP_018.pdf)

> "The assumption of proportionality of hazard will be assessed first by examining plots of complementary log-log (event times) versus log (time) and, if these raise concerns, by fitting a time-dependent covariate to assess the extent to which this represents random variation. If a lack of proportionality of hazard is evident, the variation in treatment effect will be described by presenting piecewise HR calculated over distinct time periods."
>
> — SAP D419CC00002 Edition 4.0 (30-Jul-2021), PDF p. 78 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/51/NCT03298451/SAP_018.pdf)

#### Model 2: HIMALAYA (D419CC00002), NCT03298451 — OS, durvalumab (Arm A) vs sorafenib (Arm D) (key secondary (non-inferiority, margin HR 1.08; then superiority))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Etiology of liver disease (confirmed HBV vs confirmed HCV vs others), ECOG (0 vs 1), macrovascular invasion (yes vs no); values from IWRS; CRF-based sensitivity if >10% IWRS/CRF discordance
- Covariates: treatment
- Ties: Efron (same methodology as primary)
- CI/test: Alpha-adjusted two-sided CI for HR compared with NI margin 1.08 (97.52% at interim, 95.82% at final if 453/560 events); profile likelihood
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: As primary; post-hoc treatment-by-time interaction p=0.35; non-PH handling: As primary; post-hoc piecewise HRs
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: As primary
- Interim/sample size: ~560 events at FA, 84% power for NI at margin 1.08 assuming HR 0.84; M1=1.21, M2=1.08 (95-95 fixed margin, 60% retention)
- Software: SAS
- Result: HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.73, 1.02; 95.67% CI 0.73, 1.03): NI met; superiority p=0.0674 (not significant vs 0.049); deaths 280/389
- FDA comments: FDA did not conduct detailed assessment of NI claim appropriateness (no durvalumab monotherapy indication sought); superiority failure supports contribution of both components
- Spec source: SAP Edition 4.0 §1.3/§3.4 sample size, §4.2.2.1; FDA Multi-Discipline Review

### elacestrant (Orserdu) — NDA 217639

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Stemline Therapeutics, Inc. (Menarini); trial sponsor Radius (per SAP). Approval year: 2023. Phase-3 trial(s): EMERALD (RAD1901-308), NCT03778931, Phase 3.

#### Model 1: EMERALD (RAD1901-308), NCT03778931 — PFS by blinded IRC, RECIST 1.1 (co-primary: ESR1-mut subjects and all subjects) (primary)


- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Randomization strata as recorded in eCRF (not IRT). All subjects: ESR1 mutation status (ESR1-mut vs ESR1-mut-nd), prior fulvestrant (yes/no), visceral metastases (yes/no). ESR1-mut subjects: prior fulvestrant, visceral metastases. (Applicant text in the FDA review lists only fulvestrant and visceral metastases for the primary analyses.)
- Covariates: Treatment only, factors used as strata per SAP; MDR Applicant text says "Cox regression model, including treatment and the stratification factors"
- Ties: Efron (SAP spells it "Effron")
- CI/test: Profile likelihood 95% CI for HR; p-value from stratified log-rank test; truncated Hochberg (r1=0.0475, r2=0.025) across the 2 PFS populations, 2-sided FWER 5%
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: KM curves and log(-log S(t)) vs log(time) plots; if concerning, time-dependent covariate (treatment-by-time or treatment-by-ln(time) interaction); non-PH: HR interpreted as average HR unless extensive crossing; RMST (Royston-Parmar) supplemental analysis with stratification factors as covariates
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: New anticancer therapy before PD censored at last adequate assessment before it; event after >=2 missed visits (18 weeks) censored at last adequate assessment; no post-baseline assessment censored at Day 1 unless death within 2 visits
- Interim/sample size: ESR1-mut: ~160 events, 80% power for HR 0.610 at 2-sided alpha 2.5%; all subjects: ~340 events, 92% power for HR 0.667 at 2-sided 2.5%; interim futility analysis only at ~70% enrollment (~119 events)
- Software: SAS 9.4
- Result: All subjects: HR 0.697 (95% CI 0.552-0.880), stratified log-rank p=0.0018, events 144/239 vs 156/239. ESR1-mut: HR 0.546 (0.387-0.768), p=0.0005, events 62/115 vs 78/113 (FDA MDR Table 22)
- FDA comments: FDA flagged non-proportional hazards (KM plots show steep early drop; HR and median hard to interpret) and ran its own RMST analysis (difference 2.3 mo ESR1-mut, 1.0 mo ESR1-mut-nd, 1.9 mo ITT; considered exploratory due to subjective truncation time). FDA concluded ITT benefit was driven by the ESR1-mut subgroup (ESR1-mut-nd HR 0.86, 0.63-1.19) and restricted the indication to ESR1-mut.
- Spec source: SAP v1.1 §4.2.5, §4.7.1.1-4.7.1.4; FDA MDR §8 statistical review

### quizartinib (Vanflyta) — NDA 216993

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Daiichi Sankyo, Inc.. Approval year: 2023. Phase-3 trial(s): QuANTUM-First (AC220-A-U302), NCT02668653, Phase 3 (pivotal); QuANTUM-R (AC220-007), NCT02039726, Phase 3 (supportive, per ClinicalTrials.gov).

#### Model 1: QuANTUM-First (AC220-A-U302), NCT02668653 — Overall survival (primary)


- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Randomization factors per IXRS: region (North America, Europe, Asia/Other), age (<60, >=60), WBC at diagnosis (<40, >=40 x10^9/L); FDA sensitivity re-stratified per eCRF
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 2-sided 95% CI (method not stated); stratified log-rank test as hypothesis test, 2-sided alpha 0.05; serial gatekeeping OS -> EFS -> CR...
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated; non-PH: Design-stage non-PH: sample size simulated under piecewise exponential with HR 0.7 for first 30 months and HR 1 afterwards (RATIFY plateau)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last known alive; sensitivity censoring at start of HSCT conditioning
- Interim/sample size: No efficacy interim; single analysis at 287 deaths and >=24 months after last randomization (max 30 months); ~536 subjects, ~84% power by simulation (EAST 6.3, SAS 9.2)
- Software: SAS PROC LIFETEST and PROC PHREG (protocol misspells "PHREQ")
- Result: HR 0.776 (95% CI 0.615-0.979), stratified log-rank p=0.0324 (2-sided); deaths 133/268 vs 158/271; median 31.9 vs 15.1 months
- FDA comments: FDA reproduced the result; noted plateauing curves make medians exaggerate benefit and an early OS detriment in the first months (more induction deaths on quizartinib). FDA sensitivity: unstratified 0.77 (0.61-0.97); strata per eCRF 0.77 (0.61-0.97), p=0.0265; PPS 0.76 (0.60-0.97); censoring at HSCT conditioning 0.75 (0.56-1.00), p=0.0555. Subgroup forest plot used unstratified Cox.
- Spec source: Protocol v7.0 §11.2, §11.4.1.1, §11.4.1.5, §11.5; FDA MDR §8

#### Model 2: QuANTUM-First (AC220-A-U302), NCT02668653 — Event-free survival (IRC; ITF = no CR within 42 days of last induction cycle start) (key secondary)


- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: Region, age, WBC at diagnosis (randomization factors)
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 2-sided 95% CI; stratified log-rank test (gatekeeping after OS)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated (protocol); FDA noted crossing hazards; non-PH: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Subjects without EFS events censored at last response assessment date; induction treatment failure assigned at Day 1
- Interim/sample size: Tested only after OS significant
- Software: SAS (PROC PHREG per protocol for OS; not stated separately for EFS)
- Result: HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.75-1.11), 2-sided p=0.2371 (FDA, matched Applicant); events 198/268 vs 213/271; not significant. Sensitivity (original 56-day ITF definition) HR 0.729 (0.592-0.897), nominal p=0.0031
- FDA comments: FDA: higher induction treatment failure on quizartinib (51% vs 48%) gives a larger Day-1 drop, so hazards cross
- Spec source: Protocol v7.0 §11.4.1.2; FDA MDR Table 42

### fruquintinib (Fruzaqla) — NDA 217564

Therapeutic area: Oncology Sponsor: Takeda Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc. (trial sponsor Hutchison MediPharma) Approval year: 2023 Phase-3 trial(s): FRESCO-2 (2019-013-GLOB1, NCT04322539, Phase 3, global, 2:1, double-blind, N=691); FRESCO (2013-013-00CH1, China, Phase 3, supportive; FDA MDR: "two randomized Phase 3")

#### Model 1: FRESCO-2 (2019-013-GLOB1, NCT04322539) — Overall survival (OS) (Primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Randomization-schedule (IWRS) stratification factors: prior therapy (TAS-102 vs regorafenib vs both), RAS status (wild type vs mutant), duration of metastatic disease (≤18 vs >18 months); SAS example code uses placeholders STRAT1RN-STRAT3RN
- Covariates: Treatment group only
- Ties: Not stated (example PROC PHREG code has no TIES= option)
- CI/test: Two-sided p-value from stratified log-rank test (SAP; protocol Amendment 4 states 1-sided stratified log-rank at 0.025); HR with 95% Wald CI (example code outputs WaldLower/WaldUpper); fixed-sequence OS then PFS at 2-sided 0.05
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Patients alive censored at date last known alive; no post-randomization data censored at randomization (FDA MDR). Sensitivity: COVID-19 deaths censored at death date-1 (v1.4); first 480 deaths only; censoring at start of subsequent anticancer therapy
- Interim/sample size: 480 OS events; HR 0.73 (median 5 vs 6.8 months), ~90% power, one-sided alpha 0.025, 2:1, ~687 randomized; one non-binding futility-only IA at 160 events (1/3), stop if 1-sided stratified log-rank p >= 0.772 (observed HR >= 1.133), Lan-DeMets; EAST 6.5
- Software: SAS (PROC PHREG / PROC LIFETEST example code); EAST 6.5 for sample size
- Result: Stratified HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.55, 0.80); 2-sided stratified log-rank p<0.001; deaths 317/461 (69%) vs 173/230 (75%); median 7.4 vs 4.8 months
- FDA comments: FDA describes same analysis and reports HR as adjusted for stratification factors; states results consistent in sensitivity analyses; no PH or stratification concerns raised. README discrepancy: README attributes OS HR 0.65 (0.51-0.83) to FRESCO-2, but per FDA MDR that is the FRESCO (China) OS result; FRESCO-2 OS HR is 0.66 (0.55, 0.80)
- Spec source: SAP v1.4 §9.1.1 and Appendix 8; SAP v1.0 §9.1.1 and Appendix 7; Protocol Amendment 4 §9.2.5.1.1; FDA MDR

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The two-sided p-value to test the treatment effect will be calculated using a stratified log-rank test accounting for randomization schedule stratification factors. Example SAS code is provided in Appendix 7. The hazard ratio (HR) between the 2 treatment groups (fruquintinib vs placebo), together with its 95% CIs, will be calculated from a stratified Cox proportional hazard model (i.e. accounting for randomization schedule stratification factors) in which the treatment group is the only covariate in the model. A HR < 1 indicates a favorable clinical benefit from fruquintinib over the placebo group. Example SAS code is provided in Appendix 8."
>
> — SAP v1.4 (21 Jul 2022), combined Prot/SAP document §9.1.1 (Primary Efficacy Endpoint and Analysis), PDF p. 397 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/39/NCT04322539/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

```sas
*** Hazard ratio ***;
ods output hazardratios=hazrat1;
proc phreg
       data=ADTTE(where=(PARAMCD="OS"))
       alpha=0.05;
       model AVAL*CNSR(1)=TRTPN;
       strata STRAT1RN STRAT2RN STRAT3RN;
       hazardratio TRTPN;
run;
```
— SAP v1.4 (21 Jul 2022), combined Prot/SAP document Appendix 8 (Stratified Cox Proportional Hazard Model), PDF p. 482 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/39/NCT04322539/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

> "AVAL is the time in months, CNSR is the censoring variable, TRTPN is the treatment group variable, and STRAT1RN, STRAT2RN and STRAT3RN are placeholder variables representing the randomization schedule stratification factors. The output dataset (hazrat1) contains the hazard ratio (HazardRatio) and the corresponding 95% CI (WaldLower, WaldUpper)."
>
> — SAP v1.4 (21 Jul 2022), combined Prot/SAP document Appendix 8, PDF p. 482 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/39/NCT04322539/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

> "A 1-sided stratified log-rank test will be used for the comparison of OS of the fruquintinib with placebo group at a significance level of 0.025. The same stratification factors used for randomization (Section 7.3.1) will be used for analysis. Kaplan-Meier methodology will be used to estimate the median OS and its 2-sided 95% Confidence Interval (CI) for each treatment arm. Plots will be produced by treatment arm. The HR between the 2 treatment groups (fruquintinib vs placebo), together with its 95% CI, will be calculated from a stratified Cox proportional hazard model stratified by the randomization stratification factors."
>

> "Assuming an OS hazard ratio (HR) of 0.73 (fruquintinib arm/placebo arm), this sample size yields approximately 90% statistical power to detect superiority of the fruquintinib arm over placebo arm. ### capivasertib (Truqap) — NDA 218197

Therapeutic area: Oncology Sponsor: AstraZeneca Approval year: 2023 Phase-3 trial(s): CAPItello-291 (D3615C00001, NCT04305496, Phase 3, 1:1, double-blind, N=708); FAKTION (Phase 2, supportive; out of scope)

#### Model 1: CAPItello-291 (D3615C00001, NCT04305496) — PFS (investigator, RECIST 1.1), overall population (Primary (dual))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: IWRS values of geographic region (Region 1 US/Canada/W Europe/Australia/Israel; Region 2 Latin America/E Europe/Russia; Region 3 Asia), liver metastases (yes/no), prior CDK4/6 inhibitor (yes/no); pooling rule drops factors in order region, liver metastases, CDK4/6 if <10 events per stratum or <2 per arm within stratum; sensitivity with eCRF values allowed. As analysed (FDA MDR): region, liver metastases, prior CDK4/6
- Covariates: Treatment only (stratification variables in STRATA statement)
- Ties: Efron (Cox); log-rank test uses Breslow-equivalent ties
- CI/test: p-value from stratified log-rank; HR 95% CI and multiplicity-adjusted CI by profile likelihood; overall population alpha 0.035 (2-sided) within alpha-recycling MTP (Burman 2009), FWER 5% 2-sided
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Complementary log-log vs log(time) plots; if concerning, time-dependent covariate (treatment-by-time or treatment-by-ln(time)) interaction / Piecewise HRs over time periods (e.g. 0-6, 6-12 m); primary HR interpreted as average HR unless extensive crossing
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Events after >=2 missed visits censored at last evaluable assessment; sensitivity analyses for evaluation-time bias (midpoint), attrition bias (actual event times, censor at subsequent therapy; reverse-censoring KM), ascertainment bias (BICR), deviation bias, COVID-19 deaths
- Interim/sample size: PFS primary at ~542 events (77% maturity), critical HR 0.83, >99% power assuming HR 0.64 (control median 5.5 months)
- Software: SAS 9.4 or higher (protocol: SAS PROC PHREG with Efron)
- Result: HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.51, 0.71); 2-sided stratified log-rank p<0.001; events 258/355 vs 293/353; median 7.2 vs 3.6 months. BICR sensitivity HR 0.61 (0.50, 0.73)
- FDA comments: FDA agrees endpoints met but judged overall-population PFS benefit modest and driven by the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup; indication restricted to altered population
- Spec source: SAP Ed. 5.0 §4.2.2-4.2.3.1; Protocol §9.4.1.1; FDA MDR §8.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary endpoint PFS in the overall population based on the investigator RECIST v1.1 will be analysed using a log-rank test stratified by geographic region (Region 1: United States, Canada, Western Europe, Australia, and Israel, Region 2: Latin America, Eastern Europe and Russia vs Region 3: Asia), liver metastases (yes vs no), and prior use of CDK4/6 inhibitors (yes vs no) for generation of the p-value and using a method that corresponds to the Breslow approach for handling ties (Breslow N, 1974). To estimate the effect of treatment, the HR together with its 95% CI and CI adjusted for multiplicity will be estimated from a stratified Cox proportional hazards model (Cox DR, 1972) with ties = Efron and the stratification variables included in the strata statement and the CI calculated using the profile likelihood approach. A HR less than 1 will favour capivasertib + fulvestrant."
>
> — SAP Edition 5.0 (22 Nov 2022) §4.2.3.1 PFS in the overall population, PDF p. 79 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/96/NCT04305496/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The stratification variables in the statistical modelling will be based on the values entered into the interactive web response system (IWRS) at randomisation, even if it is subsequently discovered that these values were incorrect. A sensitivity analysis may be carried out using the (correct) stratification variables data collected in the eCRF."
>
> — SAP Edition 5.0 (22 Nov 2022) §4.2.3.1, PDF p. 79 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/96/NCT04305496/SAP_001.pdf)

> "If there are primary or secondary endpoints that still do not conform to this criterion, the randomisation stratification factors will be dropped in the following order by their importance: geographic location, liver metastases, CDK 4/6 inhibitor."
>
> — SAP Edition 5.0 (22 Nov 2022) §4.2.2 Pooling strategy, PDF p. 79 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/96/NCT04305496/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The assumption of proportionality will be assessed. Proportional hazards will be tested firstly by examining plots of complementary log-log (probability of PFS) versus log (time) and, if these raise concerns, by fitting a time dependent covariate (adding a treatment-by-time or treatment-by-ln(time) interaction term) to assess the extent to which this represents random variation. If a lack of proportionality is evident, the variation in treatment effect can be described by presenting piecewise HR calculated over distinct time-periods for example 0 – 6 m, 6 – 12 m etc. In such circumstances, the HR from the primary analysis can still be meaningfully interpreted as an average HR over time unless there is extensive crossing of the survival curves."
>
> — SAP Edition 5.0 (22 Nov 2022) §4.2.3.1 Assumptions of proportionality, PDF p. 80 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/96/NCT04305496/SAP_001.pdf)

> "From the stratified Cox proportional hazards model (ties = Efron) the HR (capivasertib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant) together with its corresponding 95% CI (calculated using a profile likelihood approach) will be presented. An HR less than 1 will favour capivasertib +"
>
> — Clinical Study Protocol v5.0 (1 Aug 2023) §9.4.1.1, PDF p. 113 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/96/NCT04305496/Prot_003.pdf)

> "Treatment groups were compared using a log-rank test stratified by geographic region, presence of liver metastases, and prior use of CDK4/6 inhibitors, and using a method that corresponds to the Breslow approach for handling ties. To estimate the effect of treatment, the hazard ratio together with its 95% CI and CI adjusted for multiplicity were estimated from a stratified Cox proportional hazards model with the Efron method for handling ties and the stratification variables included in the strata statement and the CI calculated using the profile likelihood approach. A hazard ratio less than 1 favored capivasertib + fulvestrant. The dual primary endpoint of PFS in the Altered Population was analyzed in the same way, except that the log-rank test and Cox model were stratified by presence of liver metastases and prior use of CDK4/6 inhibitors."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review NDA 218197 §8.1.2, PDF p. 94 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/218197Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "FDA agrees that CAPItello-291 met its dual primary endpoints; however, the PFS improvement in the overall population was modest and was primarily driven by the PFS improvement in PI3KCA/AKT1/PTEN-altered. FDA concludes that there was only a clinically meaningful improvement in PFS in the population of patients whose tumors harbored a PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-alteration."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review NDA 218197 FDA Assessment of PFS, PDF p. 106 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/218197Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 2: CAPItello-291 (D3615C00001, NCT04305496) — PFS (investigator), PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup (Primary (dual))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Randomization stratification variables (subject to pooling); as analysed per FDA MDR: liver metastases and prior CDK4/6 (region dropped)
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: As overall population; alpha 0.021 or 0.05 (if overall rejected) per recycling MTP; profile-likelihood CI
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Complementary log-log vs log(time) plots; if concerning, time-dependent covariate (treatment-by-time or treatment-by-ln(time)) interaction (as overall population) / Piecewise HRs over time periods (e.g. 0-6, 6-12 m); primary HR interpreted as average HR unless extensive crossing
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: As overall population
- Interim/sample size: ~217 events (174 if 20% test failure); power 83.7% at alpha 0.021 or 90.8% at 0.05 assuming HR 0.64
- Software: SAS 9.4 or higher
- Result: HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.38, 0.65); p<0.001; events 121/155 vs 115/134; median 7.3 vs 3.1 months; BICR HR 0.51 (0.38, 0.68)
- FDA comments: FDA concluded clinically meaningful PFS improvement only in the altered population
- Spec source: SAP Ed. 5.0 §4.2.3.2; FDA MDR Table 18

### nirogacestat (Ogsiveo) — NDA 217677

Therapeutic area: Oncology Sponsor: SpringWorks Therapeutics, Inc. Approval year: 2023 Phase-3 trial(s): DeFi (NIR-DT-301, NCT03785964, Phase 3, 1:1, double-blind, 142 randomized)

#### Model 1: DeFi (NIR-DT-301, NCT03785964) — PFS (BICR radiographic per RECIST 1.1 or EAC-qualified clinical progression, or death) (Primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Primary tumor location (intra-abdominal vs extra-abdominal), as assigned at randomization
- Covariates: Treatment arm only (MODEL statement); tumor location in STRATA statement
- Ties: Exact (ties = EXACT)
- CI/test: 1-sided stratified log-rank test (PROC LIFETEST method=PL) at alpha 0.025; HR with 2-sided 95% CI from stratified Cox; hierarchical testing PFS then secondary endpoints
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated for PFS (PRO addendum specifies complementary log-log vs log(time) plots for PRO time-to-event) / Not stated; interval-censoring sensitivity analysis (PROC ICLIFETEST) is a log-rank-type test, not a Cox model
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: No progression/death censored at last response assessment; no assessments censored at randomization; new anticancer therapy before progression censored at last adequate assessment; sensitivity: BICR-confirmed events only, all PI clinical progressions, PP set, first missed assessment as event date, local RECIST for 15 early participants, centrally confirmed diagnosis, interval censoring
- Interim/sample size: 51 events for 90% power, 1-sided 0.025, HR 0.4 (median 20 vs 8 months), 118 planned (142 randomized due to COVID-19 screening backlog); protocol interim at 26 events (Lan-DeMets OBF, futility HR >0.91, efficacy HR <=0.31) dropped in SAP v2.0; primary analysis at 49 events
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG (ties=EXACT), PROC LIFETEST, PROC ICLIFETEST
- Result: HR 0.29 (95% CI 0.15, 0.55); 1-sided stratified log-rank p<0.001; events 12/70 vs 37/72; median NE vs 15.1 months. Radiographic-only HR 0.31 (MDR reports CI as 0.16-0.62 in one place and 0.15-0.62 in another); PP HR 0.26 (0.13, 0.53)
- FDA comments: FDA agrees; FDA re-analysed PFS excluding 6 patients with concomitant excision/radiotherapy (revised PP) HR 0.25 (0.12, 0.52); OSI discrepancy changed one censoring date without changing HR; FDA noted possible bias in timing of clinical-progression determinations. README discrepancy: README says 118 randomized; 142 were randomized (70 vs 72)
- Spec source: SAP v2.0 §3.6, §4.3.1.1-4.3.1.2, §5; Protocol Amendment 5 §9.4; FDA MDR §8.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

A stratified log-rank test on PFS will be performed using SAS PROC LIFETEST with method = PL option (Kaplan-Meier estimates, also known as the product-limit estimates). The hazard ratio with 2-sided 95% CI will be estimated from the stratified Cox proportional hazards model using SAS PHREG procedure with ties = EXACT option in the model. In this analysis, the baseline hazard function will be allowed to vary across strata, i.e., the MODEL statement will include treatment arm variable as the only covariate and the STRATA statement will include tumor location."
>

### tislelizumab-jsgr (Tevimbra) — BLA 761232

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: BeiGene, Ltd. / BeiGene USA, Inc. Approval year: 2024. Phase-3 trial(s): RATIONALE-302 (BGB-A317-302, NCT03430843), Phase 3, open-label, tislelizumab vs investigator-chosen chemotherapy (ICC), 2L ESCC.

#### Model 1: RATIONALE-302 (NCT03430843) — Overall survival (ITT) (Primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: ECOG PS (0 vs 1) and ICC option (paclitaxel vs docetaxel vs irinotecan), as recorded in IWRS; third randomization factor region (Asia ex-Japan / Japan / US-EU) deliberately excluded from the model (sparse events, small Japan enrolment)
- Covariates: Treatment arm only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% CI for HR (method Not stated); hypothesis test = one-sided stratified log-rank test at alpha 0.025; Cox used for HR only
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated (no PH test specified) / SAP: 'If necessary' RMST and MaxCombo to account for possible non-proportional hazards; RPSFT for subsequent ICI therapy (Appendix 10.6)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at last known alive date or data cut-off, whichever earlier
- Interim/sample size: No interim analysis; ~400 deaths, ~500 pts, assumed HR 0.75 (median 8 vs 6 mo), 82% power, one-sided alpha 0.025, 5%/yr dropout
- Software: SAS version 9.2 or higher (procedure not named)
- Result: Stratified HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.57-0.85), one-sided stratified log-rank p=0.0001; deaths 197/256 vs 213/256; unstratified HR 0.69 (0.57-0.84); data cutoff 01-Dec-2020
- FDA comments: FDA explained exclusion of region: 'potential sparse number of events'. Applicant sensitivity Cox models reported (PP set HR 0.68; CRF strata HR 0.69; region added as stratum HR 0.70; mITT HR 0.69; PD-L1 status as covariate HR 0.72 or as additional stratum HR 0.70). FDA noted greater subsequent anti-PD-(L)1 use in ICC arm (21.5% vs 4.3%).
- Spec source: SAP v3.0 §6.2.3, §6.4.1; FDA MDR §8.1

The stratification factor region (Asia excluding Japan, Japan, US/EU) will not be adjusted in the model."
