### inavolisib (Itovebi) — NDA 219249

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Genentech, Inc. (Roche). Approval year: 2024. Phase-3 trial(s): INAVO120 (WO41554, NCT04191499), Phase 3, double-blind, inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + palbociclib + fulvestrant.

#### Model 1: INAVO120 (NCT04191499) — Investigator-assessed PFS (Primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Randomization factors as entered in IxRS: visceral disease (yes/no), endocrine resistance (primary/secondary), geographic region (North America/Western Europe, Asia, Other)
- Covariates: Treatment arm only (implied; not explicitly listed)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI for HR (method Not stated); test = two-sided stratified log-rank at 0.05; Cox for HR only
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Treatment-policy estimand for intercurrent events (NPT, discontinuation ignored); no event censored at last tumor assessment before CCOD (or randomization if no post-baseline assessment); supplementary hypothetical (censor at NPT) and composite (NPT=event) strategies
- Interim/sample size: 194 PFS events, 85% power for HR 0.65 (11 to 16.9 mo), two-sided alpha 0.05; non-binding futility IA at 75 events (HR>1.1)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.32-0.59), p<0.0001; median PFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo; N=161 vs 164 (events per arm not in extractable text)
- FDA comments: FDA summarized sensitivity analyses (BICR, unstratified, central PIK3CA, missed assessments) and supplementary ICE analyses as supportive; no disagreement on the Cox model.
- Spec source: SAP §4.2.2-4.2.4; Protocol statistical section

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The hazard ratio will be estimated using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model. The 95% CI for the hazard ratio will be provided. The stratification factors used will be the same as the randomization stratification factors (as entered in IxRS, Section 1.2.1). Results from an unstratified analysis (see Section 4.2.3) will also be provided as sensitivity analysis."
>
> — INAVO120 SAP (WO41554), SAP §4.2.2, PDF p. 19 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/99/NCT04191499/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The treatment effect will be quantified via a hazard ratio, computed from a stratified Cox proportional-hazards regression, including a 95% confidence interval."
>
> — INAVO120 Protocol (WO41554), Protocol, statistical methods, PDF p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/99/NCT04191499/Prot_000.pdf)

> "PFS assessed by investigator based on unstratified analysis: To assess the impact of stratification (as entered in IxRS, see Protocol Section 6.4.1) the main analysis described in Section 4.2.2 will be repeated without stratification factors."
>
> — INAVO120 SAP (WO41554), SAP §4.2.3 Sensitivity analyses, PDF p. 19 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/99/NCT04191499/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Sensitivity analyses to the primary estimand of the primary PFS were performed by BICR- assessed PFS, investigator-assessed PFS based on unstratified analysis, investigator-assessed PFS in patients with PIK3CA mutation-positive status by the central test, and based on handling of missing scheduled tumor assessments."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 219249), FDA MDR §8.1 Statistical Analysis of Efficacy Endpoints, PDF p. 99 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/219249Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 2: INAVO120 (NCT04191499) — Overall survival (Key secondary (hierarchical, group-sequential))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Same IxRS randomization factors as PFS
- Covariates: Treatment arm only (implied)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; stratified log-rank test; Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming boundary (interim boundary p<=0.0098)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated

- FDA comments: FDA: no OS detriment; final OS PMC.
- Spec source: SAP §4.3.1.1; FDA MDR Table 23

### zolbetuximab-clzb (Vyloy) — BLA 761365

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Astellas Pharma Global Development, Inc. Approval year: 2024. Phase-3 trial(s): SPOTLIGHT (8951-CL-0301, NCT03504397) and GLOW (8951-CL-0302, NCT03653507); both Phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled.

#### Model 1: SPOTLIGHT (NCT03504397) — IRC-assessed PFS (Primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (FDA review table footnotes describe it as a Cox model with region, organs, gastrectomy 'as the explanatory variables')
- Stratification: Region (Asia vs non-Asia), number of organs with metastatic sites (0-2 vs >=3), prior gastrectomy (Y/N), from IRT; 'Stratified Analysis #2' repeated with eCRF strata
- Covariates: Treatment (footnote lists stratification factors as explanatory variables — ambiguous whether strata or covariates)
- Ties: Not stated for clinical endpoints (main clinical SAP not public)
- CI/test: 95% CI; test = stratified one-sided log-rank at 0.025; Cox for HR only
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated (footnote: 'Assuming proportional hazards') / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censor at last radiological assessment; censor at last assessment before new anticancer therapy; event after >=2 missed assessments censored at last assessment
- Interim/sample size: Single final PFS analysis at 300 events; 93.4% power for HR 0.67 (9 vs 6 mo), one-sided 0.025
- Software: Not stated (PRO SAP: SAS 9.4 PROC PHREG)
- Result: HR 0.751 (95% CI 0.598-0.942), one-sided p=0.0066; events 146/283 vs 167/282; eCRF-strata HR 0.745 (0.594-0.935); data cutoff 09-Sep-2022
- FDA comments: FDA agreed with primary result. After inspection found 21 accidental unblinding incidents (incl. IRT vendor upload covering 48% of SPOTLIGHT patients), FDA requested and ran sensitivity analyses: applicant censoring-at-unblinding HR 0.735 (0.568-0.951); FDA post hoc stratified Cox by in-scope (HR 0.72) vs not-in-scope (HR 0.78) patients; censoring death after new ATC HR 0.80 (0.63-1.03).
- Spec source: Protocol v8.0 §7.4.1.1; FDA MDR §8.1 tables 13-15

### ensartinib (Ensacove) — NDA 218171

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Xcovery Holdings, Inc. Approval year: 2024. Phase-3 trial(s): eXalt3 (X396-CLI-301, NCT02767804), Phase 3, open-label, ensartinib vs crizotinib, ALK+ NSCLC.

#### Model 1: eXalt3 (NCT02767804) — BICR/IRR-assessed PFS (Primary (HR from unstratified Cox))

- Model type: Standard (unstratified) Cox
- Stratification: None (primary). Randomization factors: prior chemotherapy, ECOG PS, CNS metastases, region
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Breslow (ties=BRESLOW in SAP code)
- CI/test: risklimits (Wald) 95% CI; primary test = UNSTRATIFIED log-rank, two-sided 0.05; stratified log-rank supportive
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censor at last adequate assessment; at randomization if no on-study or inadequate baseline assessment; at last assessment before alternate therapy; >16-week gap (2+ missed) before event censored at last adequate assessment
- Interim/sample size: 190 PFS events (266 pts) for HR 0.625 (10 vs 16 mo), 90% power, two-sided 0.05; IA at 143 events (75%) with O'Brien-Fleming Lan-DeMets, two-sided 0.019
- Software: SAS 9.4 PROC PHREG / PROC LIFETEST
- Result: Label: HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.40-0.79), unstratified log-rank p=0.0007; events 59/143 vs 80/147. Publication (interim, cutoff 1-Jul-2020): HR 0.51 (0.35-0.72), log-rank P<.001
- FDA comments: No FDA review posted.
- Spec source: SAP v3.0 §8.2 (in JAMA Oncol Supplement 1); Protocol §15.7.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "PFS by IRR will be tested using the log-rank test without stratification. A stratified logrank test will be used as supportive evidence of efficacy."
>
> — JAMA Oncol 2021 Supplement 1 (eXalt3 protocol X396-CLI-301 + SAP v3.0, 14-Oct-2019), SAP v3.0 §8.2.1 (PDF p. 128-129), PDF p. 128 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8414368/ (supplement jamaoncol-e213523-s001.pdf, retrieved via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles))

> "Hazard ratio estimates will also be presented using Cox models without the stratification factors at randomization. The supportive analysis will be presented using Cox models with stratification factors at randomization included as covariates."
>
> — JAMA Oncol 2021 Supplement 1 (eXalt3 protocol X396-CLI-301 + SAP v3.0, 14-Oct-2019), SAP v3.0 §8.2.1, PDF p. 129 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8414368/ (supplement jamaoncol-e213523-s001.pdf, retrieved via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles))

```sas
Cox proportional model without stratification will use the following SAS® code (SAS
Version 9.4 or more current):
   proc phreg data=DATA_NAME;
       class TREATMENT;
       model PFSTIME*CENSOR(0)=TREATMENT /risklimits ties=BRESLOW;
   run;
```
— JAMA Oncol 2021 Supplement 1 (eXalt3 protocol X396-CLI-301 + SAP v3.0, 14-Oct-2019), SAP v3.0 §8.2.1 (SAS code), PDF p. 129 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8414368/ (supplement jamaoncol-e213523-s001.pdf, retrieved via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles))

```sas
The following SAS® code (SAS Version 9.4 or more current) will be used for unstratified
log-rank test for TREATMENT, as the primary efficacy analysis.
   proc lifetest data=DATA_NAME ;
       time PFSTIME*CENSOR(0);
       strata TREATMENT;
   run;
```
— JAMA Oncol 2021 Supplement 1 (eXalt3 protocol X396-CLI-301 + SAP v3.0, 14-Oct-2019), SAP v3.0 §8.2.1 (SAS code), PDF p. 129 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8414368/ (supplement jamaoncol-e213523-s001.pdf, retrieved via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles))

> "PFS analysis will be based on the log-rank test. A stratified log rank test will be used as supportive evidence of efficacy."
>
> — JAMA Oncol 2021 Supplement 1 (eXalt3 protocol X396-CLI-301 + SAP v3.0, 14-Oct-2019), Protocol §15.7.1, PDF p. 64 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8414368/ (supplement jamaoncol-e213523-s001.pdf, retrieved via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles))

> "CI = Confidence Interval; NE=not estimable; BICR = Blinded Independent Central Review a p-value based on unstratified log-rank test"
>
> — ENSACOVE label (2024), ENSACOVE label §14 Table 6 footnote, PDF p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/218171s000lbl.pdf)

> "The primary end point was compared between the ensartinib and crizotinib groups by using a 2-sided log-rank test according to the factors used for randomization. For all time-to-event efficacy analyses, median values were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. Hazard ratios were estimated by using the Cox proportional hazards regression model."

#### Model 4: eXalt3 (NCT02767804) — Time to CNS progression (IRR) (Key secondary (exploratory, not alpha-controlled) — competing-risks supportive)

- Model type: Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards (stratified, weighted PHREG via %PSHREG); main analysis same as PFS Cox; publication reports cause-specific HR
- Stratification: Stratification factors from eCRF used to stratify baseline hazard (code: STRATA strate1 strate2)
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Not stated

- Censoring: Competing events: non-CNS progression and death
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable

- Result: Publication (patients without baseline brain mets): cause-specific HR 0.32 (95% CI 0.16-0.63), P=.001

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Time to CNS progression per IRR will be analyzed using the same methods as the primary PFS analysis supported by an analysis with a competing risks model, in which non-CNS progression and death are competing risks in the analysis."

```sas
VARLIST=Treat, OUT=outds_wgt)
```

### datopotamab deruxtecan-dlnk (Datroway) — BLA 761394

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Daiichi Sankyo, Inc. (with AstraZeneca). Approval year: 2025. Phase-3 trial(s): TROPION-Breast01 (D9268C00001, NCT05104866), Phase 3, open-label, Dato-DXd vs investigator's choice chemotherapy (ICC).

#### Model 1: TROPION-Breast01 (NCT05104866) — BICR-assessed PFS (Dual primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Number of previous lines of chemotherapy (1 vs 2), geographic region (US/Canada/Europe vs RoW), prior CDK4/6i (Y/N) — IRT values; pre-specified pooling if <10 events in a stratum or <2 per arm (CDK4/6 pooled first, then lines, then region)
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: Profile likelihood CI (95% and alpha-level-matched 99% CI); test = stratified log-rank (LIFETEST with TEST statement), two-sided alpha 1.0%
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: log(-log(S)) vs log(time) plots; if concerns, time-dependent covariate (treatment-by-time or treatment-by-ln(time)) / Piecewise HRs over time periods (0-6m, 6-12m...); HR interpreted as average unless extensive crossing; investigate treatment-by-covariate interaction
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: RECIST censoring; sensitivity analyses for evaluation-time, attrition, ascertainment bias, subsequent therapy; eCRF stratification sensitivity
- Interim/sample size: 419 BICR PFS events (60% maturity), HR 0.55 (4.7 vs 8.5 mo), >99% power at two-sided 1.0%
- Software: SAS (PROC LIFETEST, PROC PHREG)
- Result: HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.76; 99% CI 0.49-0.80), p<0.0001; events 212/365 vs 235/367
- FDA comments: FDA sensitivity analyses: eCRF strata Cox HR 0.63; unstratified Cox HR 0.64; interval-censoring HR 0.61; worst-case censoring scenarios HR 0.74/0.78; tipping-point analysis for 23 ICC patients censored at randomization (imbalanced early censoring) — supportive.
- Spec source: SAP ed. 3.0 §4.2.1; FDA MDR §8.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The HR and CI are estimated from a stratified Cox Proportional Hazards model (with ties = Efron and stratification variables number of previous lines of chemotherapy, geographic region, and prior use of CDK4/6 inhibitor) and the CI calculated using a profile likelihood approach. A HR less than 1 favours Dato-DXd."
>
> — TROPION-Breast01 SAP ed. 3.0 (17-Aug-2023; CSR App. 16.1.9), SAP ed. 3.0 §4.2.1.4, PDF p. 51 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/66/NCT05104866/SAP_001.pdf)

> "If there are less than 10 events in total for a unique stratum or less than 2 events in either treatment group for a unique stratum then the strata are combined in the following order. The CDK4/6 strata (Yes vs No) are pooled first, followed by the number of previous lines of chemotherapy strata (1 vs 2) and then finally by the geographic region strata (United States, Canada, Europe vs Rest of World)."
>
> — TROPION-Breast01 SAP ed. 3.0 (17-Aug-2023; CSR App. 16.1.9), SAP ed. 3.0 §4.2.1.4, PDF p. 51 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/66/NCT05104866/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Proportional hazards will be tested firstly by examining plots of log(-log(survival probability)) versus log (time) and, if these raise concerns, by fitting a time dependent covariate (adding a treatment-by-time or treatment-by-ln(time) interaction term) to assess the extent to which this represents random variation."
>
> — TROPION-Breast01 SAP ed. 3.0 (17-Aug-2023; CSR App. 16.1.9), SAP ed. 3.0 §4.2.1.4 Proportionality assumption, PDF p. 51 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/66/NCT05104866/SAP_001.pdf)

> "In such circumstances, the HR from the primary analysis can still be meaningfully interpreted as an average HR over the observed extent of follow-up unless there is extensive crossing of the survival curves."
>
> — TROPION-Breast01 SAP ed. 3.0 (17-Aug-2023; CSR App. 16.1.9), SAP ed. 3.0 §4.2.1.4, PDF p. 51 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/66/NCT05104866/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Where analysis models are stratified by the randomisation stratification factors, the data from the Interactive Response Technology (IRT) will be used, not the values recorded in the electronic case report form (eCRF), therefore follows the principles of intention to treat (ITT)."
>
> — TROPION-Breast01 SAP ed. 3.0 (17-Aug-2023; CSR App. 16.1.9), SAP ed. 3.0 §3.3, PDF p. 129 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/66/NCT05104866/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The hazard ratio and CI were estimated from a stratified Cox Proportional Hazards model (with ties = Efron), and the CI calculated using a profile likelihood approach. The stratification variables were defined according to data from the IRT"
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review (BLA 761394), FDA MDR §8.1 Statistical Analysis Plan, PDF p. 130 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761394Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "In the primary analysis of PFS and OS, stratification factor data collected from IRT was used in the stratified log-rank test and stratified Cox regression model to follow the intent-to-treat principle. Subgroup analyses by stratification factor were based on stratification factor data collected from the eCRF."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review (BLA 761394), FDA MDR §8.1.2, PDF p. 139 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761394Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 2: TROPION-Breast01 (NCT05104866) — Overall survival (Dual primary (alpha 4% + recycled 1%))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Same as PFS (IRT)
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Efron (same methodology as PFS)
- CI/test: Profile likelihood CI; stratified log-rank; Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming across 3 analyses, total two-sided 5%
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: SAP: same as PFS. FDA: KM curves crossed at ~month 20 at final analysis / FDA requested RMST at multiple cutoffs (supportive only): differences 0.17-0.60 months favoring Dato-DXd
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Alive censored at last known alive; FDA concerned with 23 ICC patients censored (withdrawal/randomized-not-treated)
- Interim/sample size: ~444 deaths (63% maturity), HR 0.75, ICC median 19.0 mo, 85% power two-sided 5%; IAs at ~40% and ~80% IF
- Software: SAS
- Result: Final (DCO 24-Jul-2024): HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.83-1.22), p=0.94; deaths 223/365 vs 213/367. IA1 HR 0.84 (0.62-1.14); IA2 HR 0.93 (0.76-1.13)
- FDA comments: FDA: crossing curves violate PH assumption, requested RMST. Sensitivity Cox: eCRF strata HR 1.00; unstratified HR 1.01; tipping point HR 1.09; censoring 23 ICC pts at cutoff HR 1.09; applicant post hoc IPCW HR 0.86 judged not interpretable (untestable no-unmeasured-confounders). Concluded no OS benefit but no clear detriment.
- Spec source: SAP ed. 3.0 §4.2.2; FDA MDR §8.1.2 (FDA Tables 26, 28; Figures 13-14)

>

#### Model 3: TROPION-Breast01 (NCT05104866) — PFS subgroups and global interaction test (Subgroup)

- Model type: Unstratified Cox per subgroup level (BY statement); global interaction Cox model (treatment + covariates + interactions, LRT at 10%)
- Stratification: None within subgroup
- Covariates: Treatment only (subgroups); all covariates and covariate-by-treatment interactions (global test)
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% profile likelihood CI; subgroups with <20 events not analysed
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: As primary
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG
- Result: FDA Figure 12 subgroup forest plot (values not extracted)
- FDA comments: Subgroups by eCRF stratification data.

### penpulimab-kcqx (unbranded) — BLA 761258

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Akeso Biopharma, Inc. Approval year: 2025. Phase-3 trial(s): AK105-304 (NCT04974398), Phase 3, double-blind, penpulimab + gemcitabine/platinum vs placebo + chemo, 1L R/M NPC (AK105-202 is single-arm Phase 2: no Cox).

#### Model 1: AK105-304 (NCT04974398) — BICR-assessed PFS (Primary (interim analysis at 189 events))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Applicant: stage at entry (primary metastases vs recurrent), ECOG (0 vs 1), liver metastases (from IWRS) + investigator's choice of platinum (carboplatin vs cisplatin, from EDC; added by SAP v1.2, 05-Sep-2023). FDA: excluded the platinum factor (not a randomization factor; 2.4% carboplatin -> sparse strata)
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: 95% CI; stratified log-rank two-sided; O'Brien-Fleming boundary on observed IF (IA boundary p=0.030 at 189 events)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated in detail (sensitivity 3: PD/death after >=2 missed assessments counted as event)
- Interim/sample size: 222 events for 89% power, HR 0.65 (7 vs 10.8 mo), two-sided 0.05; IA moved from 155 (70%) to ~190 events (86%) with FDA agreement; conducted at 189 (85%)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.33-0.62), two-sided p<0.0001; events 80/144 vs 109/147; unstratified HR 0.53 (0.40-0.71); EDC strata HR 0.45 (0.33-0.63)
- FDA comments: FDA re-ran stratified Cox without the post hoc chemo-choice stratum: numerically identical results. Noted interim timing changes and China-only enrolment (21 CFR 314.106(b)).
- Spec source: FDA MDR §8.1 (protocol/SAP not public)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "[c] A stratified Cox proportional hazard regression model with tied events handled by the Efron's method is used. For the stratified analysis, the stratification factors are the same as above."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review (BLA 761258, Ref ID 5577575), FDA MDR Applicant Table 11 footnote, PDF p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761258Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "[b] For the stratified analysis, the stratification factors are stage of disease at study entry (primary metastases vs. recurrent), ECOG score (0 vs. 1), liver metastases (present vs absent) obtained from the IWRS and investigator’s choice of chemotherapy regimens (carboplatin vs. cisplatin) obtained from the EDC."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review (BLA 761258, Ref ID 5577575), FDA MDR Applicant Table 11 footnote, PDF p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761258Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "1) Included the investigator’s choice of platinum chemotherapy as a stratification factor in the stratified analysis of PFS and OS endpoints."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review (BLA 761258, Ref ID 5577575), FDA MDR SAP amendment history (V1.2, 05Sep2023), PDF p. 91 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761258Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "FDA’s stratified analysis of PFS did not include the stratification factor of investigator’s choice of chemotherapy (cisplatin vs. carboplatin) as it was not a stratification factor originally considered at the time of randomization. Additionally, only 2.4% of all randomized patients received carboplatin which in turn resulted in sparse strata."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review (BLA 761258, Ref ID 5577575), FDA MDR §8.1.2 FDA's Assessment, PDF p. 108 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761258Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Sensitivity analysis 1: The unstratified log-rank test and unstratified Cox proportional hazards regression model was performed to compare PFS time between two groups, HR=0.53 (95% CI: 0.40, 0.71), P<0.0001."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review (BLA 761258, Ref ID 5577575), FDA MDR §8.1.2, PDF p. 107 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761258Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Subgroup analyses are performed based on an unstratified Cox proportional hazards regression model with tied events handled by the Efron's method."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review (BLA 761258, Ref ID 5577575), FDA MDR subgroup forest plot footnote, PDF p. 107 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761258Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 2: AK105-304 (NCT04974398) — Overall survival (Key secondary (descriptive at PFS IA with nominal alpha 0.0001; first formal IA at 70% IF))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Applicant: as PFS (incl. platinum choice). FDA: stage, ECOG, liver mets (IWRS) only
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: 95% CI; stratified log-rank; O'Brien-Fleming boundary (p=0.0150 at 70% IF)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: 172 deaths, 80% power, HR 0.65 (29 vs 44.6 mo); IAs planned at 103 (60%) and 138 (80%) deaths; first formal IA done at 121 (70%)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Descriptive (DCO 29-Apr-2024): HR 0.94 (0.63-1.40), deaths 48/144 vs 49/147; unstratified 0.97. FDA first formal IA (DCO 24-Jan-2025): HR 0.91 (0.64-1.31), p=0.615, deaths 58/146 vs 63/150
- FDA comments: FDA: interpretation challenging — 49% crossover to penpulimab, 80% of placebo patients received penpulimab or another anti-PD-(L)1; no apparent detriment.
- Spec source: FDA MDR §8.1.2, FDA Table 6

### Dordaviprone (Modeyso) — NDA 219876

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Chimerix, Inc. Approval year: 2025. Phase-3 trial(s): Pooled single-arm studies ONC006, ONC013, ONC014, ONC016, ONC018 (no Phase 3 efficacy data; Phase 3 ACTION/ONC201-108 ongoing, no results).

**Excluded.** Excluded: no Phase 3 trial contributes efficacy data. Cox models appear only in (a) exploratory landmark and time-varying-covariate analyses of response vs overall survival within the pooled single-arm (Phase 1/2) integrated efficacy population, which FDA called exploratory and difficult to interpret without randomization, and (b) exposure-response Cox models (Table 19.5). The confirmatory Phase 3 ACTION trial (NCT05580562) was ongoing with no efficacy readout at approval.

##### Supporting excerpts

> "Additionally, a multivariate Cox model analyzed overall survival with RANO 2.0 response as a time-varying covariate, considering patients as non-responders until their first response, and including other factors through backward selection."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 219876, Ref ID 5638121), FDA MDR §8.1 (Applicant's description), PDF p. 108 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219876Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "FDA considers results for the association between ORR and overall survival to be exploratory as these results are difficult to interpret in the absence of randomization and a control arm."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 219876, Ref ID 5638121), FDA MDR §8.1 FDA's Assessment, PDF p. 109 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219876Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

### Imlunestrant (Inluriyo) — NDA 218881

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Eli Lilly and Company. Approval year: 2025. Phase-3 trial(s): EMBER-3 (J2J-OX-JZLC, NCT04975308), Phase 3, open-label, imlunestrant vs investigator-choice ET (fulvestrant/exemestane) [Arm C imlunestrant+abemaciclib out of scope].

#### Model 1: EMBER-3 (NCT04975308) — Investigator-assessed PFS, ESR1m-detected population (H2) (Primary (approval basis))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Prior CDK4/6i (Y/N) and visceral metastases (Y/N) from IWRS; region excluded to reduce strata from 12 to 4
- Covariates: Treatment as only covariate
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI (method Not stated); stratified log-rank, one-sided alpha 0.02 (graphical procedure); reported 2-sided p
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / RMST reported in FDA table (restriction time 19.38 mo, difference 2.56 mo) — not prespecified as non-PH remedy in SAP text found
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: PFS event/censoring scheme table in SAP §4.3.2; sensitivity with alternative censoring rules
- Interim/sample size: Final analysis only at ~192 events; HR 0.57 (TPC median 3.6 mo), ~97% power at one-sided 0.02
- Software: SAS 9.4 or higher; EAST 6.5 for boundaries
- Result: Stratified HR 0.617 (95% CI 0.464-0.821), 2-sided p=0.0008; events 109/138 vs 102/118; RMST difference 2.56 (1.19-3.93) mo
- FDA comments: FDA noted Applicant's description stated three-factor stratification for ITT but region was removed from all ESR1m analyses (clarified via IR 06-Feb-2025). ESR1m not a stratification factor -> imbalance risk addressed by prespecified multivariate Cox. Sensitivity Cox: unstratified 0.605; CRF strata 0.612; + randomization-scheme stratum 0.602; ITT-strata 0.623; multivariate (prior CDK4/6i, age group, bone-only) 0.591; PP 0.532.
- Spec source: SAP v5 §4.3.2-4.3.4; FDA MDR §8.1

> "In a response to FDA’s Information Request dated February 6, 2025, the Applicant clarified that region was removed from all stratified analyses in the ESR1m-detected population to reduce the number of strata."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 218881, Ref ID 5665313), FDA MDR §8.1, PDF p. 120 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218881Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

### vepdegestrant (Veppanu) — NDA 219835

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Arvinas, Inc. / Pfizer Inc. Approval year: 2026. Phase-3 trial(s): VERITAC-2 (C4891001, NCT05654623), Phase 3, open-label, vepdegestrant vs fulvestrant.

#### Model 1: VERITAC-2 (NCT05654623) — BICR-assessed PFS, ESR1m population (Primary (approval basis))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Visceral disease (Y/N) from IRT in ESR1m population (FDA figure footnote); ITT: ESR1 mutation status and visceral disease (IRT)
- Covariates: Treatment as covariate
- Ties: Exact method
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% CI (method Not stated); stratified log-rank one-sided at 0.01875 (graphical procedure)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Schoenfeld residual test (Grambsch-Therneau), p<0.05 indicates departure / RMST difference as supplementary analysis at three tau choices (Zhang 2013)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Primary censors at new anticancer therapy and after >=2 missed assessments; supplementary treatment-policy and composite estimands
- Interim/sample size: 165 events, 88% power for HR<0.60, one-sided 0.01875
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Stratified HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.418-0.770), one-sided p=0.0001; median 5.0 vs 2.1 mo
- FDA comments: FDA found first 33 ESR1m BICR confirmation-of-progression reads potentially unblinded to investigator assessment; Cox sensitivity excluding them HR 0.58 (0.41-0.81). Hypothesis-testing order amended at FDA request (SAP v2). 6% per arm mis-stratified; CRF-strata sensitivity analysis 4.
- Spec source: SAP §5.2.1, §6.1.1; FDA MDR §8.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "For PFS and OS analyses, the log-rank test will be used for comparing treatments. Hazard ratios and the associated 2-sided 95% CIs are estimated by Cox proportional hazards models, including treatment as a covariate. Ties in the event times will be handled by the exact method."
>
> — VERITAC-2 SAP (C4891001, final 05/07-Nov-2024), SAP §5.2.1, PDF p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/23/NCT05654623/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The proportional hazards (PH) assumption will be tested using Schoenfeld s residual test (Therneau and Grambsch, 1994). The departures from PH could be evidenced by a p-value <0.05. If there is evidence of departures from proportional hazards, then PFS and OS may be analyzed based on restricted mean survival time (RMST) differences as a supplementary analysis (Zhang, 2013)."
>
> — VERITAC-2 SAP (C4891001, final 05/07-Nov-2024), SAP §5.2.1, PDF p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/23/NCT05654623/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Sensitivity 1 is the unstratified analysis of primary PFS and the rest are stratified by Visceral disease status (Yes/No)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 219835, Ref ID 5789627), FDA MDR Figure (Applicant SCE Figure 6) footnote, PDF p. 132 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219835Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "However, a sensitivity analysis excluding these 33 patients from the analysis population demonstrated a PFS HR of 0.58 (95% CI: 0.41, 0.81), consistent with the primary analysis HR of 0.57 (95% CI: 0.42, 0.77)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 219835, Ref ID 5789627), FDA MDR §8.1.2, PDF p. 153 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219835Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "value from CRF (instead of IRT) will be used for the two stratification factors in this analysis. The censoring rules will follow the primary PFS analysis."

> "Multivariate analysis (covariate-adjusted) (PFS Supplementary Analysis 1) – HR for PFS with the corresponding 2-sided 95% CI will be calculated based on Cox’s Proportional Hazard model with stratification factors (based on CRF) and baseline characteristics as covariates"

>

#### Model 3: VERITAC-2 (NCT05654623) — Overall survival (ESR1m, then ITT) (Key secondary (IA1 at PFS analysis))

- Model type: Stratified Cox; RPSFT-adjusted Cox (crossover to SERD) with bootstrap CI as supplementary
- Stratification: ESR1 status and visceral disease (IRT) per Applicant table
- Covariates: Treatment; supplementary multivariate model with CRF strata + baseline covariates
- Ties: Exact
- CI/test: Unadjusted 95% CI plus repeated CIs (Jennison-Turnbull) for group-sequential design; IA1 alpha 0.0002 two-sided
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Schoenfeld residual test / RMST supplementary; Wilcoxon/RPSFT for subsequent therapy
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: ESR1m 194 deaths, 80% power for HR<0.667; ITT 396 deaths, HR<0.75; one-sided 0.025
- Software: Not stated
- Result: IA1 ESR1m: stratified HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.574-1.900), p=0.89 (2-sided), deaths 22/136 vs 21/134; ITT HR 1.32 (0.846-2.050); ESR1m-nd HR 1.74 (0.894-3.384). Unplanned update (DCO 12-Jan-2026, ~50.5% IF) ESR1m HR 0.92 (0.62-1.36)
- FDA comments: Review team 'concerned with a potential OS detriment in the ESR1m population'; ITT and ESR1m-nd OS descriptive only; PMC for further OS.
- Spec source: SAP §5.2.1, §6.1.2; FDA MDR Table 24

Hazard ratio based on Cox proportional hazards model; under proportional hazards, hazard ratio < 1 indicates a reduction in hazard rate in favor of vepdegestrant compared to fulvestrant."
>

### gedatolisib (Revtorpyk) — NDA 219908

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Celcuity Inc. Approval year: 2026. Phase-3 trial(s): VIKTORIA-1 Study 1 (CELC-G-301, NCT05501886, PIK3CA wild-type cohort), Phase 3, open-label, 3-arm: A gedatolisib+palbociclib+fulvestrant, B gedatolisib+fulvestrant, C fulvestrant.

#### Model 1: VIKTORIA-1 Study 1 (NCT05501886) — BICR-assessed PFS (Arm A vs C; Arm B vs C) (Primary (two comparisons))

- Model type: Stratified Cox with a collapsed stratification factor entered as a covariate
- Stratification: Randomization factors (IRT): time to progression on immediate prior therapy (<=/>6 mo), visceral metastasis (lung/liver), geographic area (North America vs RoW). Collapsing rule: a factor with <5 events in a stratum is removed from strata and used as an independent covariate. As applied: stratified by visceral metastasis and geographic area
- Covariates: Treatment + time to progression on immediate prior therapy (collapsed factor)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: CIs for HR based on the score test; stratified log-rank test; one-sided alpha 0.025
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not extracted
- Interim/sample size: A vs C: 145 events, ~98% power for HR 0.5; B vs C: 155 events, ~75% power for HR 0.652 (one-sided 0.025)
- Software: SAS 9.4 or later
- Result: A vs C: HR 0.24 (95% CI 0.17-0.35), p<0.0001; B vs C: HR 0.33 (0.24-0.48), p<0.0001
- FDA comments: FDA noted the HR model included a stratification factor as a covariate due to the SAP collapsing rule; FDA prefers treatment as the only covariate, ran stratified Cox sensitivity analyses with treatment only — consistent.
- Spec source: SAP Final 4.0 §5.5.2.1, §5.5.3; FDA MDR §8.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "A stratification factor that causes sparsity, defined as less than 5 subjects reported with the event in one or more strata, will be removed from the stratified test in the order below to avoid a potential bias. In this case, a removed stratification factor will be utilized as an independent factor upon estimating the hazard ratio (HR) that measures the treatment effect between 2 randomized arms for PFS and OS."
>
> — VIKTORIA-1 SAP Final 4.0 (22-Jun-2025), in JCO 2026 Data Supplement 3, SAP Final 4.0 §5.5.2.1, PDF p. 342 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075786/ (supplement jco-44-1108-s003.pdf via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles))

> "The stratification factors used for randomization in the IRT system will be primary, and true stratification factors as recorded in the clinical database will be used as a sensitivity analysis if there is a mismatch with stratification factors."
>
> — VIKTORIA-1 SAP Final 4.0 (22-Jun-2025), in JCO 2026 Data Supplement 3, SAP Final 4.0 §5.5.2.1, PDF p. 342 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075786/ (supplement jco-44-1108-s003.pdf via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles))

> "The hazard ratio (HR) that measures the risk reduction by an experimental arm over the control will be estimated by a Cox regression model where the randomized treatment arm is an independent factor."
>
> — VIKTORIA-1 SAP Final 4.0 (22-Jun-2025), in JCO 2026 Data Supplement 3, SAP Final 4.0 §5.5.3, PDF p. 309 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075786/ (supplement jco-44-1108-s003.pdf via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles))

> "[2] Stratified Cox regression model, CIs for HR were based on the score test. [3] Stratified log-rank test."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 219908, Ref ID 5832496), FDA MDR Figure 8.1 footnotes, PDF p. 123 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219908Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "It was noted that the PFS and OS HRs were estimated by a Cox proportional hazards model with treatment and time to disease progression on immediate prior therapy as covariates and stratified by presence of visceral metastasis and geographic area. This was due to a collapsing rule for randomization stratification factors that was pre-specified in the SAP."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 219908, Ref ID 5832496), FDA MDR §8.1 (FDA assessment), PDF p. 200 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219908Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Since FDA generally recommends that the HR should be estimated from a Cox proportional hazards regression model with treatment as the only covariate, FDA conducted various sensitivity analyses where the PFS and OS HRs for both comparisons were estimated by stratified Cox regression models with treatment as the only covariate"
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 219908, Ref ID 5832496), FDA MDR §8.1 (FDA assessment), PDF p. 200 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/219908Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Statistical Analysis Software (SAS) version 9.4 or later will be used to analyze the data and create summary TFLs."
>
> — VIKTORIA-1 SAP Final 4.0 (22-Jun-2025), in JCO 2026 Data Supplement 3, SAP Final 4.0 §6, PDF p. 349 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13075786/ (supplement jco-44-1108-s003.pdf via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles))

#### Model 2: VIKTORIA-1 Study 1 (NCT05501886) — Overall survival (A vs C; B vs C) (Key secondary (interim at PFS analysis))

- Model type: Stratified Cox with collapsed factor as covariate (as PFS)
- Stratification: Visceral metastasis, geographic area
- Covariates: Treatment + time to progression on prior therapy
- Ties: Not stated

Median OS in months will be calculated and displayed with 95% confidence intervals per the Brookmeyer & Crowley method. The hazard ratio (HR) that measures the risk reduction by an experimental arm over the control will be estimated by a Cox regression model where the randomized treatment arm is an independent factor."

### daraxonrasib (Rasonque) — NDA 220910

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Revolution Medicines, Inc. Approval year: 2026. Phase-3 trial(s): RASolute 302 (NCT06625320), Phase 3, open-label, daraxonrasib vs investigator's choice chemotherapy, previously treated metastatic PDAC.

#### Model 1: RASolute 302 (NCT06625320) — Overall survival (RAS G12 population, then All-Patient) (Dual primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Randomization factors: ECOG PS (0/1), de novo metastatic disease (Y/N), liver metastases (Y/N), RAS mutation status (G12D/V vs other G12 vs non-G12); sparse strata pooling (zero-event strata collapsed into strata with smallest non-zero events, by population and endpoint; simplified in SAP v2)
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: 95% CI; stratified log-rank two-sided; graphical procedure, OS alpha 4.8% in RAS G12; Hwang-Shih-DeCani (gamma -0.4) spending over IA1/IA2/FA
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Withdrawal of consent censored (2 vs 13 in All-Patient); FDA tipping-point analysis
- Interim/sample size: ~314 deaths in RAS G12 for 84% power at HR 0.70 (two-sided 4.8%); IA1 at >=166 deaths, IA2 at 254
- Software: Not stated
- Result: RAS G12: HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.54), p<0.0001, deaths 72/228 vs 127/231. All-Patient: HR 0.40 (0.30-0.53), deaths 79/248 vs 141/252; unstratified HR 0.42 (0.32-0.55)
- FDA comments: FDA agreed with SAP description; FDA tipping-point analysis for 13 SOC patients censored for withdrawal — OS HR CI did not cross 1 even at 90% risk reduction.
- Spec source: FDA MDR §8.1 (SAP v1.0 23-Apr-2025, v2.0 17-Nov-2025; not public)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "PFS, OS, TTD in EORTC QLQ-PAN26 Pain Scale, and TTD in EORTC QLQ-C30 Global QoL Score were tested using log-rank tests stratified by the randomization stratification factors. Hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using the stratified Cox proportional hazards model."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 220910, Ref ID 5858563), FDA MDR §8.1 FDA's Assessment of SAP, PDF p. 108 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "In all the stratified analyses for time-to-event endpoints, overly sparse strata were pooled in the following way: All strata with zero events were collapsed into strata containing the smallest number of non-zero events."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 220910, Ref ID 5858563), FDA MDR §8.1, PDF p. 108 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "b The hazard ratio and its 95% CI were based on the stratified cox model with Efron’s method of tie handling. c The p-value was calculated using stratified log-rank test."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (NDA 220910, Ref ID 5858563), FDA MDR Table 21 footnotes, PDF p. 124 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/220910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 2: RASolute 302 (NCT06625320) — BICR-assessed PFS (RAS G12, All-Patient) (Dual primary)

## Cardiovascular / Metabolic

### Empagliflozin (Jardiance) — NDA 204629/S-008

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Boehringer Ingelheim / Eli Lilly. Approval year: 2016. Phase-3 trial(s): EMPA-REG OUTCOME (NCT01131676, Phase III).

#### Model 1: EMPA-REG OUTCOME (NCT01131676) — Time to first 3-point MACE (primary (non-inferiority then superiority))

- Model type: standard Cox (covariate-adjusted, unstratified)
- Stratification: None in model (randomization stratified by HbA1c, BMI, region, renal function via IXRS; these enter as covariates)
- Covariates: treatment (pooled empagliflozin 10+25 mg vs placebo), age, sex, geographic region (5), baseline BMI (<30 vs >=30), HbA1c (<8.5 vs >=8.5%), eGFR category
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95.02% CI (one-sided alpha 0.0249 after Haybittle-Peto 0.0001 adjustment); NI margin 1.3; CI/test type (Wald etc.) not stated
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Treated set; all events to trial termination; no-event patients censored at individual day of trial completion; non-CV deaths censored
- Interim/sample size: Primary analysis after 691 3-point MACE events; one interim analysis (supporting the original glycemic NDA) costing 0.0001 alpha (Haybittle-Peto); 4-step fixed hierarchy
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 490/4687 (10.5%) pooled empagliflozin vs 282/2333 (12.1%) placebo; HR 0.86 (95.02% CI 0.74, 0.99); two-sided p=0.0382 (superiority); NI p<0.0001
- FDA comments: FDA statistician (Clark) confirmed results; ran MI sensitivity analyses for 211 subjects with missing follow-up, before/after-interim subgroup HRs, and 3-point MACE + non-CV death. Division Director called censoring non-CV deaths an assumption 'not anchored in or compatible with reality' but found the bias favored placebo.
- Spec source: FDA Division Director, Clinical and Statistical reviews (SAP itself not public); ClinicalTrials.gov results

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "For the analyses, the applicant had pre-specified that the 10 mg and 25 mg empagliflozin treatment arms would be combined into a single group. A cox proportional hazards model with factors for treatment (pooled empagliflozin vs. placebo), age, sex, geographical region (North America [including Australia and New Zealand], Latin America, Europe, Africa, and Asia), baseline values for BMI (less than vs. greater than or equal to 30), HbA1c (less than vs. greater than or equal to 8.5%), and eGFR (normal: eGFR ≥ 90 ml/min, mild impairment: 60 ml/min ≤ eGFR ≤ 89 ml/min, and moderate impairment: 30 ml/min ≤ eGFR ≤ 59 ml/min) was used to test for non-inferiority of the primary and secondary endpoints against a margin of 1.3 using a 1 sided alpha of 0.0249 (corresponding to 95.02% confidence intervals). The alpha had been adjusted by 0.0001 based on a Haybittle-Peto method to account for a single interim analysis to preserve the overall alpha-level level at 0.025."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 204629/S-008, Division Director Review, PDF p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf)

> "The final protocol specified that the primary analysis would be based on this treated set of patients after 691 3-point MACE events had occurred. The two empagliflozin treatment arms were pooled together in the treatment variable to test against placebo. The primary analysis used a Cox proportional hazards model which included factors for treatment, age, sex, baseline BMI≥30, Baseline HbA1c≥8.5%, baseline eGFR, and geographic region."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 204629/S-008, Statistical Review (J. Clark), PDF p. 288 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf)

> "These hypotheses were tested for the primary endpoint based on the treated set (TS), including all randomized patients who received at least one dose of study medication. Following the intent-to-treat principle, all events observed until trial termination were included in the analysis. Patients who did not experience a primary endpoint event were censored at the individual day of trial completion."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 204629/S-008, Clinical Review, PDF p. 135 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf)

> "Patients who died from a non-cardiovascular cause (non-CVD) in the trial and did not experience a 3-Point MACE event prior to dying were censored (N= 135). For the purpose of the primary analysis these patients were considered to still be [...] and had a time to event imputed based on the assumption that they would have the same time to a 3-Point MACE event as those who were censored alive."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 204629/S-008, Division Director Review, PDF p. 65 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf)

> "In essence, for the purpose of the primary analysis, these patients were still considered to be alive! This assumption is necessary for the statistical method but is obviously not anchored in or compatible with reality."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 204629/S-008, Division Director Review, footnote 18, PDF p. 65 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf)

> "Cox proportional hazards model with factors for treatment, age, gender, categorised BMI, HbA1c, eGFR and geographical region."
>
> — ClinicalTrials.gov results record NCT01131676 (API v2, outcome-measure analyses), results section (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT01131676)

#### Model 2: EMPA-REG OUTCOME (NCT01131676) — Time to first 4-point MACE (3-point MACE + hospitalization for unstable angina) (key secondary (NI then superiority))

- Model type: standard Cox (covariate-adjusted)
- Stratification: None in model
- Covariates: Same as primary (treatment, age, sex, region, BMI, HbA1c, eGFR categories)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95.02% CI; NI margin 1.3; one-sided alpha 0.0249
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: As primary
- Interim/sample size: Step 2 (NI) and step 4 (superiority) of fixed hierarchy
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 599/4687 (12.8%) vs 333/2333 (14.3%); HR 0.89 (95.02% CI 0.78, 1.01); p=0.0795 — NI shown, superiority not shown
- FDA comments: Confirmed by FDA statistical reviewer
- Spec source: FDA reviews; ClinicalTrials.gov

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The hazard ratio (HR) based on Cox regression for all empagliflozin vs. placebo was 0.89 (95.02% CI 0.78, 1.01). Therefore, empagliflozin was found to be non-inferior to placebo, but not superior since the upper bound of the 95.02% CI was above 1."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 204629/S-008, Clinical Review, PDF p. 163 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf)

#### Model 3: EMPA-REG OUTCOME (NCT01131676) — 3-point MACE + all-cause death; 3-point MACE with imputed missing follow-up; before/after interim cohorts (FDA reviewer sensitivity analyses)

- Model type: standard Cox (same model as primary), applied to modified endpoint / multiply imputed data
- Stratification: None in model
- Covariates: Same as primary
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Non-CV deaths counted as events instead of censored; MI of event times for 211 prematurely discontinued subjects (2000 imputations) using off-treatment hazard rates
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 3-point MACE + non-CV death: 574 vs 333 events, HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.74, 0.97) vs primary 0.86 (0.74, 0.99); CV death HR 0.62 (0.49, 0.78); all-cause death HR 0.68 (0.57, 0.82); HRs similar before/after interim analysis
- FDA comments: Reviewer concluded bias from censoring non-CV deaths was minimal and favored placebo; missing data unlikely to change conclusions
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review (J. Clark)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "For this review, I ran sensitivity analyses imputing time until event for those who were missing follow-up time in the study. Hazard rates for the imputations with the main sensitivity analysis were based on event rates calculated during the off treatment period for those who stopped study drug but continued to be followed in the study."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 204629/S-008, Statistical Review §3.2.2, PDF p. 292 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf)

> "I ran an analysis which incorporated all-cause death into the 3-point MACE endpoint in order to assess how much censoring non-CV deaths under the assumption that they would have the same time to MACE event after death as those who were censored alive would affect the primary analysis results."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 204629/S-008, Statistical Review §3.3.5, PDF p. 302 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf)

> "The hazard ratios based on the primary Cox model yield similar results for before and after the IA."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 204629/S-008, Statistical Review, PDF p. 301 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/204629Orig1s008.pdf)

### Dapagliflozin (Farxiga) — NDA 202293/S-018

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: AstraZeneca (with TIMI Study Group). Approval year: 2019. Phase-3 trial(s): DECLARE-TIMI 58 (NCT01730534, Phase IIIb).

#### Model 1: DECLARE-TIMI 58 (NCT01730534) — Time to first 3-point MACE (dual primary (NI margin 1.3, then superiority))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: baseline hematuria; baseline CV risk category (established CV disease vs multiple risk factors) — randomization strata; source (IxRS vs CRF) not stated for model (baseline table labels CV risk 'IRVS')
- Covariates: treatment only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Wald (two-sided p for superiority per FDA table footnote); 95% CI; closed testing with one-sided alpha 0.0231 for NI, split 0.01155 for superiority
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Incomplete follow-up censored at last clinical assessment; FDA-requested MI sensitivity analysis imputing events to 21-May-2018 (exponential/piecewise exponential hazards)
- Interim/sample size: 1390 MACE events for 85% power at HR 0.85 (one-sided 0.025); 1559 accrued; 2 IAs at 1/3 and 2/3 (O'Brien-Fleming; 0.000095, 0.00614), leaving 0.023095
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 756/8582 (8.8%) vs 803/8578 (9.4%); HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.84, 1.03); superiority p=0.1723; NI p=0.0003
- FDA comments: Reviewer noted non-informative censoring assumption and requested MI sensitivity analyses; reviewer re-analysis counting 156 undetermined deaths as CV deaths gave HR 0.93 (0.85, 1.02). Endpoint hierarchy revised mid-trial (confirmed before first IA).
- Spec source: FDA Clinical Review and Statistical Review; ClinicalTrials.gov

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The study was event-driven, with 1390 MACE events required to have 85% power to demonstrate superiority of dapagliflozin to placebo with a HR of 0.85. The study ultimately accumulated 1559 MACE events. The Cox proportional hazards model was used to analyze the time-to-event variables and was stratified by baseline hematuria and baseline CV risk category."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 202293/S-018, Clinical Review, PDF p. 126 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/202293Orig1s018.pdf)

> "Applicant’s analysis method: Cox proportional hazards model was used to analyze the time-to-event variables. The model was stratified by baseline hematuria and baseline CV risk, with treatment as a model term."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 202293/S-018, Statistical Review §3.2.2, PDF p. 264 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/202293Orig1s018.pdf)

> "Reviewer’s Comments: The applicant used a Cox proportional hazard model to estimate the effect of dapagliflozin on time-to-event endpoints compared with placebo. Dropouts were censored at the time of dropout—this relies on an assumption that dropouts have the same event hazard as those patients who remained in follow-up (“non-informative censoring”) on the same treatment arm."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 202293/S-018, Statistical Review §3.2.2, PDF p. 266 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/202293Orig1s018.pdf)

> "P value (two-sided) is based on the Wald statistic for superiority of Hazard Ratio. P-value for testing non-inferiority of dapagliflozin vs. placebo on MACE is 0.0003, where the non-inferiority margin is 1.3."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 202293/S-018, Statistical Review Table 5 footnote, PDF p. 270 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/202293Orig1s018.pdf)

> "I additionally performed an analysis for MACE, where undetermined deaths were handled as CV deaths. The applicant’s MACE results were similar to the results when included those events as CV deaths."
>
> — FDA combined review package, NDA 202293/S-018, Statistical Review §3.2.4.1, PDF p. 270 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/202293Orig1s018.pdf)

#### Model 2: DECLARE-TIMI 58 (NCT01730534) — Time to first HHF or CV death (dual primary (superiority; alpha recycled))

- Model type: stratified Cox (HR) with stratified log-rank test for p-value
- Stratification: baseline CV risk group; hematuria
- Covariates: treatment only

- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated

- Result: 417 (4.7%) vs 496 (5.8%) [percentages as printed in FDA table]; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.73, 0.95); stratified log-rank p=0.0052. HHF component HR 0.73 (0.61, 0.88); CV death 0.98 (0.82, 1.17)
- FDA comments: Reviewer noted effect driven mainly by HHF component; review text gives dapagliflozin rate as '417(1.7%)' (table shows 4.7%)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review Table 6

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Hazard ratios and CIs are calculated from Cox proportional hazards model (Wald test) stratified by baseline CV risk group and haematuria with treatment as a model term. *Nominal P-value is calculated based on a stratified log-rank test."

### Semaglutide (Wegovy) — NDA 215256/S-011

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Novo Nordisk. Approval year: 2024. Phase-3 trial(s): SELECT (EX9536-4388, NCT03574597, Phase 3 per ClinicalTrials.gov).

Note: the SAP's native text layer is garbled (character-spaced); quotes below come from a tesseract OCR of the PDF page images (file sema_sap_ocr.txt) and are labelled OCR. They are cleaner than the README's manual reconstruction but may contain OCR artifacts.

#### Model 1: SELECT (NCT03574597) — Time to first 3-point MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke) (primary (superiority; ITT estimand))

- Model type: standard Cox (cause-specific in substance; 'cause-specific' wording removed in SAP v2 to clarify a standard Cox model)
- Stratification: None
- Covariates: treatment group as the only fixed factor
- Ties: exact method
- CI/test: Score test (one-sided fixed-design p-value) for hypothesis test; two-sided 95% CI based on profile likelihood; final inference adjusted via likelihood-ratio ordering
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: 'investigated by residuals' (type not specified) / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: In-trial period; no-event subjects censored at end of in-trial observation; non-CV death (competing risk) treated as censoring; undetermined deaths presumed CV
- Interim/sample size: 1,225 events for 90% power at design HR 0.83 (one-sided 2.5%); one IA at 817 events (2/3) for superiority, Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming-type spending (nominal 0.01832 interim / 0.01329 final); score test p-value at IA
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.72, 0.89); p<0.0001 (ClinicalTrials.gov); events per arm not in extracted sources
- FDA comments: No FDA review consulted (not in README documents)
- Spec source: SAP v3.0 §2.1, §2.2.4, §2.3.1 (OCR); ClinicalTrials.gov

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Unless otherwise specified, the statistical analyses of TTE endpoints are done by using a Cox proportional hazards model with treatment group (semaglutide 2.4 mg, semaglutide placebo) as fixed factor under the assumption of independent censoring. The population-level summary measure for TTE endpoints is the HR for semaglutide 2.4 mg versus semaglutide placebo. The assumption of proportional hazards is investigated by residuals. Tied event times are handled using the exact method and confidence intervals are based on the profile likelihood."

> — SELECT SAP EX9536-4388 v3.0 (OCR via tesseract of PDF page images; native text layer garbled), §2.2.4 (OCR), PDF p. 14 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT03574597/SAP_003.pdf)

The score test from the Cox model is used for testing."

### Rivaroxaban (Xarelto) — NDA 22406

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: J&J PRD. Approval year: 2011. Phase-3 trial(s): RECORD1 (NCT00329628), RECORD2 (NCT00332020), RECORD3 (NCT00361894), RECORD4 (NCT00362232) — all Phase III.

The primary efficacy analysis (total VTE) used risk-difference methods, not Cox. Cox/PH models appear only in the pooled bleeding analyses (sponsor time-to-first-event Cox; FDA Andersen-Gill). Hazard ratios for 'symptomatic VTE or death' (FDA Table 1, sponsor Table 37) are reported without the estimation method being stated, so they are not counted here. The bundled liver-safety review's Cox models concern ROCKET/EINSTEIN data (other indications) and are not counted.

#### Model 1: RECORD1-4 pooled (NCT00329628, NCT00332020, NCT00361894, NCT00362232) — Time to first bleeding event (major; major + surgical site; major or non-major clinically relevant; any) (safety (sponsor analysis, reproduced by FDA))

- Model type: standard Cox (time to first event)
- Stratification: Not stated
- Covariates: Not stated
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; p-values
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Analyzed over 3 windows: total duration, until day 12±2, active-control phase
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Total duration: major bleeding 24/6183 vs 13/6200, HR 1.8 (0.9, 3.6), p=0.076; major + surgical site 111 vs 85, HR 1.3 (1.0, 1.7), p=0.06; major or NMCR 197 vs 158, HR 1.3 (1, 1.5), p=0.039; any 434 vs 401, HR 1.1 (0.9, 1.2), p=0.3
- FDA comments: FDA judged time-to-first-event Cox inappropriate for recurrent bleeding and used Andersen-Gill instead (Model 2)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §1.3, §3.2

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The hazard ratios are all > 1 by using Cox Proportional Hazard model, and p-values for major bleeding combined with surgical site bleeding event are 0.08 and 0.06 (statistically significant at 10% level) for time to first event and time to multiple events, respectively (Table 30)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 22406, §3.2 Evaluation of Safety, PDF p. 81 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022406Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: RECORD1-4 pooled — Multiple (recurrent) bleeding events (FDA reviewer reanalysis (safety))

- Model type: Andersen-Gill (counting-process PH model for recurrent events)
- Stratification: Not stated
- Covariates: Not stated
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: p-values for 'time to multiple events'
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Total duration p-values (multiple events): major 0.05; major + surgical site 0.05; major or NMCR 0.02; any 0.3
- FDA comments: Reviewer concluded rivaroxaban increases bleeding vs enoxaparin; also criticized lack of Type I error control for secondary endpoints and comparator regimens in RECORD2/3
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §1.3

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Sponsor used Cox model for time to first event for bleeding analyses, although bleeding events are time dependent with multiple observations per subject and it is more appropriate to use time-to-event data in the multiple event setting. In this review, the Andersen-Gill (AG) formulation of the proportional hazards model as a counting process is used for the assessment of benefit in terms of bleeding."

> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 22406, §1.3 Statistical Issues and Findings, PDF p. 57 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022406Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Ticagrelor (Brilinta) — NDA 22433

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: AstraZeneca. Approval year: 2011. Phase-3 trial(s): PLATO (NCT00391872, Phase III).

#### Model 1: PLATO (NCT00391872) — Time to first CV death/MI (excl. silent MI)/stroke (primary)

- Model type: standard Cox (unstratified)
- Stratification: None
- Covariates: treatment group only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; final critical p=0.0497 (two-sided)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Early discontinuers without consent withdrawal censored at a projected date 30 days after the expected End-of-Treatment visit; FDA sensitivity censored at last real visit
- Interim/sample size: Target 1780 events; one IA at ~1200 events (2/3) with Peto-Haybittle p=0.001
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 864/9333 (9.3%) vs 1014/9291 (10.9%); HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.77, 0.92); p=0.0003. FDA sensitivity (last real visit censoring) HR 0.86 (0.78, 0.94); US HR 1.27 (0.92, 1.75)
- FDA comments: Major issue: qualitative treatment-by-region (US vs non-US) interaction; projected censoring dates questioned; Marciniak disputed AdComm claim of stratification by intended management
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.1.1.5–3.1.1.7

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary analysis compared the time from randomization to the first occurrence of any event in the composite endpoint using the Cox proportional hazards model with a factor for treatment group. All efficacy variables were analyzed using the full analysis set."

> "One interim analysis of the primary composite efficacy endpoint was performed when approximately 1200 adjudicated events (2/3rds of the total target number of 1780 events) were observed. The Peto-Haybittle group sequential boundary was used with a critical p-value of 0.001. The critical p-value at the final analysis was 0.0497."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 22433, §3.1.1.5, PDF p. 63 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022433Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Subject who discontinued the study early but did not withdraw consent was censored 30 days after the date when the End of Treatment visit should have occurred. In other words, the censoring dates of those subjects were projected."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 22433, §3.1.1.7, PDF p. 65 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022433Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In the sensitivity analysis, subjects no longer have the projected censor dates. Subjects who did not have a primary event were censored at the last real visit. HR estimate came out to be 0.86 with 95% CI (0.78, 0.94) in overall population in the sensitivity analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 22433, §3.1.1.7, PDF p. 66 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022433Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: PLATO (NCT00391872) — Primary composite (FDA reviewer exploratory (aspirin-dose and region interaction, post-CRL))

- Model type: standard Cox with interaction terms
- Stratification: None
- Covariates: treatment (T), region (R), ASA dose (A), T×A, T×R (also T+R+A+TR, T+R+A+TR+AR+AT+ATR); 13 ASA definitions × 6 imputations
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Interaction p<0.05 defined as significant
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Analyses restricted to first 30 days vs later events (US HR 1.06 early vs 1.53 later)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated

- Software: Not stated

- FDA comments: Reviewers found the ASA explanatory Cox model non-robust (high leverage of few high-dose non-US subjects; sensitive to inclusion of day-1 loading dose)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Reviews (2010, 2011)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "A total of 13 different ASA definitions and 6 imputations were proposed and analyses were performed in a number of Cox proportional hazards models under these scenarios."

> "These few subjects indeed had a large leverage on the robustness of the Cox model, as it is well known that the model fitting with covariate (i.e., dose in this case) is very sensitive to the disposition of a few events in the both ends of dose range fitted."

> "the Cox proportional hazards model did not appear robust enough due to the small number of subjects taking high dose ASA in the non-US region. The Cox proportional hazards model appeared quite sensitive to the high ASA subjects in non-US region."

#### Model 1: ARISTOTLE (NCT00412984) — Time to first stroke or systemic embolism (primary (NI margin 1.38, then superiority))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: prior warfarin/VKA status (experienced/naive) and investigative site pooled to geographic region (randomization was stratified by site and prior VKA status via IVRS)
- Covariates: treatment group
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI for NI (margin 1.38; one-sided 0.025); two-sided superiority p
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA reviewer log(-log(S(t))) vs log(t) plot: 'reasonable fit'; estimated hazard functions over time / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: ITT; Not otherwise stated for efficacy
- Interim/sample size: Target 448 primary events; 1 IA at 50% (224) with superiority stop if one-sided p<0.0001; sample size increased 15,000→18,000 (amendment 7)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 212/9120 vs 265/9081; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66, 0.95); NI p=0.0001; superiority p=0.0114
- FDA comments: FDA confirmed; sensitivity Cox with baseline covariates; medication-error sensitivity analyses questioned (Model 4)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.1.1; Medical Review; ClinicalTrials.gov

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The statistical analysis plan (SAP) was finalized on May 11, 2010. The calculation of p-values and construction of point estimates and CIs for RR will be based on Cox proportional hazard models. Site and prior Warfarin/VKA status will be included in the model as stratification factors."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202155, §3.1.1 Time to Event Analyses, PDF p. 11 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "With a target 448 primary efficacy events, the large number of strata in either approach produces very sparse data and, therefore, the baseline hazard within each stratum would be poorly estimated with such models. For this reason, when using a Cox proportional hazards model stratified by prior warfarin/VKA status and investigative site, site will be pooled to the Geographic Region level."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202155, §3.1.1 Rule for Combining Sites, PDF p. 11 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Validation of the Proportional Hazard Assumption: The basic Cox Model assumes that the hazard functions for two different levels of a covariate are proportional for all values of time, t. [...] assumption is through the plot of log(-log(S(t))) vs. log(t). However, the interpretation of the plot is subjective. In general, we can conclude PH unless a distinct pattern of non-parallelism (e.g. crossing) is seen. Hence, Figure 2 shows reasonable fit to the PH assumption."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202155, §3.1.1.3 Reviewer’s Results, PDF p. 14 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "This was calculated using a Cox proportional hazards model with treatment arm as a covariate, with stratification by investigative site (pooled at the geographic region level) and prior VKA status (experienced or naïve). A sensitivity Cox model analysis was performed that was stratified by investigative site and prior VKA status, with covariates of treatment arm, history of stroke, TIA or non-systemic embolus, history of DM, treatment for hypertension, history of MI, and history of “coronary heart failure.”"
>
> — FDA Medical Review, NDA 202155, Clinical Review, PDF p. 223 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000MedR.pdf)

> "Model included treatment group as a covariate; stratified by investigative site and prior warfarin/vitamin K antagonist status. (experienced, naïve)."
>
> — ClinicalTrials.gov results record NCT00412984 (API v2, outcome-measure analyses), results section (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT00412984)

#### Model 2: ARISTOTLE (NCT00412984) — Time to first ISTH major bleeding (key secondary / primary safety (superiority in hierarchy))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: region; prior VKA status
- Covariates: treatment group
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; two-sided p
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at earliest of 2 days after study drug discontinuation, death, or last full-assessment contact (withdrawal/LTFU)
- Interim/sample size: Tested after primary NI and superiority
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 327/9088 vs 462/9052; HR 0.69 (SE 0.07); p<0.0001
- FDA comments: Not stated
- Spec source: FDA Medical Review; Statistical Review Table 10

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Subjects who did not experience a bleeding endpoint were censored at the earlier of: 2 days after study drug discontinuation, death date, or last contact date when a full assessment was performed (for subjects who withdrew consent to be followed up or were lost to follow-up) at the end of the study. Superiority testing for the primary safety endpoint (ISTH major bleeding) was performed using a Cox proportional hazards model including treatment group as a covariate and stratified by region and prior VKA status."
>
> — FDA Medical Review, NDA 202155, Safety review, PDF p. 316 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000MedR.pdf)

#### Model 3: ARISTOTLE (NCT00412984) — All-cause death (key secondary (third in hierarchy))

- Model type: stratified Cox (pre-specified model)
- Stratification: investigative site and prior VKA status (ClinicalTrials.gov)
- Covariates: treatment group
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; two-sided p
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 603/9120 vs 669/9081; HR 0.89; p=0.0465
- FDA comments: Marciniak argued the mortality benefit was fragile given missing vital status (one additional apixaban death removes significance); addendum reviewers disagreed
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review; ClinicalTrials.gov

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Based on the pre-specified Cox proportional hazard model, Apixaban was superior to warfarin for reduction of all-cause death (HR=0.89, p-value=0.0465), see Table 11."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202155, Analysis of All-cause Death, PDF p. 19 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 4: ARISTOTLE (NCT00412984) — Stroke/SE, ISTH major bleeding, all-cause death (sensitivity (sponsor medication-error censoring; FDA tipping-point/fragility imputation))

- Model type: stratified Cox (same as primary) on modified data
- Stratification: As primary
- Covariates: treatment
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Sponsor: events after first incorrect medication excluded, subjects censored at that time; FDA: events sequentially imputed to apixaban subjects (ordered by censor date) until significance lost
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Sponsor: stroke/SE HR 0.78 (0.65, 0.94); ISTH major bleeding 0.68 (0.59, 0.79); all-cause death 0.88 (0.79, 0.98)
- FDA comments: Statistical reviewer: censoring after medication errors assumes those events are unrelated to assigned treatment; robustness conclusion 'may still be problematic'
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §1.4; Medical Review addendum

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "the sensitivity analyses as proposed by censoring the events that occurred after a medication error automatically assume that such events are not associated with the treatment assigned to."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202155, §1.4 Medication Errors, PDF p. 7 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "For example, to determine the number of apixaban-treated subjects needed to negate the statistically significant mortality finding, subjects are ordered by apixaban treatment, then censor date. Events are sequentially imputed to apixaban-treated subjects without events until the results are not statistically significant. Because the cox proportional hazards model is dependent on time, this analysis is highly conservative since the additional events are occurring early in the trial."
>
> — FDA Medical Review, NDA 202155, Clinical Review Addendum, footnote 1, PDF p. 4 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202155Orig1s000MedR.pdf)

### Alogliptin (Nesina) — NDA 022271

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Takeda. Approval year: 2013. Phase-3 trial(s): Study 010 (NCT00286455; glycemic, no Cox); EXAMINE (SYR-322_402, NCT00968708, Phase 3 per ClinicalTrials.gov).

The only FDA review posted for this NDA (Summary Review) mentions the EXAMINE interim CV analysis that supported approval but contains no model specification. The model below is documented only from the ClinicalTrials.gov results record for the final EXAMINE analysis (post-approval).

#### Model 1: EXAMINE (NCT00968708) — Time to first adjudicated 3-point MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke) (primary (CV safety NI margin 1.3, then superiority))

- Model type: Cox (two analyses posted: unstratified as listed, and stratified)
- Stratification: Second posted analysis: endpoint renal function (last observed post-baseline category) and geographic region
- Covariates: treatment
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: One-sided 97.5% repeated CIs from group-sequential stopping boundary (overall false-rejection rate 2.5%)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: Group-sequential design; superiority could be concluded after 550 MACE events if upper bound <1.0; interim analysis submitted in first NDA resubmission ruled out HR 1.8
- Software: Not stated
- Result: MACE 11.3% alogliptin (N=2701) vs 11.8% placebo (N=2679); HR 0.962 (upper one-sided 97.5% bound 1.160), p=0.315; stratified HR 0.965 (upper 1.169), p=0.332
- FDA comments: Summary Review: interim results excluded an 80% excess CV risk; trial continued as FDAAA-required postmarketing trial for the 1.3 margin. No Cox-specific comments.
- Spec source: ClinicalTrials.gov results record only

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Statistical analyses of the primary MACE composite endpoint was based on sequences of 1-sided repeated confidence intervals (CIs) to assess non-inferiority or statistical superiority with respect to the null hypotheses. Each sequence of repeated CIs was constructed using critical values from a 1-sided stopping boundary for a group sequential design (GSD), to preserve an overall false-rejection rate of 2.5%."
>
> — ClinicalTrials.gov results record NCT00968708 (API v2, outcome-measure analyses), results section (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT00968708)

> "Stratified by endpoint renal function (defined as the last observed postbaseline renal function (normal renal function/mild renal impairment vs moderate/severe renal impairment including end-stage renal disease)) and geographic region."
>
> — ClinicalTrials.gov results record NCT00968708 (API v2, outcome-measure analyses), results section (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT00968708)

> "Takeda has provided sufficient evidence from the interim analysis that alogliptin is not associated with an 80% or higher excess CV risk over standard-of-care therapies for T2DM."
>
> — FDA Summary Review, NDA 022271, §2.2, PDF p. 3 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/022271Orig1s000SumR.pdf)
