### Canagliflozin (Invokana) — NDA 204042

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Janssen. Approval year: 2013. Phase-3 trial(s): 9 Phase 2/3 trials incl. CANVAS (DIA3008, NCT01032629, Phase 3, ongoing at approval). Glycemic trials (DIA3005 etc.) used ANCOVA/MMRM, not Cox.

Flag: Model 1 is a pooled meta-analysis of Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials (dominated by the Phase 3 CVOT CANVAS), included because it is the pre-specified CV-safety basis for approval.

#### Model 1: Premarket CV meta-analysis of 9 Phase 2/3 trials incl. CANVAS (NCT01032629) — Time to first MACE-plus (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, hospitalized unstable angina) (primary CV-safety analysis (HR margin 1.8; simultaneous 1.3 test at two-sided alpha 0.001))

- Model type: stratified Cox
- Stratification: 2 strata: CANVAS vs non-CANVAS trials
- Covariates: treatment (canagliflozin 100/300 mg pooled vs all comparators)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI vs margin 1.8; 99.9% CI vs margin 1.3
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA: scaled Schoenfeld residual plot with loess (possible early non-PH); treatment-by-time interaction test p=0.76 / FDA secondary analyses split CANVAS at day 30 (piecewise-type); KM plots
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: SAP (13-Jul-2010, IND 76479) plans further analyses at 500 and 700 MACE-plus to rule out 1.3
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 130/6396 vs 71/3327; HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.68, 1.21); 99.9% CI (0.56, 1.48) — 1.8 excluded, 1.3 not excluded. Non-CANVAS trials: HR 0.64 (0.34, 1.19)
- FDA comments: Reviewer: deviations from PH 'complicate the interpretability' of the Cox model; linear time-interaction test may not detect early-imbalance pattern
- Spec source: FDA CV-safety Statistical Review §1.1, §3.1.3, §3.1.6

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The agreed upon primary meta-analysis compares the hazard ratio of MACE-plus in subjects randomized to canagliflozin 100 mg or 300 mg once daily versus subjects randomized to all comparators using a Cox proportional hazards model with two strata: CANVAS and non-CANVAS. The meta-analysis includes the 9 Phase 2 and Phase 3 clinical trials described earlier."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (CV safety, Andraca-Carrera), NDA 204042, §3.1.3, PDF p. 213 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "A test to rule out a hazard ratio of MACE-plus larger than 1.3 with a two-sided α=0.001 was planned to be conducted at the same time as the pre-specified meta-analysis assessment of the HR risk margin of 1.8. The estimated 99.9% confidence interval for the hazard ratio of MACE-plus based on the primary Cox model was (0.56, 1.48), and therefore the upper bound of the 99.9% confidence interval did not rule out a hazard ratio of 1.3 at this time as pre-specified."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (CV safety, Andraca-Carrera), NDA 204042, §1.1, PDF p. 202 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Figure 12 in the Appendix shows the plot of the scaled Schoenfeld residuals corresponding to the primary Cox model discussed above. A plot of the scaled Schoenfeld residuals as a function of time was created to evaluate the assumption of proportional hazards. In this type of plot, a non-zero slope indicates a potential violation of the proportionality assumption. The loess curve corresponding to these residuals shows possible evidence of non-proportional hazards with a steep slope during the early part of the trials."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (CV safety, Andraca-Carrera), NDA 204042, §3.1.6.2, PDF p. 225 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "These deviations from the assumption of proportional hazards complicate the interpretability of the Cox proportional hazards model. A second approach to test whether hazards are proportional in a Cox model is to include an interaction term of treatment by time in the model. This test for interaction was not significant in these data (p-value = 0.76) and shows no evidence of non-proportional hazards."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (CV safety, Andraca-Carrera), NDA 204042, §3.1.6.2, PDF p. 225 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: CANVAS (DIA3008, NCT01032629) — MACE-plus in CANVAS alone: full period, first 30 days, after day 30 (pre-specified secondary + FDA reviewer analyses)

- Model type: standard Cox; time-dependent (treatment × time interaction) Cox for after-day-30 data
- Stratification: None (single trial)
- Covariates: treatment; treatment × time (FDA)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA: scaled Schoenfeld residuals (full CANVAS and after day 30) suggest non-PH; treatment×time interaction p=0.01 after day 30 / Split at day 30 (first 30 days vs later)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: CANVAS ongoing; data lock 31-Jan-2012
- Software: Not stated
- Result: First 30 days: 13/2886 vs 1/1441, HR 6.49 (0.85, 49.64); after day 30: 95/2867 vs 52/1435, HR 0.89 (0.64, 1.25); full CANVAS 108/2886 vs 53/1441 events. (Final CANVAS 3-point MACE per ClinicalTrials.gov: HR 0.88 [0.75, 1.03], Cox)
- FDA comments: Early imbalance of MACE-plus in CANVAS raised PH concerns; hazard function shape could not be modeled reliably with decreasing follow-up
- Spec source: FDA CV-safety Statistical Review §3.1.3.3, §3.1.6.4

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Figure 5 shows that the imbalance in early events suggests possibly non-proportional hazards in CANVAS. The scaled Schoenfeld residuals plot for the full duration of CANVAS is shown in Figure 14 in the Appendix."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (CV safety, Andraca-Carrera), NDA 204042, §3.1.6.4, PDF p. 228 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Figure 15 in the Appendix shows a plot of the scaled Schoenfeld residuals for the Cox proportional hazards model for MACE-plus after day 30 in CANVAS. The plot shows evidence of an increasing slope and therefore possibly non-proportional hazards in these data. We fit a Cox proportional hazards model with an interaction term of treatment by time to these data. The interaction term was statistically significant (p-value 0.01) and suggests that the hazard ratio of MACE-plus between canagliflozin and placebo may be changing through time after day 30 in CANVAS."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (CV safety, Andraca-Carrera), NDA 204042, §3.1.6.4, PDF p. 231 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

Sources consulted:

- ✔ FDA Statistical Reviews (bundle; CV-safety review by E. Andraca-Carrera) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf (text reused from earlier project file mm/b01/cana_statr.txt, re-downloaded)
- ✔ ClinicalTrials.gov CANVAS results (API v2) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT01032629 (final 2017 results, post-approval)

### Vorapaxar (Zontivity) — NDA 204886

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Merck. Approval year: 2014. Phase-3 trial(s): TRA 2P-TIMI 50 (P04737, NCT00526474, Phase III); TRACER (supportive Phase 3 ACS trial, reviewed in same Statistical Review).

#### Model 1: TRA 2P-TIMI 50 (NCT00526474) — Time to first CV death, MI, stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization (primary)

- Model type: standard Cox with stratification factors as covariates
- Stratification: Randomization strata (qualifying condition MI > CVD > PAD; planned thienopyridine use) entered as covariates, not as strata
- Covariates: treatment + stratification factors
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; nominal alpha 0.049 final (0.003 interim, O'Brien-Fleming)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA plotted HR over time (calendar and days since randomization): HR 'stable quickly' in overall/NSH populations / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: ~25,000 subjects for power to detect 15% RRR; one planned IA at ~50% events; FDA flagged 11 DSMB meetings, unplanned interim looks and unplanned sample-size re-estimation
- Software: Not stated (a sponsor SAS-program error affected an adjudication-status variable in TRACER)
- Result: 1259/13225 (9.5%) vs 1417/13224 (10.7%); HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.82, 0.95); p=0.001. Proposed label population (post-MI, no stroke/TIA): HR 0.82 (0.74, 0.90)
- FDA comments: Concerns about unplanned interim analyses, sample size increase and population change (stroke patients discontinued after DSMB ICH finding)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2, §3.2.4.4; ClinicalTrials.gov

Thus, the apparent significant treatment by body weight interactions are difficult to interpret."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 204886, Addendum memo, PDF p. 3 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/204886Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 4: TRACER (supportive ACS trial; NCT not in README) — Time to first CV death, MI, stroke, recurrent ischemia with rehospitalization (RIR) or urgent coronary revascularization (UCR) (primary (supportive trial))

- Model type: standard Cox with stratification factors as covariates
- Stratification: Stratification factors as covariates (not listed)
- Covariates: treatment + stratification factors
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; alpha 0.049 (one interim)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: One interim analysis
- Software: Not stated

- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review (TRACER section)

### Edoxaban tosylate (Savaysa) — NDA 206316

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Daiichi Sankyo. Approval year: 2015. Phase-3 trial(s): ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (DU176B-C-U301, NCT00781391, Phase 3); Hokusai-VTE (Phase III, DVT/PE indication, reviewed in the same combined Statistical Review).

#### Model 1: ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (NCT00781391) — Time to first stroke or systemic embolic event (mITT, on-treatment) (primary (NI margin 1.38; then superiority of high dose on ITT/overall period))

- Model type: Cox with counting-process (start-stop) at-risk intervals for on-treatment periods; stratification factors as covariates
- Stratification: Randomization strata (CHADS2 2-3 vs 4-6; dose-adjustment need) entered as dichotomized covariates
- Covariates: treatment; CHADS2 ≥4 (0/1); dose adjustment (eCrCL ≤50 mL/min, weight ≤60 kg, or verapamil/quinidine) (0/1)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided 97.5% CI per edoxaban arm vs warfarin (Bonferroni for 2 arms); superiority of high dose at two-sided alpha 0.01
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA: log(-log(survival)) plot; nonparametric 30-day hazard estimates with loess; parametric Weibull fits / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: On-treatment: subjects excluded from risk set during interruptions (on treatment through 3 days after last dose); off-treatment events not counted in primary analysis
- Interim/sample size: Event-driven; details not in extracted text
- Software: Not stated
- Result: On-treatment events: high dose 182, low dose 253, warfarin 232. High dose HR 0.79 (97.5% CI 0.632, 0.985), NI p<0.0001; low dose HR 1.07 (0.874, 1.314), NI p=0.0055 (ClinicalTrials.gov)
- FDA comments: Reviewer believed ITT (all events) should have been primary; ~1/4 of follow-up excluded by on-treatment approach; data quality 'fair'
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §1.4.2; ClinicalTrials.gov

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The analysis approach used the on-treatment period to count events. Subjects were excluded from the at risk set during periods of treatment interruptions. Subjects were considered on treatment for 3 [...] days after last dose and back on treatment if the treatment recommenced. The primary analysis used the counting process approach to include only subjects at risk in each time interval in the Cox proportional hazards regression model analysis. The Cox proportional hazards model included treatments and the following 2 stratification factors as covariates: 1. The dichotomized CHADS2 score (1 if CHADS2 ≥ 4; 0 otherwise) 2. The dichotomized dose adjustment variable (1 if eCrCL ≤ 50 mL/min, or body weight ≤ 60 kg, or taking verapamil or quinidine; 0 otherwise)"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206316, §1.4.2, PDF p. 23 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206316Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

> "Because there were two treatment arms being compared simultaneously to the active control group, a Bonferroni type approach was used to control the overall error rate. The two-sided 97.5% confidence interval (CI) for the hazard ratios (each edoxaban treatment group versus warfarin) was estimated using the proportional hazards model. If the upper limit of this CI of the hazard ratio was below 1.38, then non-inferiority to warfarin was considered established for the corresponding edoxaban treatment group."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206316, §1.4.2, PDF p. 24 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206316Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

> "For the test of superiority, the ITT analysis and overall study period would be used (i.e. all events would be counted, not just the on-treatment events)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206316, §1.4.2, PDF p. 24 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206316Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

> "The analysis was complicated because the sponsor used an on-treatment approach. In my opinion, the intention to treat analysis should be used for the primary analysis, even in an active control, non-inferiority trial."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206316, §1.3, PDF p. 22 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206316Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

> "Two stratification factor covariates: 1) CHADS2 score 2) dose-adjustment factor. If upper limit of CI of HR was below 1.38, then non-inferiority to warfarin was established for group."
>
> — ClinicalTrials.gov results record NCT00781391 (API v2, outcome-measure analyses), results section (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT00781391)

#### Model 2: ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (NCT00781391) — Stroke/SEE (and CV death) as a function of renal function (eCrCL) and region (FDA reviewer subgroup / interaction reanalysis)

- Model type: Cox (primary model) extended with cubic spline of eCrCL and dose×eCrCL, region×dose×eCrCL interactions; martingale residuals for functional form
- Stratification: As primary (covariates)
- Covariates: primary model + cubic spline eCrCL (boundary knots 60, 100) + two-way interactions dose×eCrCL; region (6) and region interactions in regional model
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Gail-Simon likelihood-ratio test for qualitative interaction (and a NI-margin version)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Martingale residuals vs eCrCL (functional form) / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: As primary
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable
- Software: R (reviewer's simulation program in appendix)
- Result: High dose vs warfarin: HR 0.53 (50≤eCrCL<80) vs 1.41 (eCrCL≥80); qualitative interaction p=0.035 (superiority) vs 0.45 (NI-margin version)
- FDA comments: Reviewer argued the superiority-based qualitative-interaction test is the wrong test in an NI trial; simulated ~37% conditional chance of a spurious qualitative interaction
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §1.8 and Appendix

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "If we look at the treatment effect in those two subgroups (high dose vs. warfarin only) adjusting only for chads score variable and treatment, the estimated hazard ratios are 0.53 (50≤eCrCL<80 subgroup) and 1.41 (eCrCL≥80 subgroup)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206316, §1.8, PDF p. 37 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206316Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

> "In Figure 11 the estimated hazard ratios are shown as a function of eCrCL using splines (cubic splines with boundary knots at 60 and 100). For this figure, I started with the model used in the primary analysis and included the cubic spline function of eCrCL together with the two way interactions between dose and eCrCL."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206316, §1.8, PDF p. 37 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206316Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

> "To do this, I started with the proportional hazards model used in the primary analysis and added terms for eCrCL as a continuous variable, the 6 regions, and all the two-way interactions between region, dose and eCrCL."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206316, §1.8, PDF p. 39 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206316Orig1Orig2s000StatR.pdf)

x2=lam2/s2

mean((lamhat-log(1.38))/s<(-z025)) #90% power for noninferiority

#### Model 3: Hokusai-VTE (DVT/PE indication) — Time to symptomatic recurrent VTE or VTE-related death (primary (NI margin 1.5))

- Model type: standard Cox (unstratified)
- Stratification: None (randomization stratified by diagnosis, risk factors, dose-adjustment need)
- Covariates: treatment
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI; p from asymptotic normal test; secondary endpoints: unstratified log-rank test + unstratified Cox HR
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: 12-month study period; on-treatment PP sensitivity analyses
- Interim/sample size: ~220 events for 85% power, alpha 0.05, NI margin 1.5; 7500 subjects
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 130/4118 (3.2%) vs 146/4122 (3.5%); HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.70, 1.13); NI p<0.0001; superiority p=0.34
- FDA comments: FDA did not agree with the 1.5 margin (retains ~70% of warfarin effect; FDA recommended 85-90%)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review (VTE section §3.2.2)

> "The secondary efficacy endpoint was compared between Edoxaban and Warfarin using un-stratified log-rank test. The hazard ratio and corresponding 95% confidence interval (CI) were estimated for secondary efficacy endpoint using un-stratified Cox proportional hazard model."

### Ivabradine (Corlanor) — NDA 206143

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Amgen Inc. (SHIFT conducted by Servier). Approval year: 2015. Phase-3 trial(s): SHIFT (CL3-063), NCT02441218, Phase 3 (described in the FDA Statistical Review as a "pivotal phase 3 outcomes study").

#### Model 1: SHIFT (NCT02441218) — Time to first CV death or hospitalization for worsening HF (primary composite) (Primary)

- Model type: Standard Cox (covariate-adjusted)
- Stratification: None (randomization was stratified by beta-blocker intake and center, but the model adjusts for beta-blocker intake as a covariate)
- Covariates: Treatment; beta-blocker intake at randomization (yes/no)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Cox-model HR with 95% CI and two-sided p-value at 5% significance (test type not named in the review; README calls it a Wald test)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated; non-PH: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: Three DMC interim analyses (20% harm-only; 40% and 70% efficacy/harm) with Peto-type 0.1% efficacy boundary; original design 5,500 patients / 1,220 events for a 17% RRR with 90% power, increased by Amendment 5 to 7,000 patients and >=1,600 events
- Software: Not stated
- Result: RS (N=6,505): 793 ivabradine vs 937 placebo events; HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.75-0.90), p<0.0001. RSBBdose: 330 vs 362 events; HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.77-1.04), p=0.155
- FDA comments: Statistical reviewer used the Cox estimates for a Cui-Hung-Wang weighted-Z adjustment (HR 0.77 at 655 events, HR 0.82 at 1,730 events; weighted Z=4.24, p<0.0001) because the event-count amendments could not be shown to be independent of internal data; also re-ran the Cox model at successive artificial cut-off dates (nominal p<0.05 by June 17, 2008)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2 (Efficacy Analysis Methods); no protocol/SAP available

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary composite endpoint was tested using a survival analysis conducted on a time-to-first event basis using the intention-to-treat principle. A Cox’s proportional hazards model adjusted for previous beta-blocker intake at randomization was used to estimate the treatment effect and calculate the associated two-sided p-value (significance level: 5%)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Efficacy Analysis Methods, PDF p. 9 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206143Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "All analyses were carried out both on the RS and RSBBdose (hierarchical procedure)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Efficacy Analysis Methods, PDF p. 9 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206143Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The original protocol proposed a sample size of 5,500 patients for the detection of a 17% relative risk reduction of the PCE (90% power and 1220 events) and an expected mean follow-up of 2 years, assuming an annual incidence rate of the PCE of 14% in Placebo group and an incidence of non-cardiovascular death of 1% in both groups."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2, PDF p. 8 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206143Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In the RS, a total of 793 patients reached the primary composite endpoint in the Ivabradine group versus 937 patients in the Placebo group. The superiority of Ivabradine over Placebo in the reduction of the incidence of the primary endpoint was demonstrated, using a Cox proportional hazards model adjusted for beta-blocker intake at randomization, with an estimate of the hazard ratio of 0.82 (95% CI [0.75; 0.90], p < 0.0001). In the RSBBdose over the study period, a total of 330 patients reached the primary composite endpoint in the Ivabradine group versus 362 patients in the Placebo group. The estimate of the hazard ratio of the primary endpoint in this analysis set was 0.90 (95% CI [0.77; 1.04]), indicating a 10% RRR, but statistical significance was not reached (p = 0.155)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, primary results, PDF p. 11 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206143Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Figure 3-4 shows the P-values of Cox proportional hazards model for the primary endpoint as a function of calendar date of the study. In this analysis, the ascending event dates (regardless the treatment assignments) are assumed to be the artificial new end of trial dates, and the subjects’ event/censor statuses are modified accordingly. The Cox proportional hazards models were repeated to each new modified analysis dataset."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.3.1 (reviewer analysis), PDF p. 15 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/206143Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: SHIFT (NCT02441218) — Secondary endpoints: death (all-cause, CV, sudden cardiac, HF, non-CV) and hospitalization (any cause, CV, WHF, unplanned) (Secondary)

- Model type: Standard Cox (covariate-adjusted)
- Stratification: None
- Covariates: Same as primary (treatment; beta-blocker intake at randomization)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR, 95% CI, p-value
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated; non-PH: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: Not stated
- Result: All-cause death HR 0.90 (0.80-1.02), p=0.092; CV death 0.91 (0.80-1.03), p=0.128; sudden cardiac death 1.05 (0.87-1.26); HF death 0.74 (0.58-0.94), p=0.014; hospitalization for WHF 0.74 (0.66-0.83), p<0.0001; any-cause hospitalization 0.89 (0.82-0.96), p=0.0027
- FDA comments: Tables labelled "Reviewer's results"; reviewer notes most of the benefit is in HF hospitalization
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review ("For other efficacy endpoints, the analyses were performed as for the primary composite endpoint")

#### Model 3: SHIFT (NCT02441218) — Time to CV death (FDA reviewer (CDTL) exploratory analysis of loop-diuretic interaction)

- Model type: Standard Cox with multiple covariates and treatment-by-factor interaction terms
- Stratification: None
- Covariates: Ivabradine, loop diuretic, ivabradine x loop diuretic, age, age>=75 (+ x ivabradine), male, NYHA III-IV (+ x ivabradine), LVEF, HR, HR>75 (+ x ivabradine), SBP, weight, history of MI, ischemic etiology (+ x ivabradine), creatinine, potassium, K>5, MRA (+ x ivabradine, x loop diuretic), beta-blocker target (+ x ivabradine), ARB, ACEi, statin (each + x ivabradine), digoxin (+ x MRA, x loop diuretic)
- Ties: Breslow (Stata output header)
- CI/test: Wald z with 95% CI (Stata output)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated; non-PH: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: Stata (output format; review names the Stata mfpigen command for a related interaction analysis)
- Result: 911 CV deaths in 6,558 subjects; ivabradine x loop diuretic interaction HR 0.629 (95% CI 0.443-0.893), p=0.010; LR chi2(35)=522.57
- FDA comments: Division Director memo rejected this analysis: covariates and 13 interaction terms (from 231 possible) chosen without documented selection method, 5 interaction terms with p>0.2; found the loop-diuretic interaction "not to be credible" and excluded it from labeling
- Spec source: FDA CDTL Summary Review (Table 12) and Division Director memo

None of these choices is"

### Insulin degludec (Tresiba) — BLA 203314

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Novo Nordisk A/S. Approval year: 2015. Phase-3 trial(s): DEVOTE (NCT01959529), Phase 3b CVOT (interim analysis supported resubmission); pooled Phase 3a BEGIN program CV meta-analysis (17 randomized Phase 3 trials). BEGIN glycemic trials used ANCOVA (no Cox)..

#### Model 1: DEVOTE (NN1250-3998), NCT01959529 — Time to first adjudicated 3-point MACE (CV death incl. unknown cause, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke) — interim analysis vs 1.8 margin (Primary (pre-specified interim for regulatory resubmission))

- Model type: Standard Cox (unadjusted)
- Stratification: None
- Covariates: Treatment only (IDeg vs IGlar); "not adjusted for covariates"
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% CI for HR; upper bound compared with 1.8 (interim) / 1.3 (final) margin; sample size based on log-rank test, one-sided 2.5%
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA Appendix A.1 "Assessment of proportional hazards in primary MACE analysis" with log-log survival curves (Figure 6) and Schoenfeld residuals plot (Figure 7); appendix pages withheld (b)(4); non-PH: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: On-study: subjects without EAC-confirmed MACE censored at last direct contact before interim DBL; on-treatment sensitivity analyses SA1-SA4 (applicant) and SA5-SA7 (FDA reviewer); SA8 includes events pending adjudication
- Interim/sample size: Single interim at >=150 adjudicated first MACEs (95% power to rule out HR 1.8 at true HR 1.0); final at 633 MACEs (91% power to rule out 1.3, one-sided 2.5%)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Interim: 3,818 IDeg vs 3,820 IGlar randomized; HR and 95% CI redacted (b)(4) in the public review; upper bound ruled out 1.8 (README reports the post-approval final result HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.78-1.06, from the publication)
- FDA comments: "There are no statistical concerns on the design, conduct, and pre-specified analysis of the primary endpoint"; FDA requested on-treatment censoring sensitivity analyses and ran component, all-cause death and post hoc MACE+ Cox analyses with the same model
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review (2015 DEVOTE interim, Ref ID 3813664) §3.2.2.2.2

### Lixisenatide (Adlyxin) — BLA 208471

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Sanofi-Aventis U.S. LLC. Approval year: 2016. Phase-3 trial(s): ELIXA (NCT01147250), Phase III CVOT. GetGoal glycemic Phase 3 trials used ANCOVA/MMRM (no Cox)..

#### Model 1: ELIXA (EFC11319), NCT01147250 — Time to first adjudicated MACE+ (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina) (Primary (CV safety, non-inferiority vs 1.3 margin, then superiority))

- Model type: Standard Cox (covariate-adjusted)
- Stratification: None
- Covariates: Treatment; region (North America, South and Central America, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, Africa/Near East, Asia/Pacific)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% CI; NI if upper bound <1.3, superiority if upper bound <1 (step-down)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA reviewer: scaled Schoenfeld residual plot (Appendix A, Figure 14); no evidence of non-zero slope; non-PH: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: ITT, on-study (events from randomization to common study end date); on-treatment sensitivity (up to 30 days after last injection)
- Interim/sample size: ~6,000 patients for 844 positively adjudicated events; 96% power to rule out 30% excess risk at two-sided 5%
- Software: SAS (applicant submitted SAS code for primary MACE+ analysis)
- Result: 406/3,034 lixisenatide vs 399/3,034 placebo; HR 1.017 (95% CI 0.886-1.168), reported as 1.02 (0.89-1.17); 1.3 margin ruled out
- FDA comments: No statistical concerns; FDA PH check supported the model
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.3.3.1 (protocol-specified)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The analysis for the primary safety endpoint (the time to the first occurrence of the primary composite cardiovascular event, MACE+) was performed using a Cox proportional hazards model with treatment (lixisenatide, placebo) and region (North America, South and Central America, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, Africa/Near East, and Asia/pacific) as the covariates to estimate the hazard ratio between lixisenatide and placebo and the associated two-sided 95% confidence interval."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.3.3.1, PDF p. 16 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The safety objective (i.e. ruling out a relative excess risk of 30%) would be considered to be met if the upper bound of the 2-sided 95% CI of the hazard ratio is less than the 1.3 risk margin. If the 1.3 risk margin was ruled out, the superiority of lixisenatide over placebo was planned and would be claimed if the upper bound of the 2-sided 95% CI of the hazard ratio is less than1."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.3.3.1, PDF p. 16 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The trial was planned to recruit approximately 6000 patients, over an estimated 37 months enrollment period and estimated 10 months follow up period, in order to obtain 844 positively-adjudicated events for the primary cardiovascular endpoint based on the assumption of 10% yearly event rate for the first year and 7% yearly rate afterwards. The number of total events was expected to provide 96% power to rule out a relative excess cardiovascular risk of 30% for lixisenatide versus placebo at the 2-sided 5% level of significance."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.3.1, PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The primary MACE+ analysis used a Cox proportional hazards model to estimate hazard ratio and associated confidence intervals. To assess the proportional hazards assumption, Scaled Schoenfeld residuals were plotted in Figure 14. It included residuals from both the lixisenatide and placebo groups. In the plot, deviations from the horizontal line of the fitted line indicated potential violation of the proportional hazards assumption. The fitted line did not show evidence of a non-zero slope. Hence the proportional hazards assumption was reasonable for the Cox proportional hazards model fit to the primary MACE+ Cox analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review Appendix A, PDF p. 37 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Using the pre-specified Cox proportional hazards model, the hazard ratio estimate and associated 95% confidence interval is 1.017 (0.886, 1.168)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, PDF p. 8 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Semaglutide (Ozempic) — NDA 209637 (original approval)

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Novo Nordisk A/S. Approval year: 2017. Phase-3 trial(s): SUSTAIN 6 (NCT01720446), Phase 3a CVOT. SUSTAIN 1-5 glycemic trials used MMRM/ANCOVA (no Cox)..

#### Model 1: SUSTAIN 6 (NN9535-3744), NCT01720446 — Time to first 3-point MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke) (Primary (CV safety, NI vs 1.8 margin))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: 9 strata from 3 randomization factors: CV disease at baseline (clinical/subclinical), insulin at baseline (none/basal/premix), GFR <30 mL/min/1.73m2
- Covariates: Treatment (pooled semaglutide 0.5+1.0 mg vs pooled placebo) as fixed factor
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Two-sided 95% CI at 5% alpha; H0: HR>=1.8
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Pre-specified graphical check of scaled Schoenfeld residuals vs time; FDA: PH "appears to hold" (Figure 14); non-PH: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: FAS (ITT, in-trial): followed to last visit, loss to follow-up, or event; SAS on-treatment +42 days sensitivity
- Interim/sample size: No interim analyses; 3,260 subjects / 122 events for 95% power to reject HR>=1.8 (1.98% annual rate, true HR 1)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 108/1,648 semaglutide vs 146/1,649 placebo; HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.58-0.95)
- FDA comments: Treated as supportive safety evidence (trial designed for NI, not superiority)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review (SUSTAIN 6) §3.1.3.2

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary analysis of MACE was pre-specified as a time to first event analysis. This analysis was conducted to rule out a hazard ratio greater than 1.8 at two-sided 5% alpha level based on a stratified Cox proportional hazard model with treatment arm as fixed factor. The stratification factor was categorized into 9 strata based on three stratification variables. This analysis will successfully rule out a hazard ratio of 1.8 if the upper bound of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio is below 1.8."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.1.3.2, PDF p. 68 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The proportional hazards assumption of the primary Cox model was evaluated graphically by plotting the scaled-Schoenfeld residuals of the model against time."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.1.3.2, PDF p. 68 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Randomization was stratified by three variables (total of 9 strata): 1) evidence of cardiovascular disease at baseline (clinical or subclinical), 2) insulin treatment at baseline (none, basal insulin or pre-mixed insulin), and 3) renal impairment with GFR value <30 mL/min/1.73m2 per MDRD at baseline (presence or absence). Note that subjects with severe renal impairment (GFR value <30 mL/min/1.73m2 per MDRD at baseline), by trial design, always fall into the “clinical evidence of CV disease” stratum. Therefore, this resulted in a total of 9 strata."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.1.2, PDF p. 66 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The sample size projection was based on the following assumptions: 1.98% annual event rate in each group, less than 10% dropout rate, an average observation time of 2.1 years, and a true hazard ratio of 1. Based on these assumptions, 3260 randomized subjects were needed to achieve"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.1.3.2, PDF p. 68 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "There were 108 MACE observed among 1648 subjects randomized to semaglutide and 146 MACE observed among 1649 subjects randomized to placebo. The pre-specified stratified Cox proportional hazard model obtained an estimated hazard ratio of semaglutide vs. placebo of 0.74 with 95% confidence interval of (0.58, 0.95)."

The Anderson-Gill model is an extension of the Cox proportional hazards model, where the hazard for the kth event, i.e. including both first and recurrent, for a subject i at time t, is given by hik(t) = h0(t) exp(βTx), with h0(t) being the baseline hazard and x the vector of covariates for subject i."

Robust standard errors will be used to account for correlations of event times within a subject [15] [16]. The following null hypothesis will be compared with the alternative hypothesis: H0: HRVericiguat/Placebo = 1 H1: HRVericiguat/Placebo < 1 Superiority of MK-1242 (vericiguat) over placebo in prolonging the time to total HF hospitalization will be concluded, if the upper limit of the confidence interval of the hazard ratio is below 1 with the confidence level matching the nominal alpha level used for testing at the interim or final analysis. Estimates of treatment comparisons and effect size including 95% confidence intervals will be provided based on the fitted model. In addition, time to total HF hospitalizations and CV death will be analyzed using the Wei, Lin, Weissfeld (WLW) method [17], and details will appear in the supplemental SAP."

### Dasiglucagon (Zegalogue) — NDA 214231

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Zealand Pharma A/S. Approval year: 2021. Phase-3 trial(s): ZP4207-16137 (NCT03378635), ZP4207-17145 (NCT03688711), ZP4207-17086 (NCT03667053) — all Phase 3 (Phase III per FDA review).

#### Model 1: ZP4207-16137, NCT03378635 — Time to plasma glucose recovery (beneficial event; rescue IV glucose censored as not recovered at 45 min) (Additional/descriptive analysis of primary endpoint (inference by stratified log-rank test))

- Model type: Standard Cox, discrete-time (exact discrete partial likelihood)
- Stratification: None in Cox (injection site entered as categorical effect; log-rank test stratified by injection site)
- Covariates: Treatment group; injection site (abdomen, buttock, thigh) as categorical effects; baseline plasma glucose (continuous)
- Ties: Discrete ("exact discrete" partial likelihood, ties=discrete)
- CI/test: Rate (hazard) ratios with 95% CI; pairwise inferences by two-sided likelihood ratio tests; injection-site influence by type 3 test
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Pre-condition: graphical comparison of log-minus-log survival curves, and no more than two-thirds of recovery times censored per arm; non-PH: Cox model not fit if PH not supported; FDA reviewer added log-normal parametric survival "recovery time ratio" (R rms::psm) because the HR is not intuitive
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Rescue IV glucose: censored as not recovered at 45 min; sensitivity analyses without censoring and with censoring at time of rescue
- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG (or TPHREG)
- Result: Dasiglucagon n=82 vs placebo n=43: HR 111 (95% CI 38-330); median 10 vs 40 min; recovery time ratio 0.29 (0.26-0.33)
- FDA comments: SAP §4.2 calls the Cox model descriptive but §4.10 says "used for inferences" (internal inconsistency); FDA preferred survival time ratio for interpretability
- Spec source: SAP v1 §4.7.2 (p.19) and §4.10

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary endpoint will additionally be analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards (CPH) time to event statistical model, if the hazards by treatment group can be assumed proportional using a graphical comparison of log-minus-log survival curves and no more than two-thirds of the recovery times are censored in each treatment group. The CPH model will be used for descriptive purposes, with treatment group and injection site modeled as categorical effects, and baseline plasma glucose modelled as a continuous covariate. The treatment group rate ratios, active versus placebo, will be estimated together with the 95% confidence intervals, and pairwise treatment group inferences (dasiglucagon vs placebo, GlucaGen vs placebo) will be evaluated using two-sided likelihood ratio tests. Due to the discrete nature of blood sampling in time, and the fact that there must be a true, but unmeasured, ordering of the recovery times, the method using the “exact discrete” partial likelihood for tied failure times will be applied. In SAS, this is implemented in the phreg procedure with the option ties=discrete. The influence of injection site on time to recovery will also be evaluated in the proportional hazards model by a ‘type 3” test in the phreg procedure."
>
> — SAP v1 Final 1 (ZP4207-16137), primary analysis — tesseract OCR of PDF p.19, PDF p. 19 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/35/NCT03378635/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The primary endpoint will be additionally analyzed using a Cox Proportional Hazards (CPH) time to event statistical model. The CPH model will be used for inferences, with treatment group and injection site (abdomen, buttock, or thigh) modelled as categorical effects, and baseline plasma glucose modelled as a continuous covariate. The treatment group rate ratios, active versus placebo, will be estimated together with the 95% confidence intervals, and pairwise"
>
> — SAP v1 Final 1 §4.10 Adjustment for Covariates, PDF p. 27 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/35/NCT03378635/SAP_001.pdf)

> "In addition to presenting the median time to recovery with 95% CI in each group, since plasma glucose were collected at discrete time such as pre-dose, and at 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, 20, 25 etc. post-dose, the sponsor performed a discrete-time Cox Proportional Hazard (CPH) model with treatment group and stratification factors as categorical effects and baseline plasma glucose as continuous covariate as an additional analysis and showed the hazard ratio (HR) in terms of summary statistic of comparison for two groups in Trials 16137 and 17145 (adult studies) ."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Recovery (Survival) Time Ratio, PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/214231Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Since the primary endpoint is time to recovery that is a beneficial outcome rather than hazardous outcome such as death, the hazard ratio was not intuitively understood for the time to plasma glucose recovery. To better understand, this reviewer borrowed the concept of a survival time ratio from the parametric survival model1 with log-normal distribution for a comparison of time to plasma glucose recovery in two groups. With time to recovery in the placebo group as a reference, the survival time ratio will be the ratio of time to recovery in the dasiglucagon group over one in the placebo group. In this review, the “recovery” time ratio is used in lieu of the survival time ratio. If the recovery time ratio is less than 1, then the results are interpreted as a favor to dasiglucagon because the recovery time becomes shorter with the group change from placebo. Parametric Survival Model (psm) function in the R package, rms v.6.6 was used to calculate the survival time ratio."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Recovery (Survival) Time Ratio, PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/214231Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Finerenone (Kerendia) — NDA 215341

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.. Approval year: 2021. Phase-3 trial(s): FIDELIO-DKD (NCT02540993), Phase III.

#### Model 1: FIDELIO-DKD (BAY 94-8862/16244), NCT02540993 — Time to first kidney failure, sustained eGFR decrease >=40%, or renal death (primary renal composite) (Primary (HR estimation; test is stratified log-rank))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Region (North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Others), eGFR category at screening (25-<45, 45-<60, >=60), type of albuminuria (high, very high); strata based on screening values corrected via IxRS; sensitivity analysis using randomization (IxRS) strata if stratification errors
- Covariates: Treatment only (trtgrpn)
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: Stratified log-rank test for inference; HR with two-sided 95% CI from PHREG (RL); adjusted alpha for interim/Bonferroni-Holm
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: log(-log(KM)) vs log time plots and treatment x log(time) interaction in Cox model; FDA: interaction p=0.4133; non-PH: If interaction significant and plots show non-proportionality, time-dependent HRs from the interaction model
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Last visit with complete information on all components (extended up to the next planned visit for kidney failure/renal death); non-renal deaths censored; on-treatment (30 days) and PPS sensitivity; tipping-point MI analysis using stratified Cox
- Interim/sample size: 1,068 events for >=90% power (HR 0.80, two-sided 3.3333%); ~4,690 subjects; interim at 2/3 information (716 events), stopping p<0.0027 — not stopped (HR 0.882, p=0.095)
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG / PROC LIFETEST
- Result: 504/2,833 finerenone vs 600/2,841 placebo; HR 0.825 (95% CI 0.732-0.928), p=0.0014
- FDA comments: Applicant analysis verified; PH supported (interaction p=0.4133)
- Spec source: SAP §6.2.1.1-6.2.1.2, §4.1, §4.7; FDA Integrated Review

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "In order to provide a point estimate of the hazard ratio and a corresponding two-sided 95% confidence interval, a stratified Cox proportional hazard regression model will be used. The stratification variables will be included in the STRATA statement in SAS PROC PHREG, which will assume proportional hazards for each level of one particular stratification factor. Kaplan Meier curves will be provided for the cumulative incidence risk of outcome events by treatment groups."
>
> — SAP §6.2.1.1, PDF p. 28 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02540993/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
PROC PHREG DATA = <dataset>;
  MODEL ttevalue * ttecnsr(1) = trtgrpn / RL TIES=EFRON
ALPHA=0.05;
  STRATA {stratumn};
RUN;
```
— SAP §6.2.1.1 (Cox SAS code), PDF p. 28 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02540993/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The logrank test as well as the Cox regression model will also be performed without including stratification factors. The plausibility of the proportional hazards assumption will be assessed by visually examining the plot of the log of the negative log of Kaplan-Meier estimates of the survival function versus log time for evidence of non-parallelism, and by including a treatment by log-transformed time interaction into the Cox model. For the latter, the SAS code is adapted as follows:"
>
> — SAP §6.2.1.2, PDF p. 29 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02540993/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
PROC PHREG DATA = <dataset>;
  MODEL ttevalue * ttecnsr(1) = trtgrpn trtltime / RL
TIES=EFRON ALPHA=0.05;
  STRATA {stratum};
  trtltime = trtgrpn*log(ttevalue);
RUN;
```
— SAP §6.2.1.2 (PH-check SAS code), PDF p. 29 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02540993/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The significance of the interaction will be tested at the 5% type I error level. If the interaction is significant and there is strong evidence of non-proportionality from the plots, time-dependent hazard ratios will be estimated with the model that includes the interaction term."
>
> — SAP §6.2.1.2, PDF p. 29 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02540993/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The stratified analyses mentioned in this SAP will be conducted in consideration of the randomization stratification factors region, eGFR category and type of albuminuria unless specified otherwise, see also section 4.5.4. The strata variables type of albuminuria and eGFR category used in the statistical analysis will be based on the screening UACR and eGFR assessments and corrected via the interactive voice/web response system (IxRS) if necessary. All subjects will be analyzed according to their correct stratification category. If screening values are not available, the run-in values will be used. If a subject’s actual UACR / eGFR combination results in a stratification group that does not exist in the study (e.g. in 16244, very high albuminuria and eGFR ≥75 mL/min/1.73m2) then the stratification group the investigator originally specified in IxRS will be kept. In case of stratification errors, the primary analysis will also be repeated based on the stratification category used in the randomization as a sensitivity analysis."
>
> — SAP §4.1, PDF p. 13 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02540993/SAP_001.pdf)

> "A total of 1068 primary efficacy endpoint events will have a minimum 90% power to demonstrate superiority of finerenone to placebo using a logrank test at a two sided significance level of 3.3333%, assuming a 20% relative risk reduction, i.e. a true hazard ratio of 0.80 (the hazard ratio that will be observed in the study will be different, i.e. closer to 1 due to treatment discontinuations). The study will stop when at least 1068 primary efficacy endpoints accrue across both treatment arms."
>
> — SAP §3 Study Design (sample size), PDF p. 10 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02540993/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Impute events to the end of the study 1000 times, calculate the hazard ratios with the stratified Cox model specified in section 6.2.1.1 and combine them using standard multiple imputation combining rules."
>
> — SAP §6.2.1.2 (tipping point), PDF p. 30 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02540993/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Furthermore, the SAS code for the Cox model was corrected to the stratified Cox model specified in the text (by means of adding the stratification factors to the STRATA statement)."
>
> — SAP change history, Modification 11, PDF p. 42 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/93/NCT02540993/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Primary and secondary efficacy analyses for time to event variables were to be based on the FAS dataset. The data were to be analyzed using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model with randomization factors (region, type of albuminuria, and eGFR category) and a log rank test stratified by the randomization factors."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review §III, PDF p. 40 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/215341Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Based on stratified Cox proportional hazards model including treatment by log-transformed time interaction, a p-value of 0.4133 (two-sided) of the interaction term showed no strong evidence against the proportional hazard assumption, which can also be supported from visually examine the curves in the KM plot."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, primary endpoint, PDF p. 48 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/215341Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Sotagliflozin (Inpefa) — NDA 216203

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Lexicon Pharmaceuticals, Inc.. Approval year: 2023. Phase-3 trial(s): SOLOIST-WHF (NCT03521934) and SCORED (NCT03315143), both Phase 3.

#### Model 1: SOLOIST-WHF (EFC15156), NCT03521934 — Total (first and subsequent) CV deaths, HHF and urgent HF visits (Primary)

- Model type: Marginal Cox for recurrent events with non-CV death as competing event (FDA describes as "Fine and Gray method")
- Stratification: Region (North America, Latin America, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, rest of world) and LVEF (<50%, >=50%)
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Same-day events jittered by 0.1 day so every event time is unique
- CI/test: Stratified Wald test, two-sided 0.05; HR with two-sided 95% CI
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Pre-specified test of a piecewise HR before/after 240 days vs constant HR; FDA: time-by-treatment interaction p=0.9583; non-PH: Piecewise (240-day) HR model comparison
- Robust variance / frailty: Robust sandwich covariance
- Censoring: Alive patients censored at last known alive date; deaths not in endpoint are competing events; on-treatment (+30 days) sensitivity; IRT vs eCRF stratum sensitivity
- Interim/sample size: Trial terminated early (March 2020, funding); SAP finalized blinded after termination
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 245 events (142 pts) sotagliflozin n=608 vs 355 (194) placebo n=614; HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.53-0.85), p=0.001
- FDA comments: FDA labels the model Fine-Gray-based; PH check passed; Bayesian shrinkage subgroup analysis added
- Spec source: SOLOIST SAP v1.0 (09-Aug-2020) §2.4.4.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint will be the comparison between the two treatments using a Wald test stratified by region (North America, Latin America, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, and rest of world) and LVEF (<50%, >50%). This primary comparison will be a 2-sided test at the 0.05 type 1 error level for the following hypothesis: HO: HR=1 versus H1: HR #1 The estimates of the hazard ratio (HR) and corresponding 2-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) will be provided by a marginal Cox proportional hazard model stratified by region and ejection fraction, with non-cardiovascular (non-CV) death treated as a competing event. By using a robust sandwich covariance matrix estimate, the model allows for the possibility of multiple events within a given patient. If a given patient has more than one event on a given day, the event times will be varied by 0.1 day so that ever event time is unique."
>
> — SOLOIST-WHF SAP §2.4.4.1 (tesseract OCR), PDF p. 18 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/34/NCT03521934/SAP_001.pdf)

> "To determine whether the treatment effect on the primary endpoint is different before and after 240 days (the end of the window for up-titration of dose), a marginal proportional hazards model that allows the treatment HR to vary before and after 240 days will be compared with the model in which the treatment HR is assumed constant over time, to test whether a nonconstant HR provides a better fit to the observed data."
>
> — SOLOIST-WHF SAP §2.4.4.1 (tesseract OCR), PDF p. 18 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/34/NCT03521934/SAP_001.pdf)

> "In the analyses of time-to-event efficacy endpoints: e Deaths not included among the events in the endpoint will be treated as competing events; e Patients alive at the end of the study will be right censored on the date they were last known to be alive;"
>
> — SOLOIST-WHF SAP (tesseract OCR), PDF p. 10 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/34/NCT03521934/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Primary efficacy analysis: A marginal Cox proportional hazard model using Fine and Gray method was used to derive the estimates of the hazard ratio (HR) and corresponding 2-sided 95% confidence interval (CI), stratified by region and LVEF, with non-cardiovascular (non-CV) death treated as a competing event. By using a robust sandwich covariance matrix estimate, the model allowed for the possibility of multiple events within a given patient. If a given patient had more than one event on a given day, the event times were varied by 0.1 day so that every event time was unique. A Wald test was used to compare the number of total occurrences (first and potentially subsequent) of events of CV death, HHF, and urgent HF between the two treatment groups stratified by region (North America, Latin America, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, and rest of world) and LVEF (<50%, ≥50%) in SOLOIST trial; and stratified by region (North America, Latin America, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, and rest of world) and HF-related criteria (yes/no) in SCORED trial. The primary comparison was conducted at 2-sided 0.05 significance level."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review §III, PDF p. 30 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216203Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "To check the proportional hazard assumption for the Fine–Gray model: An analysis was conducted by including the interaction of time by treatment. The results of a non-significant interaction (p=0.9583, p=0.6003 for SOLOIST and SCORED, respectively) suggested that the proportional hazard assumption was held."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, reviewer analyses, PDF p. 45 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216203Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "placebo in reducing the risk of the primary composite endpoint (HR [95% CI]: 0.67 [0.53, 0.85], p=0.001 SOLOIST; 0.75 [0.63, 0.88], p = 0.0004 SCORED)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, results, PDF p. 43 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216203Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

- Ties: Same-day events jittered by 0.1 day
- CI/test: Stratified Wald test, two-sided 0.05; HR with 95% CI
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Piecewise HR before/after 180 days vs constant; FDA time-by-treatment interaction p=0.6003; non-PH: Piecewise (180-day) HR model comparison
- Robust variance / frailty: Robust sandwich covariance
- Censoring: As SOLOIST; IRT vs eCRF HF-criteria stratum sensitivity if >5% discrepancy; SGLT-2 initiation censoring sensitivity
- Interim/sample size: Terminated early (March 2020, loss of funding); SAP finalized blinded
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 400 events (310 pts) vs 530 (391), n=5,292 per arm; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.63-0.88), p=0.0004
- FDA comments: Stratification described by FDA as region and HF-related criteria
- Spec source: SCORED SAP v1.0 (21-Aug-2020) §2.4.4.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint will be the comparison between the two treatments using a Wald test stratified by region (North America, Latin America, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, and rest of world) and HF-related criteria (yes/no). This primary comparison will be a 2-sided test at the 0.05 type 1 error level for the following hypotheses: HO: HR =1 versus H1: HR #1 The estimates of the hazard ratio (HR) and corresponding 2-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) will be provided by a marginal Cox proportional hazard model stratified by region and ejection fraction, with non-cardiovascular (non-CV) death treated as a competing event. By using a robust sandwich covariance matrix estimate, the model allows for the possibility of multiple events within a given patient. If a given patient has more than one event on a given day, the event times will be varied by 0.1 day so that every event time is unique."
>
> — SCORED SAP §2.4.4.1 (tesseract OCR), PDF p. 22 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/43/NCT03315143/SAP_001.pdf)

> "To determine whether the treatment effect on the primary endpoint is different before and after 180 days (the last opportunity for up-titration in SCORED), a marginal proportional hazards model that allows the treatment HR to vary before and after 180 days will be compared with the model in which the treatment HR is assumed constant over time, to test whether a nonconstant HR provides a better fit to the observed data."
>
> — SCORED SAP §2.4.4.1 (tesseract OCR), PDF p. 22 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/43/NCT03315143/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The primary analysis was repeated using the actual stratification of HF related criteria based on the electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) if discrepancy in stratum assignment between Interactive Response Technology (IRT) and eCRF occurred in more than 5% of patients."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, sensitivity analyses, PDF p. 31 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216203Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Acoramidis (Attruby) — NDA 216540

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (Eidos Therapeutics). Approval year: 2024. Phase-3 trial(s): ATTRibute-CM Part B (NCT03860935), Phase 3; primary endpoint Finkelstein-Schoenfeld (not Cox).

#### Model 1: ATTRibute-CM (AG10-301 Part B), NCT03860935 — Time to all-cause mortality by Month 30 (heart transplant/CMAD counted as death) (Key secondary (4th in fixed sequence at alpha_B=0.04))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: ATTR-CM genotype (ATTRm vs ATTRwt), baseline NT-proBNP category, baseline eGFR/renal function — IWRS randomization levels (actual-strata sensitivity if mis-stratification >10%)
- Covariates: Treatment; baseline 6MWT (SAP v3.0 text). Original Appendix 1.4 code had treatment only; addendum updated code adds bl6mwt
- Ties: Exact
- CI/test: Wald CI/p-value for HR (hazardratio / cl=wald); stratified log-rank also performed; CMH at Month 30
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: log(-log) plots and treatment x log(time) interaction at 0.05; non-PH: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Treatment-policy estimand (tafamidis initiation ignored); ITT repeat
- Interim/sample size: No efficacy interim; N~510 (2:1); Part B alpha 0.04
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG
- Result: 79/409 acoramidis vs 52/202 placebo; HR 0.77 (96% CI 0.54-1.10), p=0.0754 (not significant)
- FDA comments: FDA review restates the SAP method and reports the non-significant result; no critique of the Cox specification found. SAP fallback: unstratified Cox with stratification factors as covariates if the stratified model does not converge
- Spec source: Part B SAP v3.0 §11.2.4 and Appendix 1.4; SAP Addendum v1.0 §5

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The time to All-Cause Mortality will be analyzed using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model that includes treatment as an explanatory factor along with baseline 6MWT. P-values and confidence intervals for the HR will be based on the Wald statistic (Appendix 1.4). Prior to running the Cox proportional hazards model, the overall validity of proportional hazards assumption will be examined by graphical methods and model, such as: Log (-log) plots; if the assumption holds the curves should be approximately parallel to each other. Include treatment*log (time) as a factor in the model and test the interaction factor at the 0.05 significance; non significance (p>0.05) of this factor would suggest proportionality. In case the stratified Cox model does not converge, then a regular Cox proportional hazards model will be used with stratification factors, treatment, and baseline 6MWT as explanatory variables. In addition, stratified log-rank test will be performed."
>
> — Part B SAP v3.0 §11.2.4, PDF p. 34 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/35/NCT03860935/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
PROC PHREG DATA=xxx;
CLASS trt (ref=< >) genotype (ref= < >) renal_function (ref= < >) NT_proBNP (ref= < >);
MODEL days*status(0)=trt / ties=EXACT;
STRATA genotype renal_function NT_proBNP;
RUN
```
— Part B SAP v3.0 Appendix 1.4 (original sample code, as printed), PDF p. 54 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/35/NCT03860935/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
PROC PHREG DATA=xxx;
CLASS trt (ref=< >) genotype (ref= < >) renal_function (ref= < >) NT_proBNP (ref= < >);
model days*status(0)=trtn bl6mwt / ties=exact;
strata genotype renal_function NT_proBNP;
hazardratio 'H1' trtn / cl=wald;
LSMEANS trtn / diff cl exp;
ODS OUTPUT HazardRatios = HazardRatios Diffs=diff;
RUN;
```
— SAP Addendum v1.0 (30 June 2023) §5, "Updated" PHREG code, PDF p. 65 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/35/NCT03860935/SAP_001.pdf)

> "For statistical analyses, the stratification factor levels used during randomization in the Interactive Web Response System (IWRS) will be utilized. If the overall mis-stratification proportion is greater than 10% of subjects, a sensitivity analysis on the primary and key secondary endpoints using actual stratification factors will be performed."
>
> — Part B SAP v3.0 §2.3, PDF p. 14 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/35/NCT03860935/SAP_001.pdf)

> "All-Cause Mortality by Month 30 (stratified cox proportional hazard model) In this hierarchical approach"

### Etripamil (Cardamyst) — NDA 218571

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Milestone Pharmaceuticals Inc.. Approval year: 2025. Phase-3 trial(s): RAPID / NODE-301 Part 2 (NCT03464019), Phase 3; NODE-301 Part 1 (Phase 3, failed; HR 1.1 by Peto-Peto, HR method not stated); NODE-303 single-arm safety (no Cox).

#### Model 1: RAPID (NODE-301 Part 2, MSP-2017-1138), NCT03464019 — Time to adjudicated PSVT termination and conversion to sinus rhythm >=30 s within 30 min (Primary (HR estimation; test is Wilcoxon via PROC LIFETEST))

- Model type: Standard Cox
- Stratification: Not stated
- Covariates: Not stated
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Wilcoxon test (LIFETEST) for p-value; Cox HR with 95% CI; log-rank sensitivity
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated; non-PH: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: ECG interruption: censored at interruption; additional medical intervention without conversion or conversion after window: censored at 31 min; alternative censoring at intervention-induced conversion (sensitivity)
- Interim/sample size: 180 confirmed PSVT episodes for >=90% power at two-sided 0.05 (54% vs 30%)
- Software: SAS
- Result: Efficacy population (n=184: 99 vs 85): KM 64.3% vs 31.2%; HR 2.62 (95% CI 1.66-4.15), p<0.001. mITT (n=255): HR 2.59 (1.64-4.09). Alternative censoring: HR 2.59 (1.64-4.10). Repeat-dose regimen: HR 2.76 (1.66-4.58); single-dose: 1.69 (0.59-4.89)
- FDA comments: FDA considered the mITT population more appropriate and verified results; README quotes HR "2.59-2.6 (95% CI 1.66, 4.15)", mixing mITT HR with efficacy-population CI
- Spec source: FDA Integrated Review §6.2.2.3 (SAP signed June 6, 2022; SAP not public)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary endpoint was analyzed via Statistical Analysis System Lifetest procedure using Wilcoxon test. The hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval were calculated using the Cox proportional hazards model. In addition, Kaplan Meier estimates of time to conversion were calculated and reported as a Kaplan Meier plot."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review §6.2.2.3, PDF p. 69 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/218571Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Using the Applicant’s proposed analysis set (i.e., Efficacy Population of 184 confirmed PSVT), the Kaplan-Meier estimates for subjects converted to SR within 30 minutes are 31.2% and 64.3% for placebo and etripamil arms, respectively. The result is shown in Table 10. The hazard ratio is 2.62 with 95% confidence interval (1.66, 4.15) and p-value<0.001, showing the superiority of etripamil."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, primary endpoint, PDF p. 73 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/218571Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Based on the mITT Population of 255 subjects who took the study drug for perceived PSVT episodes, the Cox proportional hazards model was used. The hazard ratio is 2.59 with 95% confidence interval (1.64, 4.09) and p-value<0.001."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, primary endpoint (mITT), PDF p. 74 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/218571Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "A sensitivity analysis based on the alternative censoring method was also conducted. In the primary analysis, the subjects who received additional medical intervention were censored at the time examined (i.e., 30 minutes), even though they received their intervention within the 30-minute window. In the sensitivity analysis, these subjects were censored at the time when their PSVT were converted due to this intervention. The result is shown in Table 12. The hazard ratio is 2.59 with 95% confidence interval (1.64, 4.10) and p-value<0.001."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, sensitivity analyses, PDF p. 75 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/218571Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

Therapeutic area: Infectious Disease. Sponsor: Janssen Research & Development. Approval year: 2012. Phase-3 trial(s): C208 (NCT00449644) Phase II; C209 single-arm Phase II; no Phase 3 at approval.

Supporting quotes:

The first stage is exploratory and the second stage is a proof-of-efficacy stage (pivotal study) to demonstrate the superiority of TMC207 over placebo in time to culture conversion. C209 is a single-arm, open-label study to provide additional efficacy and safety data."

### Peramivir (Rapivab) — NDA 206426

Therapeutic area: Infectious Disease. Sponsor: BioCryst Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Approval year: 2014. Phase-3 trial(s): Study 0815T0631 ("815", Shionogi, Phase III per Kohno et al. 2011 title; no NCT); BCX1812-311 (NCT00610935, Phase 3 per ClinicalTrials.gov; terminated early at ~10% of planned size). Scope note: the FDA-designated pivotal trial 0722T0621 ("722"/README "Study 621") is called "the previous phase II study" in the Phase III publication (its ref. 12 = Kohno et al. 2010), so its protocol-specified stratified Cox (HR 0.681/0.666) is out of scope and not modeled below; BCX1812-211 and -212 are Phase 2 per ClinicalTrials.gov. The FDA Statistical Review never states phases.

#### Model 1: Study 815 (0815T0631) — time to alleviation of symptoms (primary, non-inferiority vs oseltamivir)

- Model type: Standard Cox (covariate-adjusted)
- Stratification: None (no strata statement; randomization was dynamic allocation/minimization on smoking, baseline composite symptom score, country, influenza type)
- Covariates: Treatment; composite symptom score at baseline; current smoking (yes/no); country (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan); influenza type by RAT (A, B, A and B); sex; medically important coexisting disease (yes/no); any drug treatment from influenza onset to randomization (yes/no). Last three added before unblinding after blind review.
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 97.5% CI for HR of each peramivir dose vs oseltamivir; non-inferiority if upper limit <1.170; Bonferroni adjustment for two doses stated in publication (two-sided 0.05). CI type (Wald etc.) not stated.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Non-PH handling: Not stated (FDA reviewer showed crossing K-M differences in H3N2 subset; see Model 2)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Patients without alleviation of influenza symptoms censored
- Interim/sample size: 1,050 patients (350/arm) for 80% power, two-sided 0.025, NI margin 0.170, assuming HR vs placebo 0.67 (peramivir) and 0.73 (oseltamivir), duration 73 h; no interim stated
- Software: SAS version 9.1 for Windows (publication)
- Result: ITTI N=364/362/365 (300 mg/600 mg/oseltamivir). HR 300 mg vs oseltamivir 0.946 (97.5% CI 0.793-1.129); 600 mg 0.970 (0.814-1.157); medians 78.0/81.0/81.8 h. Events per arm not stated.
- FDA comments: FDA: 97.5% bound makes no multiplicity adjustment (98.75% appropriate); FDA-guidance-based margin would be HR 1.09, so 'the applicant's methodology would not yield a conclusion of non-inferiority'; widespread oseltamivir-resistant H1N1 meant trial could not be pivotal NI evidence.
- Spec source: Kohno et al. 2011 Methods; FDA Statistical Review §2.2.5, §2.2.6.4

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The duration of influenza, the primary endpoint, was analyzed using a Cox proportional-hazards model with the following covariates: the composite symptom score at baseline, current smoking behavior (yes or no), country (Japan, South Korea, or Taiwan), influenza virus type identified by RAT (type A, B, or A and B), sex (male or female), the presence of coexisting disease at baseline that was considered by the physician to be medically important and/or affecting evaluation (yes or no), and treatment with any drugs from the onset of influenza to randomization (yes or no). The factors of sex, coexisting disease at baseline, and receipt of drugs before randomization were added as covariates prior to unblinding, because the blind review revealed that these factors may have affected the duration of influenza."
>
> — Kohno et al. 2011, AAC (Study 815 publication, PMC HTML), HTML full text (no PDF page) (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3195028/)

> "Patients without alleviation of influenza symptoms were treated as censored data. The 97.5% confidence intervals (CI) for the hazard ratios of the 300- and 600-mg-peramivir groups compared to the oseltamivir group were calculated. Noninferiority to the oseltamivir group was indicated if the upper confidence limit was less than 1.170. All statistical tests were performed at a two-sided significance level of 0.05 using the Bonferroni adjustment for multiplicity."
>
> — Kohno et al. 2011, AAC (Study 815 publication, PMC HTML), HTML full text (no PDF page) (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3195028/)

> "This calculation was based on the assumptions that the hazard ratios of peramivir and oseltamivir versus the placebo were 0.67 and 0.73, respectively, and that the duration of influenza was 73 h."
>
> — Kohno et al. 2011, AAC (Study 815 publication, PMC HTML), HTML full text (no PDF page) (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3195028/)

> "Trial 815 also based its primary analysis on a Cox regression. Because this trial had an active control, Tamiflu, a non-inferiority comparison was proposed. A conclusion of efficacy for either the 300 mg or the 600 mg arm would be made if the 97.5% upper bound for the hazard ratio of that arm to Tamiflu was <1.17"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206426, PDF p. 61 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206426Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "One may briefly note that using 97.5% upper bound makes no adjustment for multiplicity. The appropriate confidence limit would have been 98.75%."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206426, PDF p. 61 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206426Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The log hazard ratio has a normally distributed hazard ratio so the computation of the non- inferiority bound using the methodology of the FDA guidance would involve taking one half of the upper limit"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206426, PDF p. 67 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206426Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: Study 815 — time to alleviation of symptoms (FDA reviewer stratified Cox reanalysis and indirect peramivir-vs-placebo synthesis)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Current smoking status and baseline total symptom score (FDA chose 2 of the 4 dynamic-allocation factors because 4-factor strata were too small)
- Covariates: Treatment only (stated as Cox of time to healing on treatment)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 95% CI on log HR; HR peramivir/placebo obtained by adding log HR peramivir/Tamiflu (Study 815) to log HR Tamiflu/placebo from Tamiflu NDA (0.73, SE 0.051) with SEs combined as root sum of squares; sensitivity moving Tamiflu HR 10% toward 1 and inflating SE by 10%
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Graphical: K-M curves and 95% confidence bands for difference in percent healed (vs time and vs percent healed) / Non-PH handling: Descriptive only; reviewer notes peramivir faster early and slower late vs Tamiflu in H3N2 subset
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable (post hoc)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Log HR peramivir/Tamiflu, all subjects: 300 mg 0.04198 (SE 0.07879) FDA times; 600 mg 0.04817 (SE 0.07820). H3N2 only (n=329): 300 mg -0.1394 (SE 0.15011); 600 mg -0.0518 (SE 0.14926). Indirect peramivir vs placebo shown graphically only.
- FDA comments: NI analysis restricted to H3N2 (Tamiflu-susceptible) subset; conclusion that peramivir unlikely effective against influenza B or Tamiflu-resistant A strains.
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2-3.2.3

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Trial 815 was not exactly stratified but was balanced with respect to current smoking status, baseline total symptom score, type of influenza, and country by dynamic allocation. The correct analysis of this type of randomization can be approximated by stratifying on the same four variables. Unfortunately, that yields strata too small to get valid estimates. After exploring the strata sizes using only two or three of the baseline covariate, the FDA statistical reviewer elected to analyze this trial stratifying on current smoking status and baseline total symptom score."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206426, PDF p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206426Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The FDA reviewer obtained the hazard ratios for peramivir to placebo by multiplying the hazard ratio peramivir/Tamiflu by the hazard ratio Tamiflu/placebo from the Tamiflu NDA. (The standard errors needed to get confidence intervals were obtained by adding the standard errors for log hazard ratios from the same two sources.)"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206426, PDF p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206426Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "it is quite noticeable that peramivir starts off ahead of Tamiflu but is lagging behind for the longer healing subjects."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206426, PDF p. 114 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206426Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "the current FDA reviewer calculated a sensitivity analysis in which the hazard ratio of Tamiflu to placebo is moved 10% closer to one"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 206426, PDF p. 119 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206426Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 3: BCX1812-311 — time to alleviation of symptoms (primary, protocol-specified; pooled with Phase 2 trial 211)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: FDA analysis: current smoking status and influenza type (randomization strata); applicant pooled analysis used trial 211 methodology (Cox stratified by smoking status)
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Cox with Bonferroni adjustment specified in protocol; applicant reported Wilcoxon-Gehan p-value instead of the Cox p-value for the pooled 211+311 data
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated
- Interim/sample size: Terminated at ~10% of planned sample size (82 randomized 2:1); no testing done
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Pooled 211+311, 300 mg IM vs placebo: HR 0.838 (95% CI 0.648-1.085), p=0.161 (Wilcoxon-Gehan). 311-alone HR not stated in text.
- FDA comments: FDA: 'The p-value for the Cox regression is not reported even though that was the protocol specified test.'
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §2.2.5, §2.2.6.2, §3.2.2
