### Baloxavir marboxil (Xofluza) — NDA 210854

Therapeutic area: Infectious Disease. Sponsor: Shionogi Inc. Approval year: 2018. Phase-3 trial(s): CAPSTONE-1 (1601T0831, NCT02954354); CAPSTONE-2 (NCT02949011) not part of the original NDA review.

**Excluded.** The only Cox proportional-hazards models in this application belong to the Phase 2b dose-ranging trial T0821 (primary analysis adjusted for composite symptom score and smoking; none of the dose-vs-placebo comparisons reached significance with Cox, and the applicant's post hoc check found non-proportional hazards). The Phase 3 CAPSTONE-1 SAP and protocol use only stratified generalized Wilcoxon (Peto-Prentice), log-rank, ANCOVA, van Elteren and Wilcoxon rank-sum methods; neither 'Cox' nor 'hazard ratio' appears in the CAPSTONE-1 SAP/protocol or in the CAPSTONE-2 SAP (ClinicalTrials.gov SAP_001.pdf). The FDA's Phase 3 sensitivity analyses used log-rank, Peto and modified-Peto tests (PROC LIFETEST), not Cox. The FDA review's Phase 3 time-to-fever result is reported with Wilcoxon and log-rank p-values only.

> "For the phase 2b trial, the applicant used the Cox proportional hazards model for the primary analysis adjusting for stratification variables of composite symptom scores (q11 vs. ≥12) and smoking status (yes, no)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 210854, PDF p. 12 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210854Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "None of the applicant’s statistical comparisons of each dose of S-033188 against placebo were statistically significant using the Cox proportional hazards model. This was most likely due to the lack of proportional hazards as statistical significance was achieved using the Gehan Wilcoxon test. The applicant performed a post-hoc analysis and found that the hazards were not proportional."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 210854, PDF p. 22 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210854Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The proportional hazards assumption does not hold for acute uncomplicated influenza because it is an illness of limited duration and survival curves converge after a few days."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 210854, PDF p. 58 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210854Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Artesunate (unbranded) — NDA 213036

Therapeutic area: Infectious Disease. Sponsor: Amivas LLC. Approval year: 2020. Phase-3 trial(s): SEAQUAMAT (no NCT) and AQUAMAT (ISRCTN50258054), both called 'phase 3 trials' in the FDA Multi-Discipline Review.

#### Model 1: SEAQUAMAT — in-hospital mortality / time to death (protocol-specified; not reported)

- Model type: Standard Cox (protocol-level; details not stated)
- Stratification: Not stated
- Covariates: Not stated
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Not stated (SAP primary: CMH stratified by site with RR/OR and 95% CI; FDA log-rank p=0.0002)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Non-PH handling: Not stated

- Censoring: FDA K-M: subjects who did not die censored at Day 35

### Remdesivir (Veklury) — NDA 214787

Therapeutic area: Infectious Disease. Sponsor: Gilead Sciences, Inc. Approval year: 2020. Phase-3 trial(s): ACTT-1 (NIAID, NCT04280705); GS-US-540-5773 (NCT04292899, Phase 3 per ClinicalTrials.gov); GS-US-540-5774 (NCT04292730, Phase 3 per ClinicalTrials.gov). Wang et al. 2020 (NCT04257656) summarized by FDA from publication only (HR 1.23, 95% CI 0.87-1.75, log-rank p=0.24); no patient-level review and no model text, not modeled.

#### Model 1: ACTT-1 — time to recovery through Day 29 (primary; recovery rate ratio)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (hazard ratio for favorable event = 'recovery rate ratio')
- Stratification: Baseline disease severity (mild/moderate vs severe); analyses used 'actual' strata from blinded review (differed from IxRS 'randomized' strata for 70 patients); applicant CSR generally used randomized strata
- Covariates: Treatment only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Wald CI (cl=Wald); p-value from stratified log-rank test; primary CI to account for group-sequential design; stage-wise ordering/median-unbiased estimate if stopped early; two-sided alpha 0.05
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: None stated (sample size 'under a proportional hazards assumption') / Non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Lost to follow-up/early termination censored at last observed assessment; non-recovered completers censored at Day 29 visit; deaths before recovery censored at Day 28/29 (worst rank); sensitivity censoring at crossover or unblinding
- Interim/sample size: Event-driven: 400 recoveries for 85% power to detect rate ratio 1.35 (two-sided 0.05); Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming spending, interim at ~50% information (t=r/400; protocol said 33%/67%); interim results disclosed April 2020
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG (final); R for interim analyses; R package ldbounds for boundaries
- Result: Final data: recoveries 399/541 vs 352/521; median 10 vs 15 days; rate ratio 1.29 (95% CI 1.12-1.49), p<0.001. April 28 cut: 1.31 (1.12-1.53).
- FDA comments: FDA reproduced results using 'actual' strata; stratifying by randomized strata 'virtually unchanged'; differences vs applicant in second decimal; competing risk of death handled by censoring at Day 29 judged reasonable; readmission-as-nonrecovery sensitivity rate ratio 1.22 (1.05-1.41); noted protocol/SAP inconsistency on interim timing.
- Spec source: ACTT-1 SAP v3.0 §6.1, §8.1.1, §5; FDA Statistical Review §3.1.3, §3.1.5.1

```sas
proc phreg data=dataset;
   class StrataVariable(ref=StrataLabel) TreatmentVariable(ref=PlaceboLabel);
   model TimeVariable * CensorVariable(1) = TreatmentVariable;
   strata StrataVariable;
   hazardratio TreatmentVariable / diff=ref cl=Wald;
   ods output HazardRatios = HRest;
run;
```

### Taurolidine/heparin (Defencath) — NDA 214520

Therapeutic area: Infectious Disease. Sponsor: CorMedix Inc. Approval year: 2023. Phase-3 trial(s): LOCK-IT-100 (NCT02651428), Phase 3, randomized 1:1, double-blind, active-controlled (heparin) in hemodialysis patients with a central venous catheter.

#### Model 1: LOCK-IT-100 — time to first CAC-adjudicated CRBSI (primary; Cox for HR only)

- Model type: standard (unstratified) Cox; stratified log-rank not used. The test is an unstratified log-rank, and Cox gives only the HR and CI.
- Stratification: None. Randomization used permuted blocks "without additional stratification".
- Covariates: treatment only ("only treatment in the MODEL statement").
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: two-sided log-rank test (PROC LIFETEST), 95% CI for the HR from PROC PHREG (CI method not stated). Pocock-adjusted nominal two-sided alpha was 0.0294 at both the interim and final analyses.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: patients without a CRBSI were censored at the earliest of catheter removal, study completion, or last study-drug dose plus 3 days (SAP addendum). CAC "indeterminate" cases were not counted as events; a sensitivity analysis counted them as events.
- Interim/sample size: designed for 80% power with a two-sided overall alpha of 5%, an assumed 55% risk reduction (HR about 0.45), and 56 CRBSI events in total. One interim analysis at 28 events used Pocock boundaries (0.0294). The trial stopped for efficacy at the interim analysis, and the analysis through the last patient's last visit (LPLV) is supportive, not a second test.
- Software: SAS PROC LIFETEST (log-rank, KM) and PROC PHREG (HR).
- Result: interim — 6/327 vs 22/326, log-rank p=0.0034, HR 0.28 (0.11, 0.70). Final (LPLV) — 9/397 (2.3%) vs 32/398 (8.0%), log-rank p=0.0006, HR 0.29 (0.14, 0.62) (MDR Table 11). Applicant sensitivity counting CAC-indeterminate cases as events: HR 0.32 (0.16, 0.65), p=0.0008.
- FDA comments: the reviewer noted that the endpoint definition changed mid-trial (CAC added, sample size raised to 900, interim analysis added). The reviewer also questioned the noninformative-censoring assumption and ran sensitivity analyses (see Model 3). Two screen-failure randomized subjects were added and censored at Day 1, and the results were identical.
- Spec source: SAP (29-Jan-2018) §1.3, §1.5, §2.4.1, §3.7.2; SAP Addendum (10-Nov-2018) §1.1; FDA Multi-Discipline Review §8.1.

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Permuted block randomization (centralized) will be utilized without additional stratification."
>
> — LOCK-IT-100 SAP §1.3, PDF p. 4 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/28/NCT02651428/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The primary analysis will be conducted using a log-rank test for the time to CRBSI at an overall 2-sided 5% alpha level. The null hypothesis is that there is no difference in the hazard rates of CRBSI over time between the two treatments."
>
> — LOCK-IT-100 SAP §2.4.1, PDF p. 6 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/28/NCT02651428/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The p-value for the log-rank comparison, hazard ratio (HR) with 95% confidence interval (active/control), and the incidence of CRBSI with 95% CI for each treatment group will be presented. The log-rank test will be performed using PROC LIFETEST in SAS. The HR and confidence interval will be calculated using PROC PHREG in SAS with only treatment in the MODEL statement and study day as the response variable."
>
> — LOCK-IT-100 SAP §3.7.2, PDF p. 11 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/28/NCT02651428/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Neutrolin is associated with a 55% reduction in the risk of CRBSI relative to the control arm, a 1 to 1 ratio will be used for the allocation of subjects to treatment arms, and one interim analysis will be performed at the midpoint of the trial with adjustment of the alpha level using the method of Pocock. Fifty-six CRBSI events in total will be needed to achieve the desired power."
>
> — LOCK-IT-100 SAP §1.5, PDF p. 5 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/28/NCT02651428/SAP_001.pdf)

> "If there is no such CRBSI, the patient will be censored at the earliest of the following dates: 1. Date of catheter removal, if any 2. Date of study completion, if any 3. Date of last study drug dose plus 3 days"
>

>

#### Model 2: LOCK-IT-100 — time to catheter removal for any reason and time to loss of catheter patency (secondary; fixed-sequence)

- Model type: standard (unstratified) Cox for the HR, with a log-rank test.
- Stratification: None.
- Covariates: treatment only (same approach as the primary analysis).
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: log-rank p-value and HR with 95% CI. Testing follows a fixed sequence after the primary endpoint.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: catheter removal was censored at the earlier of study completion or last dose plus 3 days. Loss of patency was censored at the earliest of catheter removal, study completion, or last dose plus 3 days.
- Interim/sample size: analyzed on LPLV data.
- Software: SAS (PROC LIFETEST and PROC PHREG by reference to the primary methods).
- Result: catheter removal for any reason — 236/397 vs 225/398, log-rank p=0.4161, HR 1.08 (0.90, 1.29). Loss of patency — 63 vs 48, p=0.1224, HR 1.34 (0.92, 1.96). The tPA-use and removal-for-patency components (HR 1.42 and 1.09) were computed by the FDA reviewer.
- FDA comments: FDA computed the component HRs itself.
- Spec source: SAP §3.7.3; FDA MDR §8.1.

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The analyses of the time until catheter removal for any reason and of time until loss of catheter patency will be based on the Full Analysis Population using the log-rank comparison, hazard ratio with 95% confidence interval (active/control), and incidence of the event of interest with 95% CI."
>
> — LOCK-IT-100 SAP §3.7.3, PDF p. 11 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/28/NCT02651428/SAP_001.pdf)

#### Model 3: LOCK-IT-100 — FDA reviewer sensitivity Cox analyses (alternative event definitions: death as event, nonpositive dispositions as events, FDA readjudication, gram-positive only)

- Model type: standard Cox (HR and 95% CI) with a log-rank test, as in the primary analysis.
- Stratification: None stated.
- Covariates: Not stated (presumably treatment only, as in the primary analysis; not explicit).
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: log-rank p-value and HR with 95% CI.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: the reviewer said the censoring rule matched the Applicant's. The point of these analyses was to probe informative censoring: death, or every "nonpositive" disposition (catheter malfunction, death, transfer, withdrawal, etc.), was treated as an event.
- Interim/sample size: N/A.
- Software: Not stated.
- Result: FDA-adjudicated CRBSI HR 0.29 (0.14, 0.62), p=0.0006. CAC CRBSI + death HR 0.59 (0.37, 0.94), p=0.0250. Protocol-definition CRBSI + death HR 0.74 (0.40, 1.36), p=0.3294. Gram-positive only HR 0.45 (0.20, 1.04), p=0.0551. All nonpositive disposition events HR 0.86 (0.70, 1.07), p=0.1723 (MDR Tables 15, 16, 23).
- FDA comments: the noninformative-censoring assumption "may not be valid". The reviewer still judged the effect "fairly consistent in the sensitivity analyses".
- Spec source: FDA MDR §8.1 (reviewer analyses).

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The Applicant assumed all censored data was noninformative, which implied that censoring was unrelated to the study treatment. This assumption may not be valid. The statistical reviewer conducted sensitivity analyses to evaluate the robustness of the study results by including death as an event in addition to CRBSI and also by considering nonpositive disposition events as events."

## Neurology / Psychiatry

### Dimethyl fumarate (Tecfidera) — NDA 204063

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Biogen Idec, Inc. Approval year: 2013. Phase-3 trial(s): DEFINE (Study 109MS301, NCT00420212) and CONFIRM (Study 109MS302, NCT00451451). Both are Phase 3, 96-week, placebo-controlled trials of BG00012 240 mg BID/TID; CONFIRM also had a glatiramer acetate reference arm.

#### Model 1: DEFINE (301) — time to first INEC-confirmed relapse / proportion relapsed at 2 years (primary)

- Model type: standard Cox (covariate-adjusted, unstratified).
- Stratification: none in the model. Randomization was stratified by site (for MRI-cohort balance).
- Covariates: treatment, number of relapses in the year before entry, baseline age (<40 vs ≥40), baseline EDSS (≤2.0 vs >2.0), and region. The protocol had EDSS ≤3.5 vs >3.5; the later-dated SAP used ≤2.0, which FDA accepted while checking ≤3.5 for robustness. The proportion relapsed is the KM estimate at 2 years.
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: Cox HR with 95% CI and p-value (test type not stated); two-sided 0.05. Fixed-order testing, with TID tested before BID for each endpoint.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: FDA reported "The proportional hazards assumption was checked and the assumption held" (method not stated). The FDA reviewer also ran a log-rank sensitivity analysis.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: only INEC-confirmed relapses count. Data after a switch to alternative MS medication are excluded, and time is censored at the switch.
- Interim/sample size: 337 per group for 90% power to detect a 30% reduction in proportion relapsed (48% vs 33.6%), using a chi-square test, 23% dropout, and alpha 0.05.
- Software: Not stated.
- Result: placebo 171/408 relapsed (KM 0.46); BID 98/410 (0.27), HR 0.51 (0.40, 0.66), p<0.0001; TID 95/416 (0.26), HR 0.50 (0.39, 0.65), p<0.0001. Pre-specified Cox sensitivity analyses: per-protocol, all CRF relapses, objective relapses, and relapses before plus after the alternative-medication switch. FDA worst-case Cox (all relapses counted for drug arms, only INEC pre-switch relapses for placebo): HR 0.60 (0.47, 0.76) BID and 0.63 (0.50, 0.80) TID. Subgroup Cox HRs were reported by sex, age, race, and region; the effect was larger in patients under 40.
- FDA comments: the reviewer resolved the protocol-vs-SAP EDSS cut-point discrepancy (≤3.5 vs ≤2.0) in favor of the SAP and re-ran the model with ≤3.5 (similar result). Worst-case analyses addressed possible unblinding from flushing.
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2, §3.2.4.1; FDA Medical Review (protocol amendments, sample size).

#### Model 2: DEFINE (301) — time to 12-week confirmed disability progression (secondary)

- Model type: standard Cox (covariate-adjusted).
- Stratification: None.
- Covariates: treatment, baseline EDSS (continuous), region, and age (<40 vs ≥40).
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: Cox HR with 95% CI and p-value; part of the fixed-order hierarchy.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated. The FDA reviewer ran a log-rank sensitivity analysis.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: patients without sustained progression were censored at the last EDSS evaluation that was not a tentative progression, before end of study or alternative medication. Post-switch EDSS may confirm a pre-switch tentative progression. Death due to MS counts as progression.
- Interim/sample size: N/A.
- Software: Not stated.
- Result: 89/408 vs 57/410 (BID) vs 62/416 (TID). HR 0.62 (0.44, 0.87), p=0.0050 for BID and 0.66 (0.48, 0.92), p=0.0128 for TID. 24-week CDP sensitivity: HR 0.77 (p=0.1893) and 0.69 (p=0.0760). FDA sustained-to-end-of-study sensitivity: HR 0.66 (p=0.0491) and 0.62 (p=0.0274).
- FDA comments: the reviewer added a Cox analysis counting post-switch progression, a log-rank test, and a sustained-progression analysis; all were consistent.
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2, Table 11.

### Peginterferon beta-1a (Plegridy) — BLA 125499

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Biogen Idec Inc. Approval year: 2014. Phase-3 trial(s): ADVANCE (105MS301, NCT00906399; ClinicalTrials.gov phase "PHASE3"), a 2-year randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 125 mcg every 2 weeks or every 4 weeks.

#### Model 1: ADVANCE — time to first INEC-confirmed relapse / proportion relapsed at 1 year (secondary)

- Model type: standard Cox (covariate-adjusted).
- Stratification: None stated. Per the FDA review, the primary analysis was pre-specified not to adjust for region.
- Covariates: treatment, baseline EDSS (<4 vs ≥4), baseline age (<40 vs ≥40), baseline relapse rate (relapses in the 3 years before entry), and baseline Gd-enhancing lesions (presence vs absence).
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: Cox HR with 95% CI and p-value. Sequential closed testing: every-2-weeks before every-4-weeks within each endpoint, each at 0.05.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: patients who withdrew without a relapse were censored on the last date of the 1-year phase. Patients who started alternative MS medication were censored at the start. Patients still relapse-free at Week 48 were censored at Week 48.
- Interim/sample size: the sample size was driven by ARR (blinded re-estimation from 420 to 500 per group). FDA analyzed the first 420 per group: HR 0.612 (p=0.0010) for every 2 weeks and 0.716 (p=0.0192) for every 4 weeks.
- Software: Not stated.
- Result: KM proportion relapsed 0.291 (placebo) vs 0.222 (every 4 weeks) vs 0.187 (every 2 weeks). HR 0.74 (0.57, 0.95), p=0.0200 for every 4 weeks; HR 0.61 (0.47, 0.80), p=0.0003 for every 2 weeks. Per-protocol and all-relapse sensitivity analyses were consistent.
- FDA comments: dropouts had a higher relapse risk. The FDA post hoc analysis imputing AE/withdrawal dropouts as relapses gave HR 0.838 (p=0.1543) for every 4 weeks and 0.758 (p=0.0290) for every 2 weeks; random 75% and 67% imputation gave p of 0.07 and 0.05 for every 2 weeks. Subgroup Cox HRs were reported with interaction p-values. The US/North America subgroup HR was in the wrong direction (every 2 weeks: 1.343 in North America vs 0.581 elsewhere), which FDA attributed to small numbers.
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2 (methods), §3.2.1.4, §4.1.

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The analysis method for the proportion of subjects relapsed at 1 year was to be a Cox proportional hazards model for time to first relapse, adjusted for baseline EDSS score (<4 or ≥ 4), baseline age ( <40 vs. > 40 years old), baseline relapse rate, and Gd enhancing lesions at baseline (Presence vs. absence)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 14 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125499Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "If a subject started alternative MS medication without experiencing a protocol-defined INEC-confirmed relapse, data for the subject was to be censored at the time of starting MS medication."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 14 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125499Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The hazard ratios obtained from the model were 0.74 (95% CI, 0.57, 0.95) for the BIIB017 every 4 weeks group versus placebo and 0.61 (95% CI, 0.47, 0.80) for the BIIB017 every 2 weeks group versus placebo"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 23 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125499Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "This reviewer’s post hoc sensitivity analysis of time to first relapse which assumed dropouts due to AE were relapses at the time of dropout gave first relapse hazard ratio results of 0.838, p=0.1543 for BIIB017 every 4 weeks and 0.758, p=0.0290 for BIIB017 every 2 weeks."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.4.2, PDF p. 30 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125499Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The estimated first relapse hazard ratio of BIIB017 every 2 weeks over placebo in North America in Year 1 was 1.343 as compared to 0.581 for Non North America."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §4.1.2, PDF p. 38 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125499Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: ADVANCE — time to 12-week confirmed disability progression at 1 year (secondary)

- Model type: standard Cox (covariate-adjusted).
- Stratification: None stated.
- Covariates: treatment, baseline EDSS (continuous), and age (<40 vs ≥40). A post hoc sensitivity analysis added baseline Gd-enhancing lesions.
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: Cox HR with 95% CI and p-value.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: progression cannot be confirmed during a relapse. Post-switch EDSS may confirm a pre-switch tentative progression. No imputation.
- Interim/sample size: N/A.
- Software: Not stated.
- Result: KM 0.105 (placebo) vs 0.068 in both active arms. HR 0.62 (0.40, 0.97) for both: p=0.0380 (every 4 weeks) and p=0.0383 (every 2 weeks). Sensitivity analyses: per-protocol p=0.0392 and 0.0287; tentative progression at withdrawal treated as an event p=0.0197 and 0.0928; adding Gd as a covariate p=0.0417 and 0.0623.
- FDA comments: none specific beyond reporting the sensitivity analyses.
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2 (methods), §3.2.1.

### Ocrelizumab (Ocrevus) — BLA 761053

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Genentech, Inc. (F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd). Approval year: 2017. Phase-3 trial(s): OPERA I (WA21092, NCT01247324) and OPERA II (WA21093, NCT01412333), Phase III trials in RMS of ocrelizumab vs interferon beta-1a 44 μg SC; ORATORIO (WA25046, NCT01194570), Phase III in PPMS vs placebo (2:1).

#### Model 1: OPERA I and II — time to first protocol-defined relapse (supportive to the ARR primary)

- Model type: Cox (HR) with a log-rank test. The SAP says all efficacy endpoints are analyzed stratified by region and baseline EDSS, but stratified-vs-covariate use for this endpoint is not stated.
- Stratification: region (US vs ROW) and baseline EDSS (<4.0 vs ≥4.0), from the SAP general statement.
- Covariates: treatment (otherwise Not stated).
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: log-rank p-value; Cox HR.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: Not stated.
- Interim/sample size: N/A (the trials were powered on ARR).
- Software: Not stated for this endpoint.
- Result: log-rank p<0.0001 in both studies. The FDA review reports "hazard ratio from the Cox model was 0.536 for both Studies". 0.536 is also the WA21092 ARR rate ratio, so this figure may be a transcription error (not verified).
- FDA comments: none beyond reporting.
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.5.1; OPERA SAP v5 §4.4.3.1.1 (OLE) and general stratification statement.

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The log-rank test for the time to first PDR yielded a p-value of < 0.0001 for both studies. The hazard ratio from the Cox model was 0.536 for both Studies WA21092 and WA21093."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 24 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761053Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Time to the first protocol defined relapse will also be analyzed during the DB and OLE period. Hazard ratio between randomized arms based on the Cox model, p-value based on the log-rank test and Kaplan-Meier estimates will be presented."
>
> — OPERA I/II SAP v5 §4.4.3.1.1, PDF p. 50 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/33/NCT01412333/SAP_001.pdf)

> "All primary and secondary efficacy endpoints will be analyzed stratified by geographical region (United States vs. ROW) and baseline EDSS (< 4.0 vs. ≥ 4.0)."
>
> — OPERA I/II SAP v5 §4.4, PDF p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/33/NCT01412333/SAP_001.pdf)

#### Model 2: OPERA I+II pooled — time to 12-week confirmed disability progression (first key secondary; pooled)

- Model type: stratified Cox.
- Stratification: region (US vs ROW) and baseline EDSS (<4.0 vs ≥4.0), the same strata as the stratified log-rank test.
- Covariates: treatment group only. A sensitivity analysis added relapses in the prior 2 years, baseline Gd lesions, prior MS treatment, and age (<40 vs ≥40).
- Ties: Not stated (`ties=` not specified in the PHREG code, so the SAS default applies; not stated in the documents).
- CI/test: two-sided stratified log-rank test (the p-value) and the Cox HR with Wald-type CI via `/ rl`. Alpha 0.05 within the hierarchy, with the pooled analysis as the confirmatory test.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated. Pooling of the two studies was not modeled with a study term or stratum in the code shown.
- Censoring: patients without CDP by Week 96, early discontinuation, or loss to follow-up were censored at the last EDSS in the double-blind period. In the primary analysis, discontinued patients with an initial progression were counted as confirmed. SAP sensitivity analyses used 50% multiple imputation (m=1000) and 100% imputation.
- Interim/sample size: the studies were pooled because each alone was underpowered for disability (about 800 per arm needed).
- Software: SAS PROC LIFETEST and PROC PHREG (SAP sample code, "draft").
- Result: pooled 12-week CDP 9.75% vs 15.18%, HR 0.60, p=0.0006. Per study: WA21092 31/410 vs 50/411, HR 0.57, p=0.0139; WA21093 44/417 vs 63/418, HR 0.63, p=0.0169.
- FDA comments: the reviewer judged imputing confirmed CDP for dropouts biased toward ocrelizumab, because interferon had more discontinuations. The reviewer re-ran the analysis censoring at discontinuation: HR 0.589 (p=0.0195) for WA21092 and 0.681 (p=0.0511) for WA21093.
- Spec source: OPERA I/II SAP v5 §4.4.2.3; FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.6.

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Time to confirmed disability progression in the ocrelizumab group and in the interferon beta-1a 44 μg SC group will be compared using a two-sided log-rank test stratifying by geographical region (United States vs. ROW), and baseline EDSS (< 4.0 vs. ≥ 4.0). The proportion of patients with confirmed disability progression will be estimated using Kaplan-Meier methodology. A by-treatment Kaplan-Meier plot will be presented for this endpoint. The overall hazard ratio will be estimated using a stratified Cox regression model with treatment group as covariate and the same stratification factors used in the stratified log-rank test above."
>
> — OPERA I/II SAP v5 §4.4.2.3, PDF p. 38 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/33/NCT01412333/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
* Log-rank test;
    proc lifetest data=CDP12;
        time CDP12TIME*CNSR(1);
        strata REGION BEDSSCAT / group=ARMCD;
        ods output HomTests =_logrank;
    run;
* Cox regression model;
proc phreg data=CDP12;
[... page header omitted ...]
        class ARMCD / descending;
        model CDP12TIME*CNSR(1) = ARMCD / rl;
        strata REGION BEDSSCAT;
        ods output ParameterEstimates=est;
    run;
```
— OPERA I/II SAP v5 §4.4.2.3, PDF pp. 38–39 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/33/NCT01412333/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Sensitivity analysis will use the same tests above but will, in addition, adjust for the number of relapses occurring within a 2-year period prior to study entry, baseline presence of Gd lesions (present or absent), prior MS treatment, and age (< 40 vs. ≥ 40 years)."
>
> — OPERA I/II SAP v5 §4.4.2.3, PDF p. 39 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/33/NCT01412333/SAP_001.pdf)

> "For disability related endpoints (CDP at 12 weeks, CDI at 12 weeks and CDP at 24 weeks) data from the 2 studies WA01292 and WA01293 were to be pooled together in the analysis as the two studies were not sufficiently powered to detect treatment difference by each individual study."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 19 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761053Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Instead of assuming all initial disability progressions were confirmed for patients who discontinued, an opposite assumption was made that no initial disability progression was confirmation after discontinuation, i.e., patients who discontinued before confirmation could be made were censored at discontinuation."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.6.2, PDF p. 29 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761053Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 3: OPERA I+II pooled — time to 24-week confirmed disability progression (key secondary; pooled)

- Stratification: region (US vs ROW) and baseline EDSS (<4.0 vs ≥4.0).

- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.

> "In the pooled analysis from Studies WA21092 and WA21093, treatment with ocrelizumab showed a 40% risk reduction in both 12-week CDP (hazard ratio=0.60; p=0.0006) and 24-week CDP (hazard ratio=0.60; p=0.0025) compared with interferon beta-1a."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 27 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761053Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 4: ORATORIO — time to 12-week confirmed disability progression (primary)

- Model type: stratified Cox (HR), with a stratified log-rank test as the primary test.
- Stratification: region (US vs ROW) and age (<45 vs ≥45), the same as the log-rank strata and the randomization strata.
- Covariates: treatment group only. Sensitivity analysis 6 added strata for baseline Gd-enhancing T1 lesions and baseline EDSS (5.5 cut-point; inequality symbols lost in text extraction).
- Ties: Not stated (`ties=` not specified in the code).
- CI/test: two-sided stratified log-rank (alpha 0.05); Cox HR with CI (`rl`).
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: none pre-specified. The FDA reviewer did informal at-risk landmark re-fits from Weeks 24, 48, 72, 96, and 120, which showed attenuation after Week 24 (HR 0.759 overall, then 0.858, 0.852, 0.806, 0.634, 0.464).
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: patients without initial progression were censored at the last EDSS in the treatment period. Initial progression without confirmation while still on treatment at database lock was censored at the last EDSS. Discontinuation after initial progression with no confirmatory EDSS was counted as confirmed CDP (an "imputed" event). Sensitivity analyses used 50% multiple imputation (m=1000) and treated such patients as non-events.
- Interim/sample size: assumed 2-year progression of 30% vs 43% (HR 0.635), exponential survival and dropout, 2:1 allocation, 20% dropout. Planned N=630 and 253 events (80% power at alpha 0.01 / about 90% at 0.05). The actual N was 732 because of a late screening boost; FDA's CDTL called this off-protocol.
- Software: SAS PROC LIFETEST and PROC PHREG (SAP sample code).
- Result: 160/487 (32.9%) vs 96/244 (39.3%), HR 0.76, p=0.0321 (log-rank). Without imputation: HR 0.82 (0.63, 1.07), p=0.1477.
- FDA comments: 21 of 256 events were imputed (12.5% of placebo events vs 5.6% of ocrelizumab events), and significance was lost without imputation. Excluding an OAI inspection site gave HR 0.769 and log-rank p=0.0454. Excluding two dispensing-error patients gave HR 0.766 and p=0.0384. The addendum re-censored 5 of the 21 imputed events at random 500 times; mean p=0.050 (range 0.0177–0.0931). The CDTL concluded "the PPMS trial is not well controlled".
- Spec source: ORATORIO SAP v5 §2.2, §4.5.1, §4.5.4; FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2 and Addendum; Medical Review package (CDTL).

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The overall hazard ratio will be estimated using a stratified Cox regression model with the same stratification factors used in the aforementioned stratified log-rank test."
>
> — ORATORIO SAP v5 §4.5.1, PDF p. 28 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/70/NCT01194570/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
* Log-rank test;
    proc lifetest data=CDP12;
        time CDP12TIME*CNSR(1);
        strata REGION AGE45 / group=ARMCD;
        ods output HomTests =_logrank;
    run;

* Cox regression model;
proc phreg data=CDP12;
        class ARMCD / descending;
        model CDP12TIME*CNSR(1) = ARMCD / rl;
        strata REGION AGE45;
        ods output ParameterEstimates=est;
    run;
```
— ORATORIO SAP v5 §4.5.1, PDF p. 28 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/70/NCT01194570/SAP_001.pdf)

#### Model 5: ORATORIO — time to 24-week confirmed disability progression (first secondary)

- Model type: stratified Cox, with a stratified log-rank test (as for the primary analysis).
- Stratification: region (US vs ROW) and age (<45 vs ≥45).
- Covariates: treatment only.
- Ties: Not stated.
- CI/test: stratified log-rank; Cox HR with 95% CI.
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated.
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated.
- Censoring: as for the primary analysis (imputed events for dropouts after initial progression); confirmation at least 24 weeks (≥161 days) later.
- Interim/sample size: N/A.
- Software: SAS (by reference to the primary analysis).
- Result: HR 0.75 (0.58, 0.98), p=0.0365. Without imputation: HR 0.82, p=0.1884.
- FDA comments: the same imputation issue as the primary analysis ("almost identical ... with the same issues").
- Spec source: ORATORIO SAP v5 §4.5.2.1; FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.5.2 and §3.2.2.6.1.

### Siponimod (Mayzent) — NDA 209884

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry Sponsor: Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation Approval year: 2019 Phase-3 trial(s): EXPAND (CBAF312A2304, NCT01665144), Phase 3

#### Model 1: EXPAND (A2304, NCT01665144), Phase 3 — Time to 3-month confirmed disability progression (EDSS) (Primary)

- Model type: standard Cox (covariate-adjusted, unstratified)
- Stratification: None in model (randomization stratified by country; country entered as covariate)
- Covariates: Treatment, country (country/region), baseline EDSS, SPMS group (with/without superimposed relapses in the 2 years prior to screening)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI and p-value; two-sided significance level 0.0434 (O'Brien-Fleming-adjusted); KM and log-rank also performed (log-rank p=0.0129 incl. 4 patients with missing covariate). Wald/score/likelihood-ratio not stated
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Patients without 3-month CDP censored at date of last EDSS assessment; data after switch to open-label siponimod included in primary analysis; no imputation for discontinuation before confirmation (sensitivity analysis assumed CDP)
- Interim/sample size: Event-driven: 374 3-month CDP events; 90% power for HR 0.70 by 2-sided 5% log-rank, 2:1 randomization, ~1530 patients; futility-only interim (DMC 14-Jul-2015 at >60% of events; efficacy stopping dropped); final alpha 0.0434 per O'Brien-Fleming spending; study duration extended post-interim (protocol amendment 3)
- Software: Not stated (FDA clinical reviewer used JMP for KM/log-rank re-analysis)
- Result: Siponimod 288/1096 (26.3%) vs placebo 173/545 (31.7%); HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.65-0.95), p=0.0134 (21.2% risk reduction); confirmed by FDA reviewer; 4 patients excluded for missing prior-relapse covariate
- FDA comments: Reviewer: post-interim extension increasing events could compromise type I error without adjustment; dual-database blinding breach (see Model 6); FDA inspection questioned SPMS entry criteria; effect on CDP may be partly mediated by strong relapse effect (see Model 5)
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.2 (decoded); FDA Clinical Review "Endpoints"/"Power"

### Ozanimod (Zeposia) — NDA 209899

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry Sponsor: Celgene Corporation (Bristol-Myers Squibb) Approval year: 2020 Phase-3 trial(s): SUNBEAM (RPC01-301, NCT02294058), Phase 3; RADIANCE Part B (RPC01-201B, NCT02047734), Phase 3 portion of a Phase 2/3 protocol

#### Model 1: SUNBEAM (RPC01-301) + RADIANCE Part B (RPC01-201B), pooled — Time to onset of disability progression confirmed at 3 months and at 6 months (EDSS ≥1.0) (Key secondary (3rd ranked; pre-specified pooled analysis))

- Model type: standard Cox (covariate-adjusted)
- Stratification: Not stated (randomization stratified by baseline EDSS and country per README)
- Covariates: Region, age, baseline EDSS score (plus treatment)
- Ties: Not stated for pooled analysis (RADIANCE SAP specifies Efron; pooling plan not public)
- CI/test: Log-rank test primary for hypothesis test; Cox HR with 95% CI; each ozanimod dose vs IFN β-1a within hierarchical testing (1 mg before 0.5 mg)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at later of last EDSS assessment or last dose if follow-up ended before sustained progression; death due to MS counted as confirmed progression; 3-month-confirmed but not 6-month-confirmed counted as event in 3-month and censored in 6-month analysis; withdrawal before first scheduled clinical visit censored at Baseline
- Interim/sample size: Pooling agreed with Division because individual studies lacked power for disability progression; no interim stated
- Software: SAS Version 9.1 or higher (RADIANCE SAP)
- Result: Pooled 3-month CDP: IFN 69/889, 0.5 mg 58/890 HR 0.86 (0.605-1.223) p=0.4024, 1 mg 67/880 HR 1.05 (0.747-1.463) p=0.7959; 6-month CDP: 36, 43, 51 events; HR 1.19 (0.764-1.852) p=0.4434 and 1.42 (0.927-2.175) p=0.1075 (FDA reviewer analysis)
- FDA comments: Reviewer judged pooling not appropriate given divergent direction in RADIANCE; pooled results presented without inferential statement; concluded no evidence of benefit on disability progression
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.3.2 and §3.2.1.5.2, Table 7; RADIANCE SAP §9 (decoded)

### Flortaucipir F18 (Tauvid) — NDA 212123

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry Sponsor: Avid Radiopharmaceuticals, Inc. (Eli Lilly) Approval year: 2020 Phase-3 trial(s): A16 (NCT02516046), FR01 (NCT03901092), A05C, PX01 — all Phase 3 single-arm diagnostic/prognostic imaging studies

#### Excluded

Flortaucipir F18 is excluded. All four Phase 3 studies were single-arm imaging studies with no randomized treatment comparison. The only Cox models are in the longitudinal prognostic studies A05C and PX01. There, a Cox model compares the hazard of a ≥1-point CDR-SB increase within 18 months between scan-read groups (τAD++ vs non-τAD++), adjusted for baseline age, ANART score and baseline CDR-SB. FDA describes A05C as an observational trial. This is a prognostic association model in single-arm studies, not a treatment-effect analysis, so it falls under the single-arm exclusion. A05C did not meet its prespecified success criteria, and the prognostic claim was not part of the approval.

> "This is a cross-sectional and longitudinal observational trial designed to confirm the relationship between FTP uptake in the brain as measured using FTP PET brain imaging and the subsequent rate of cognitive and functional decline observed over longitudinal follow-up."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (Ref ID 4615642), PDF p. 37 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212123Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Then the hazard ratio of τAD++ rated subjects progressing to the event when compared to non-τAD++ rated subjects along with the 95% CI was to be calculated. The Cox proportional hazard model was to be adjusted for baseline age, American National Adult Reading Test (ANART) scores, and baseline CDR-SB scores."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (Ref ID 4615642), PDF p. 40 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212123Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Inebilizumab-cdon (Uplizna) — BLA 761142

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry Sponsor: Viela Bio, Inc. Approval year: 2020 Phase-3 trial(s): N-MOmentum (CD-IA-MEDI-551-1155, NCT02200770), Phase 2/3

#### Model 1: N-MOmentum (CD-IA-MEDI-551-1155, NCT02200770) — Time to first AC-determined NMO/NMOSD attack through Day 197 — AQP4-IgG seropositive cohort (Primary (first hypothesis in sequence))

- Model type: standard Cox (unadjusted, treatment only)
- Stratification: None in model; randomization stratified by AQP4-IgG serostatus and region (Japan vs non-Japan); region indicator deliberately excluded from Cox model
- Covariates: Treatment indicator only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI; overall two-sided alpha 0.05 controlled by Bonferroni-based chain (graphical) procedure; test statistic type not stated
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at Day 197/discontinuation visit if no AC-determined attack; only attacks with assessment visit within 120 h of symptoms and assessments within 10 days counted; no imputation
- Interim/sample size: 67 AC-determined attacks for 90% power to detect 60% reduction (HR 0.4), two-sided 0.05, 3:1 randomization; simulation (5000 runs) gave 94% (overall) and 91% (seropositive) power; unmasked futility-only interim at ~34 (50%) attacks using Cox chi-square-based Z and predictive power (<20% in both populations); IDMC stopped trial early (43 attacks)
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG (SAP)
- Result: HR 0.227 (95% CI 0.1214-0.4232), p<0.0001; attacks 18/161 inebilizumab vs 22/52 placebo (summed from FDA subgroup Table 11)
- FDA comments: Clinical reviewer: with 3:1 randomization, IDMC likely aware of interim HR 0.18 (0.08-0.38) since early meetings and sponsor aware by Jan 2017; statistical reviewer: results driven by seropositive cohort; seronegative data insufficient
- Spec source: SAP Amendment 4 §4 primary efficacy analysis, Appendix 1 & 5 (decoded); FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2

### Satralizumab-mwge (Enspryng) — BLA 761149

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Genentech, Inc. (Roche); trials run by Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Approval year: 2020. Phase-3 trial(s): SAkuraSky (BN40898/SA-307JG, NCT02028884, Phase 3, add-on) and SAkuraStar (BN40900/SA-309JG, NCT02073279, Phase 3, monotherapy).

#### Model 1: SAkuraSky (BN40898/SA-307JG, NCT02028884, Phase 3) — time to first protocol-defined relapse (TFR/PDR) (primary endpoint; Cox for HR estimation; FDA labels it 'Secondary Analysis-Cox model')

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Baseline ARR (1 vs >1) and geographic region (Asia vs EU/Other), the randomization strata. Whether IxRS or CRF values were used is not stated
- Covariates: Treatment only (SAS code: model DURATION*STATUS(0)=TREATMENT). The SAP also specifies pairwise treatment-by-covariate interaction terms as an additional check
- Ties: Exact (ties=exact)
- CI/test: Wald CI for the HR (rl option); two-sided stratified log-rank test at alpha 0.05 is the primary test
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated. Treatment-by-covariate interactions were tested in the Cox model. No PH diagnostics were specified
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at the earliest of: end of the double-blind period, switching or increasing baseline treatment, or receiving rescue therapy for clinical relapse
- Interim/sample size: Event-driven: 26 TFR events; HR 0.335 (66.5% risk reduction); 80% power; two-sided log-rank at 5%; exponential placebo hazard 0.4184/yr; about 70 patients. FDA Appendix: Chugai staff used fibrinogen to guess treatment assignments and computed HRs in Nov 2015 and Jun 2017 (FDA Appendix Table 2: HR from assumed assignments NA in Nov 2015 and 0.35 in Jun 2017; HR from actual data 0.24 and 0.37 at those times). No formal alpha-spending interim analysis
- Software: SAS 9.2 or later; PROC PHREG (SAP Appendix 7.7)
- Result: HR 0.38 (95% CI 0.16, 0.88), Cox p=0.0231; log-rank p=0.0184; PDR 8/41 (19.5%) satralizumab vs 18/42 (42.9%) placebo (ITT; FDA reviewer analysis)
- FDA comments: Reviewer reproduced the result. The main FDA concern was the fibrinogen-based internal unblinding, which affected trial conduct, not the Cox specification itself
- Spec source: SAP v9.0 §5.10.1-5.10.2, §5.14, Appendix 7.7; FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1

```sas
proc phreg data=final;

    class TREATMENT/descending;

    Model DURATION*STATUS(0)=TREATMENT / ties=exact rl;

    strata ARR REGION;

    ods output parameterEstimates=est;

run;
```
— SAkuraSky SAP v9.0 Appendix 7.7 "SAS Codes: Cox Regression Model", PDF p. 58 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT02028884/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
proc lifetest data=final;

    time DURATION*STATUS (0);

    strata ARR REGEON / group=TREATMENT;

    ods output test=_logrank;

run;
```
— SAkuraSky SAP v9.0 Appendix 7.7 "SAS Codes: Log-rank test", PDF p. 58 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT02028884/SAP_001.pdf). The `REGEON` misspelling is in the source

#### Model 2: SAkuraSky — TFR under alternative relapse definitions (sensitivity)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Baseline ARR and geographic region (same as primary)
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Exact (same specification as primary)
- CI/test: Wald; stratified log-rank test reported alongside
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Same censoring rules as the primary endpoint, except for the specific event of interest
- Interim/sample size: N/A (sensitivity)
- Software: SAS (PROC PHREG)
- Result: FDA Table 4: all clinical relapses HR 0.59 (0.33, 1.08), p=0.0893; confirmed regardless of EDSS window HR 0.41 (0.19, 0.92), p=0.0304; treated clinical relapses HR 0.62 (0.34, 1.14), p=0.1270; treated optic neuritis HR 0.59 (0.23, 1.52), p=0.2720
- FDA comments: Reviewer attributes the non-significant sensitivity results to a higher CEC confirmation rate in placebo (66.7%) than in satralizumab (44.4%)
- Spec source: SAP v9.0 §5.10.2; FDA Statistical Review Table 4

#### Model 3: SAkuraStar (BN40900/SA-309JG, NCT02073279, Phase 3) — time to first protocol-defined relapse (primary endpoint; Cox for HR estimation)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Prior therapy for NMO/NMOSD attack prevention (B-cell depleting vs immunosuppressants/others) and most recent attack in the year before screening (first attack vs relapse). Source (IxRS/CRF) not stated
- Covariates: Treatment; pairwise treatment-by-covariate interactions assessed separately
- Ties: Exact
- CI/test: Wald CI; two-sided stratified log-rank test at 5% as primary test. Under an FDA Type C response (28 Mar 2017), the primary test changed from a permutation log-rank test to the asymptotic stratified log-rank test
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: No formal PH test. The sample size assumes a delayed effect (HR 1.0 for the first 2 months, then 0.25). Non-PH handling: Sensitivity analysis (added in SAP v7.0): stratified weighted log-rank test with Fleming-Harrington(0,1) weights 'adjusting for a change in the hazard ratio over time (i.e. non-proportional hazards)'
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at the end of the double-blind period. A sensitivity analysis also censors at the start of relapse-prevention therapy, rescue therapy, or systemic steroids for >5 days
- Interim/sample size: Event-driven: 44 TFR events (≥80% power, two-sided 5%, piecewise HR 1.0/0.25, placebo hazard 1.1295/yr, 10% 2-year dropout), about 90 patients 2:1. The SPA amendment of 9 Mar 2016 raised the target from 19 to 44 events and from 70 to 90 patients. The DB period ended at 1.5 years after the last patient was randomized (35 of 44 PDRs). Sponsor blinded data review allowed
- Software: SAS 9.2 or later (PROC LIFETEST code given; PROC PHREG code not shown)
- Result: HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.23, 0.89), Cox p=0.0215; log-rank p=0.0184; PDR 19/63 (30.2%) satralizumab vs 16/32 (50.0%) placebo
- FDA comments: FDA Statistical Review: the fibrinogen-based unblinding 'almost certain[ly]' affected trial conduct. The sample-size/event increase could not be shown to be independent of it. Under the original design (19 events), HR would have been 0.58, p=0.2413/0.2414
- Spec source: SAP v7.0 §4.10.2 (image-only pages, OCR), §4.14 (OCR), §5.5, Appendix 7.1; FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2; Medical Review

### Ublituximab-xiiy (Briumvi) — BLA 761238

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: TG Therapeutics, Inc. Approval year: 2022. Phase-3 trial(s): ULTIMATE I (TG1101-RMS301, NCT03277261, Phase 3) and ULTIMATE II (TG1101-RMS302, NCT03277248, Phase 3).

#### Model 1: ULTIMATE I (TG1101-RMS301, NCT03277261, Phase 3) — time to first IRAP-confirmed relapse (sensitivity for ARR primary)

- Model type: Standard (unstratified) Cox with covariates
- Stratification: None stated (the README describes a 'stratified Cox model', but the SAP and FDA review describe covariate adjustment only)
- Covariates: Treatment, region, number of relapses in the previous year, baseline EDSS strata (≤3.5 vs >3.5), baseline number of T1 Gd-enhancing lesions, sex, age at baseline. The protocol lists 'baseline EDSS score' instead of EDSS strata
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Not stated
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Time from randomization to relapse onset (+1 day); censored at end of treatment (protocol §8.9.4)
- Interim/sample size: Blinded sample-size re-estimation based on pooled ARR (BART, 15 Oct 2020; +30/arm). Not HR-based
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.33, 0.75), p=0.0009; relapse-free at 96 weeks 86.0% vs 74.4% (ublituximab vs teriflunomide). CSR, confirmed by the FDA reviewer
- FDA comments: Confirmed by reviewer; no critique of the Cox model
- Spec source: SAP v3.0 §2.4.2 Sensitivity Analysis item 2 (OCR); Protocol v5.0 §8.9.3-8.9.4 (OCR); FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1

- Interim/sample size: As ULTIMATE I
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.28, 0.65), p<0.0001; relapse-free at 96 weeks 87.4% vs 72.1%
- FDA comments: Confirmed by reviewer
- Spec source: ULTIMATE II SAP v3.0 §2.4.2 (OCR); FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "A time to relapses analysis using Cox proportional hazards model with first IRAP-confirmed relapse as the primary event will be conducted to compare with the primary analysis in a negative binomial model."
>
> — ULTIMATE II (TG1101-RMS302) SAP v3.0 §2.4.2 Sensitivity Analysis (OCR; text layer garbled) [OCR], PDF p. 25 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/48/NCT03277248/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Hazard Ratio (Ublituximab/Teriflunomide) 0.43 (0.28, 0.65) P-value <0.0001"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761238 Study 302 efficacy table, PDF p. 16 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761238Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 3: ULTIMATE I + II pooled — time to 12-week confirmed disability progression (key secondary, gatekept); HR reported, estimating model not specified

- Model type: HR reported alongside stratified log-rank test; the HR model (presumably Cox) is not specified in the available documents. Pooled analysis defined in an unavailable master SAP (11 Nov 2020)
- Stratification: Log-rank stratified by region, baseline EDSS strata and study
- Covariates: Not stated
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Not stated
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at the last scheduled EDSS assessment if no event
- Interim/sample size: Confirmatory only if ARR and both MRI endpoints were significant in both trials
- Software: Not stated
- Result: 12-week CDP: 28/543 (5.2%) vs 32/546 (5.9%); HR 0.843 (95% CI 0.504, 1.407), p=0.5099 (not significant, so all later secondary endpoints were not formally tested). 24-week CDP (exploratory): HR 0.657, nominal p=0.1716
- FDA comments: Summary Review: a superiority design against an active comparator with known disability efficacy, and so few events, could not support any claim of equivalence
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1, Table 5; FDA Summary Review; per-study SAP §2.4.3.5 (OCR) only specifies KM

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The master SAP was dated November 11, 2020 which specified the analysis of the time to confirmed disability progression using pooled data of the 2 studies."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761238 §3.2.1, PDF p. 6 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761238Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The time to onset of CDP was compared between treatment using a log-rank test stratified by region, baseline EDSS strata and study."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761238 §3.2.1, PDF p. 9 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761238Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "If no event occurs, the time to CDP is regarded as censored at the last scheduled EDSS assessment."
>
> — ULTIMATE I (TG1101-RMS301) SAP v3.0 §2.4.3.5 (OCR; text layer garbled) [OCR], PDF p. 30 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/61/NCT03277261/SAP_001.pdf)

> "time to CDP for at least 12 weeks was not statistically significant using a stratified log-rank test (hazard ratio =0.843, p=0.5099; Table 5)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761238 §3.2.3.2, PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761238Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The applicant provided an exploratory analysis of time to 24-week confirmed disability which was also not significant (hazard ratio 0.657, nominal p=0.1716)"

## Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic

### Icatibant (Firazyr) — NDA 22150

Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic. Sponsor: Shire Orphan Therapies, Inc. (originally Jerini US, Inc.). Approval year: 2011. Phase-3 trial(s): FAST-1 (JE049-2103, NCT00097695, Phase 3), FAST-2 (JE049-2102, NCT00500656, Phase 3), FAST-3 (HGT-FIR-054, NCT00912093, Phase 3).

#### Model 1: FAST-3 (HGT-FIR-054, NCT00912093, Phase 3) — time to onset of symptom relief (composite VAS-3) (supportive analysis of the primary endpoint)

- Model type: Standard Cox with covariates
- Stratification: None as a strata statement. The randomization stratification factors (symptom type, prior C1-INH use; stochastic minimization) enter as covariates
- Covariates: Treatment, stratification factors, edema location, previous use of C1-INH
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI and p-value (method not stated)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated. Non-PH handling: The primary test was Peto-Peto Wilcoxon, chosen because it 'gives more weight to earlier achievement of symptom relief'. A stratified Peto-Peto Wilcoxon was reported in parallel
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Patients without symptom relief were censored at the last observation time. A sensitivity analysis censored at rescue medication
- Interim/sample size: No interim. Sample size from Query Advisor, based on FAST-1 percentages without relief at 1-24 h
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR not reported in the FDA review. Primary: median 2.0 h vs 19.8 h, p<0.001
- FDA comments: None on the Cox model
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review (Hoberman 2011), Statistical Methodologies, PDF p. 18

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "To control for study design factors, time to symptom relief was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model which included covariates for treatment and stratification factors, edema location and previous use of C1-INH."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review(s), NDA 22150 Hoberman 2011 review, Statistical Methodologies, PDF p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The hazard ratio (icatibant - control), corresponding 95% confidence interval, and p-value assessing differences among treatment groups were presented for the non-laryngeal ITT population."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review(s), NDA 22150 Hoberman 2011 review, Statistical Methodologies, PDF p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "A Peto-Peto Wilcoxon test with a global 2-sided significance level of 5% was used to test the null hypothesis for the non-laryngeal ITT, non-laryngeal per-protocol, ITT, and laryngeal populations."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review(s), NDA 22150 Hoberman 2011 review, Statistical Methodologies, PDF p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Patients who did not achieve symptom relief within the observation period were censored at the last observation time."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review(s), NDA 22150 table footnote, PDF p. 5 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: FAST-1 (JE049-2103) and FAST-2 (JE049-2102) (Phase 3) — time to onset of symptom relief, sponsor 'proportional hazard model' (supportive)

- Model type: Cox with (post-randomization) covariates
- Stratification: Not stated
- Covariates: Rescue medication use and time from first moderate symptom to treatment start (treatment term implied but not stated)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Not stated
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated. Non-PH handling: Primary analysis used Wilcoxon (Gehan-type). The reviewer also ran log-rank, stratified Wilcoxon and stratified log-rank tests
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at the last assessment if no relief
- Interim/sample size: None. 40 evaluable per arm; log-rank, 80% power, no effect size stated
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Not stated
- FDA comments: FDA reviewer (Li 2008) rejected the analysis because rescue medication use is a post-randomization consequence of treatment
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review (Li 2008), Statistical methods, PDF p. 37

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "A proportional hazard model was used including the rescue medication use and the time from the first symptom to treatment start as covariates. This reviewer did not think that this analysis was appropriate as the use of rescue medication was the consequence of the treatments."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review(s), NDA 22150 Li 2008 review, Statistical methods, PDF p. 37 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Wilcoxon log-rank test was used to analyze the time from treatment to the symptom relief."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review(s), NDA 22150 Li 2008 review, Statistical methods, PDF p. 36 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 3: FAST-1 and FAST-2 — FDA reviewer Andersen-Gill multivariate survival model of time to relief of all baseline symptoms (exploratory)

- Model type: Andersen-Gill (multivariate/recurrent-type Cox)
- Stratification: Not stated
- Covariates: Not stated
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: p-value only
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored if relief not achieved
- Interim/sample size: N/A
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Andersen-Gill p<0.001 in both Study 2103 and Study 2102 (Table 7)
- FDA comments: Reviewer called it 'only an exploratory analysis' because of concerns about assessing all symptoms by VAS and about symptoms that emerged after treatment
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review (Li 2008), Executive Summary and §3 Table 7, PDF pp. 34, 41

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "this reviewer explored to perform multivariate survival analyses including all the symptoms at pre-dose. Anderson-Gill model was used appropriate for these analyses."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review(s), NDA 22150 Li 2008 review, §3, PDF p. 41 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "This reviewer considered this only an exploratory analysis since there were concerns on if it was appropriate to assess all the symptoms using VAS."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review(s), NDA 22150 Li 2008 review, Executive Summary, PDF p. 34 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2011/022150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Givinostat (Duvyzat) — NDA 217865

Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic. Sponsor: Italfarmaco S.p.A. Approval year: 2024. Phase-3 trial(s): EPIDYS (DSC/14/2357/48, NCT02851797, Phase 3).

#### Model 1: EPIDYS (NCT02851797, Phase 3) — time to 10% persistent worsening in 6MWT (secondary)

- Model type: Standard Cox with covariates
- Stratification: None in the model. Randomization stratified by concomitant steroid regimen (4 strata), which enters as a classification covariate
- Covariates: Randomized treatment, concomitant steroid use (classification factors), baseline 4SC, time to rise from floor, time to run/walk 10 m, 6MWT distance, re-derived age at first dose
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: 2-sided CI and p-value (alpha-adjusted where §4.4.5 applies)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at the last 6MWT assessment (including imputed), i.e., Month 18, if no persistent worsening
- Interim/sample size: Not HR-based
- Software: SAS 9.2 or higher
- Result: Not stated in available documents
- FDA comments: No FDA comment on this Cox model. The Integrated Review's HRs (persistent loss of rise from floor, 4SC, ambulation) are from an applicant comparison with external natural-history data, not EPIDYS
- Spec source: SAP v6.0 §4.3.5, §4.4.2 Modelling Methods

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The time to event variables (time to 10% persistent worsening in 6MWT, time to persistent loss of standing) will be analysed using Cox proportional hazards modelling, including baseline values for: 4SC, time to rise from floor, time to run/walk 10 metres, distance walked in 6 minutes and re-derived age at first dose (in years and months) as independent covariates and randomised treatment group and concomitant steroid"
>
> — EPIDYS (DSC/14/2357/48) SAP v6.0 §4.4.2 Modelling Methods, PDF p. 29 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT02851797/SAP_001.pdf)

> "use as independent classification factors. The hazard ratio will be presented, together with its associated 2-sided CI and p-value."
>
> — EPIDYS (DSC/14/2357/48) SAP v6.0 §4.4.2 Modelling Methods, PDF p. 30 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT02851797/SAP_001.pdf)

> "If a subject has not achieved ≥10% persistent worsening in 6MWT, then time to 10% persistent worsening in 6MWT will be censored at the date of the last 6MWT assessment (including imputed assessments per Section 4.4.4.1), i.e. the 18 month assessment."
>
> — EPIDYS (DSC/14/2357/48) SAP v6.0 §4.3.5, PDF p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT02851797/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The analysis and statistical reporting will be conducted at Veristat using SAS version 9.2 or higher."

## Immunology / Rheumatology / Dermatology

### Belatacept (Nulojix) — BLA 125288

Therapeutic area: Immunology / Rheumatology / Dermatology Sponsor: Bristol-Myers Squibb Approval year: 2011 Phase-3 trial(s): BENEFIT (NCT00256750) and BENEFIT-EXT (NCT00114777), Phase 3

**Excluded.** No Cox proportional-hazards model was found in any accessible source. The three co-primary endpoints (patient/graft survival, composite renal impairment, acute rejection) are Month-12 proportions compared as differences with 97.3% CIs in the label. The FDA Statistical, Medical and Summary Reviews are almost entirely withheld under (b)(4): the Statistical Review text layer holds only a cover page and a filing checklist. The BENEFIT and BENEFIT-EXT publications (Am J Transplant 2010) are not open access, and their PubMed abstracts do not mention Cox or hazard ratios. ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted protocol or SAP.

> "Efficacy failure at one year was defined as the occurrence of biopsy proven acute rejection (BPAR), graft loss, death, or lost to follow-up."
>
> — Nulojix Package Insert (2011), PDF p. 31 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/125288s0000lbl.pdf)

> "Patient and graft survival was 98% (198/202) in NULOJIX-treated patients and 92% (170/184) in cyclosporine-treated patients"
>
> — Nulojix Package Insert (2011), PDF p. 33 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/125288s0000lbl.pdf)

### Anacaulase-bcdb (NexoBrid) — BLA 761192

Therapeutic area: Other / Misc Sponsor: MediWound Ltd. Approval year: 2022 Phase-3 trial(s): DETECT (MW2010-03-02, NCT02148705), Phase 3 pivotal; Study MW2004-11-02 ("Study 2004"), Phase 3 supportive

#### Model 1: DETECT (MW2010-03-02, NCT02148705) — Time to complete eschar removal (NexoBrid vs SOC), patient level (Secondary)

- Model type: Standard Cox (covariate-adjusted), conditional on PH; PH test via time-dependent treatment interaction
- Stratification: None in the Cox model; the Gehan fallback stratifies by depth group, number of TWs, %TBSA group, center group
- Covariates: Treatment, overall TW depth (all FT / mixed / all DPT), total %TBSA per patient, center group (Non-surgical, Mixed, Surgical, West, East), number of TWs (1, 2, ≥3)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Wald z-test (treatment coefficient / SE vs standard normal)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Time-since-randomization x treatment interaction term in the Cox model; the PH assumption is rejected if p<0.05 / Pre-specified switch to a generalized Wilcoxon-Gehan test (PROC LIFETEST, stratified). PH was rejected (interaction p<0.0001), so Gehan was used
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Patients without complete eschar removal censored at the last non-missing eschar removal assessment (typically the last debridement)
- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: SAS (PROC LIFETEST code given; Cox procedure not named)
- Result: The Cox model was not used for inference. Gehan test: median 1.02 vs 3.83 days, statistic 23.14, p<0.0001 (N=75 per arm, FAS)
- FDA comments: The reviewer describes how the applicant rejected PH and used the Gehan test; no objection raised.
- Spec source: DETECT SAP V03 §11.1.3.2; FDA MDR

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The treatment groups will be compared using a Cox regression model. The comparison will be adjusted for the explanatory variables overall TW"
>
> — DETECT (MW2010-03-02) SAP V03, 29 Nov 2018, PDF p. 86 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02148705/SAP_005.pdf)

> "The treatment groups will be compared by testing the null hypothesis of no difference, comparing the ratio of the estimated treatment coefficient to its standard error to a standard normal distribution."
>
> — DETECT (MW2010-03-02) SAP V03, 29 Nov 2018, PDF p. 87 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02148705/SAP_005.pdf)

> "This will be checked by including in the regression model a variable representing the interaction between time since randomization and treatment group. If the coefficient for this time variable is non-significant at the 5% significance level, then the Cox Regression analysis will be adopted."
>
> — DETECT (MW2010-03-02) SAP V03, 29 Nov 2018, PDF p. 87 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02148705/SAP_005.pdf)

```sas
PROC LIFETEST DATA=burn_data; TIME time*status(0); STRATA depthgroup numtw tbsagroup centergroup / GROUP = treatment_group; RUN;
```
— DETECT (MW2010-03-02) SAP V03, 29 Nov 2018, PDF p. 87 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02148705/SAP_005.pdf)

> "When this analysis was conducted, the p-value for the interaction term was <0.0001. Thus, the applicant rejected the proportional hazards assumption and analyzed the endpoint with a generalized Wilcoxon-Gehan test"
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review, BLA 761192, PDF p. 118 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761192Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 2: DETECT (MW2010-03-02, NCT02148705) — Time to ≥95% wound closure (wound level; non-inferiority with a 7-day margin) (Safety endpoint (NI))

- Model type: Marginal Cox (clustered wounds within patient), conditional on PH; fallback is an AFT model with shared frailty
- Stratification: None
- Covariates: Treatment, TW depth (wound level), %TBSA (wound level), number of TWs (1, 2, ≥3); a time x treatment interaction for the PH check
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Not stated
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Time-since-randomization x treatment interaction (p<0.05 means non-PH) / Log-logistic AFT model with a normal random subject effect (PROC NLMIXED). PH was rejected (p<0.0001) and the AFT model was used
- Robust variance / frailty: Robust sandwich variance (Binder) via COVS(AGGREGATE) in PHREG; the fallback uses a shared frailty (random subject effect)
- Censoring: Missing data censored. The NI margin was built in by adding 7 days to SOC closure times
- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG (COVS(AGGREGATE) robust variance); PROC LIFETEST for Gehan fallback; PROC NLMIXED for AFT shared frailty
- Result: The Cox model was not used. Median time to ≥95% closure was 27 days (NexoBrid) vs 28 days (SOC); FDA called the AFT result uninterpretable
- FDA comments: FDA strongly disagreed. Adding a 7-day constant to SOC times does not give a valid NI test for hazard-ratio or AFT parameters. The AFT model was not fully pre-specified (no parametric family justification, no handling of zero follow-up times). FDA used subgroup medians instead of a model and recommended a per-subject analysis of 100% closure.
- Spec source: DETECT SAP V03 §11.1.4.1; FDA MDR

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "If the coefficient for this time variable is non-significant at the 5% significance level, then the proportional hazards assumption will be considered appropriate. In this case we will use a marginal Cox regression analysis with a robust sandwich estimator. If not, then we will use an accelerated failure time (AFT) model with shared frailty."
>
> — DETECT (MW2010-03-02) SAP V03, 29 Nov 2018, PDF p. 90 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02148705/SAP_005.pdf)

> "The marginal Cox regression model is implemented in the PHREG procedure and the robust variance option is implemented by specifying the COVS(AGGREGATE) option. This induces the use of the robust variance method of Binder et. al. [34]."
>
> — DETECT (MW2010-03-02) SAP V03, 29 Nov 2018, PDF p. 90 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02148705/SAP_005.pdf)

```sas
PROC NLMIXED DATA=burn_data; BOUNDS gamma>0; linp = b0 + b1*treatment_group + b2*spt + b3*dpt + b4*ft + b5*tbsa + b6*number_tw2+ b7*number_tw3 + b8*center2 + b9*center3 + b10*center4 + b11*center5 + z; alpha = exp(-linp); G_t = 1/(1+alpha*time**gamma); g = alpha*gamma*time**(gamma-1)/(1+alpha*time**gamma)**2; ll = (censor=0)*log(g) + (censor=1)*log(G_t); model time~general(ll); RANDOM z ~ normal(0,sigma) subject=subject_id; RUN;
```
— DETECT (MW2010-03-02) SAP V03, 29 Nov 2018, PDF p. 90 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02148705/SAP_005.pdf)

> "This is clearly not the case for time to event endpoints, where Cox regression assumes that the hazards are proportional, and the accelerated failure time model assumes the survival functions differ by an acceleration factor on the time scale."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review, BLA 761192, PDF p. 109 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761192Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The applicant rejected the proportional hazards assumption, because the coefficient of the time- treatment interaction was significant at the 0.05 level (p <0.0001)."
>
> — FDA Multi-disciplinary Review, BLA 761192, PDF p. 127 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761192Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

### Ensifentrine (Ohtuvayre) — NDA 217389

Therapeutic area: Other / Misc Sponsor: Verona Pharma, Inc. Approval year: 2024 Phase-3 trial(s): ENHANCE-1 (RPL554-CO-301, NCT04535986) and ENHANCE-2 (RPL554-CO-302, NCT04542057), Phase 3

#### Model 1: ENHANCE-1 (RPL554-CO-301, NCT04535986) — Time to first moderate/severe COPD exacerbation (all patients, truncated at Week 24, 48-week stratum) (Sensitivity analysis to the stratified log-rank test (an 'other' endpoint outside the multiplicity hierarchy))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Region, background medication strata, smoking strata (SAP; the log-rank uses 'actual' strata)
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Primary test is a stratified log-rank test; the Cox model gives the HR and 95% CI (publication reports a separate p-value)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: SAP: check covariate independence via PROC PHREG; log(-log(survival)) vs log(time) plot; treatment x log(time) interaction test. Publication: 'interaction tests were not significant'. / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Patients without exacerbations censored at last day in the treatment period, including post-withdrawal recording; follow-up-period events excluded
- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG (named for the assumption check); FDA used SAS 9.4
- Result: Week 24: HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.39, 0.97), p=0.038; events/N ENS 38/477 vs PBO 36/283. Week 48 stratum: HR 0.48 (0.28, 0.82), ENS 35/280 vs PBO 21/89
- FDA comments: The FDA confirmed the HRs but called the results exploratory, outside the hierarchy, based on few events in a population that rarely exacerbates, and of unclear clinical relevance.
- Spec source: ENHANCE-1 SAP §16.3.4 (OCR); FDA IR; Anzueto 2023

### Nerandomilast (Jascayd) — NDA 218764

Therapeutic area: Other / Misc Sponsor: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Approval year: 2025 Phase-3 trial(s): FIBRONEER-IPF (1305-0014, NCT05321069), Phase 3. FIBRONEER-ILD (NCT05321082) is out of this entry's scope

#### Model 1: FIBRONEER-IPF (1305-0014, NCT05321069) — Time to first acute IPF exacerbation, first hospitalization for respiratory cause, or death (over the whole trial) (Key secondary (graphical multiplicity procedure across 2 doses))

- Model type: Standard Cox (covariate-adjusted)
- Stratification: None stated
- Covariates: Treatment, baseline antifibrotic (AF) therapy, age (continuous), baseline FVC % predicted, baseline DLCO % predicted (Hb-corrected)
- Ties: Breslow
- CI/test: Two-sided Wald test for the treatment effect; HR with 95% CI
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at the last day known event-free; censored at lung transplant; same-day events ordered as exacerbation, then hospitalization, then death
- Interim/sample size: Power for HR 0.60-0.75 with assumed 15-20% placebo 52-week event proportions: 37-46% (HR 0.75) to 79-89% (HR 0.6). Interim analysis for futility of the 9 mg dose
- Software: Not stated
- Result: DBL1 (up to 91 weeks): 9 mg HR 1.03 (0.75, 1.41), p=0.8568, 79/392 events; 18 mg HR 1.17 (0.86, 1.59), p=0.3102, 85/392; placebo 80/393
- FDA comments: FDA disagreed that lung transplant should not count as an intercurrent event, but agreed that censoring at transplant is reasonable. Unblinded DBL2 data were set aside as not pre-specified.
- Spec source: TSAP v2.0 §7.5.1.1; FDA IR §6.2.1.5.4, §15.1.5.7
