## Hematology

### Peginesatide (Omontys) — NDA 202799

Therapeutic area: Hematology Sponsor: Affymax, Inc. (with Takeda) Approval year: 2012 Phase-3 trial(s): EMERALD 1/2 (AFX01-12, AFX01-14; dialysis) and PEARL 1/2 (AFX01-11, AFX01-13; non-dialysis), all Phase 3

#### Model 1: Pooled EMERALD 1/2 + PEARL 1/2 (AFX01-12, -14, -11, -13) — Time to first adjudicated composite safety endpoint (CSE: death, stroke, MI, serious CHF, unstable angina, arrhythmia) (Primary safety (pooled CV non-inferiority, margin HR 1.3))

- Model type: Stratified Cox per study; inverse-variance meta-analytic pooling of study log-HRs
- Stratification: Study-specific randomization stratification factors: screening Hb (≤10.4 vs ≥10.5 g/dL) and NYHA CHF class (0-1 vs ≥2), per IVRS; per-study models
- Covariates: Treatment
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: One-sided 95% CI (reported as a two-sided 90% CI) by normal approximation; upper bound <1.3. Secondary two-sided 95% CI requested by FDA (14 Jun 2007 meeting)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Non-death CSE events through study termination; deaths through 28 days after termination; non-event patients censored at study termination (on-study)
- Interim/sample size: Event-driven: 553 patients with CSE events needed to exclude HR >1.3 with 89% probability (one-sided 95% CI), assuming a 17.4% annual CSE rate, exponential times, 12-month accrual, ≥12-month follow-up, 5% annual dropout. Required 2400 patients (1600 peginesatide : 800 control)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Dialysis (AFX01-12+14): CSE HR 0.95 (90% CI 0.79, 1.13), 243/1066 vs 132/542. Non-dialysis (AFX01-11+13): CSE HR 1.32 (90% CI 1.02, 1.72), 141/656 vs 56/327. By study: AFX01-11 HR 1.07 (0.71, 1.61); AFX01-13 HR 1.58 (1.05, 2.38)
- FDA comments: The statistical reviewer judged non-dialysis results unfavorable to peginesatide. A reviewer analysis adding imbalanced baseline factors to the stratified Cox base model gave similar results. NYHA class was a stratification factor in all primary safety models.
- Spec source: FDA Statistical Review §3.3.3-3.3.4; Medical Review

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The primary statistical analysis of the CSE was the estimation of hazard ratios using stratified Cox regression for each study with the study-specific stratification factors, and then combining these estimates over studies using weights inversely proportionate to the variance of the study- specific log-hazard ratio estimates."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202799, PDF p. 41 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202799Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In the presentation of the statistics for this analysis, a two-sided 90% CI was provided (the one-sided 95% CI was obtained by use of the upper limit of the two-sided 90% CI)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202799, PDF p. 41 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202799Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "a total of 553 patients with CSE events were required for a one-sided 95% confidence interval to exclude a hazard ratio greater than 1.3 with 89% probability"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202799, PDF p. 40 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202799Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The hazard ratio along with the 95% confidence interval (one-sided or the comparable 90% two-sided interval) was calculated using Cox regression stratified by the randomization factors."
>
> — FDA Medical Review, NDA 202799, PDF p. 90 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202799Orig1s000MedR.pdf)

> "The base model we used was the primary model, which is Cox regression model stratified by study adjusting stratification variables. And then we added these imbalanced baseline factors either separately each time or both of them at the same time into the base model"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, NDA 202799, PDF p. 46 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/202799Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Caplacizumab-yhdp (Cablivi) — BLA 761112

Therapeutic area: Hematology Sponsor: Ablynx NV Approval year: 2019 Phase-3 trial(s): HERCULES (ALX0681-C301, NCT02553317), Phase 3

#### Model 1: HERCULES (ALX0681-C301, NCT02553317) — Time to platelet count response (≥150×10^9/L with stop of daily PE within 5 days) (Primary (HR accompanying stratified log-rank test))

- Model type: Standard Cox with the stratification factor as a covariate (not a strata statement)
- Stratification: Not in the Cox model; the log-rank test is stratified by GCS category (≤12 / 13-15)
- Covariates: Treatment group, GCS category
- Ties: Efron
- CI/test: Two-sided stratified log-rank test at α=0.05 decides; Cox gives HR with 95% CI (risklimits; estimate statements)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Lin, Wei & Ying (1993) cumulative martingale-residual score processes; graphical plus supremum test (ASSESS PH / RESAMPLE) / Expanded Cox with time interaction(s) (Part 3 of table shell); explore stratified PH models for rituximab use, baseline severity, baseline ADAMTS13
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at 45 days after first study drug if no response (any cause, e.g., not reached, lost to follow-up)
- Interim/sample size: No interim analyses. 132 subjects (121 events) give 80% power for a 40% reduction in time to response (placebo median 7 vs 4.2 days), two-sided log-rank α=0.05, 2.5-year accrual, 10% early dropout
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG / PROC LIFETEST
- Result: Label: stratified log-rank p=0.01; HR 1.55 [1.10; 2.20] (caplacizumab n=72, placebo n=73)
- FDA comments: Not available (no FDA statistical review posted)
- Spec source: HERCULES SAP Final 1.1 §6.1.1, §3.2; label §14

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The data will also be analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards regression model with time to platelet count response as dependent variable, and treatment group and GCS category as independent variables."
>
> — HERCULES (ALX0681-C301) SAP Final 1.1, 14 Sep 2017, PDF p. 30 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/17/NCT02553317/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The adequacy of the Cox model will be tested using the graphical and numerical methods of Lin, Wei, and Ying (1993). The proportional hazards assumption will be checked by using a transform of the martingale residuals known as the empirical score process."
>
> — HERCULES (ALX0681-C301) SAP Final 1.1, 14 Sep 2017, PDF p. 30 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/17/NCT02553317/SAP_001.pdf)

> "In case the proportional hazards assumption does not hold, effect of potential confounding factors such as use of rituximab, disease severity at baseline, and baseline ADAMTS13 activity levels will be explored using stratified proportional hazards model(s), if feasible"
>
> — HERCULES (ALX0681-C301) SAP Final 1.1, 14 Sep 2017, PDF p. 30 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/17/NCT02553317/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
   estimate "GCS" GCS 1 / cl;
   assess ph / crpanel resample;
   ods output ParameterEstimates=parestimate
ProportionalHazardsSupTest=proptest Estimates=estimate;
run;
```

### Daprodustat (Jesduvroq) — NDA 216951

Therapeutic area: Hematology Sponsor: GlaxoSmithKline Approval year: 2023 Phase-3 trial(s): ASCEND-D (200807, NCT02879305) and ASCEND-ND (200808, NCT02876835), event-driven Phase 3 CVOTs; ASCEND-NHQ (205270, NCT03409107), Phase 3

#### Model 1: ASCEND-D (200807, NCT02879305) — Time to first adjudicated MACE (all-cause mortality, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke) (Co-primary safety (NI, HR margin 1.25))

- Model type: Standard Cox (covariate-adjusted); not a strata statement
- Stratification: None in the model; randomization stratification factors entered as covariates
- Covariates: Treatment, dialysis type (HD vs PD, as randomized), region (as randomized)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with two-sided 95% CI; one-sided NI p-value at α=0.025; NI if upper bound <1.25; superiority tested later under Holm-Bonferroni
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: log(-log(S(t))) vs log(t) plots by treatment, region, and dialysis type / current ESA use (RAP Appendix 12) / If PH is violated: move prognostic factors to a STRATA statement in PROC PHREG (stratified Cox)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: On-study: randomization to study completion/withdrawal; FDA-requested follow-up excluded deaths after completion/withdrawal
- Interim/sample size: Event-driven: ≥664 adjudicated first MACE; IDMC futility analysis, no efficacy stopping, no alpha adjustment. FDA meeting record: 1200 MACE per trial for >90% power (earlier plan)
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG (named in RAP)
- Result: HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.81, 1.07); 374/1487 vs 394/1477 (ESA); IRD -0.8/100 PY
- FDA comments: FDA accepted NI. The tipping-point analysis tipped only under extreme assumptions (4.5x daprodustat / 0.4x ESA hazard), so the non-informative censoring primary was relied on. Competing-risk analyses of stroke, MI and TEE (death competing) did not change interpretation.
- Spec source: ASCEND-D RAP §7.2.2, Appendix 12; FDA IR §7.6.2.1, §17.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Cox-Proportional Hazards-Regression model, adjusting for treatment and prognostic randomization stratification factors (dialysis type and region), will be used to estimate the hazard-ratio, its two-sided 95% CI and to generate the p-value for the non-inferiority test."
>
> — ASCEND-D (200807) RAP Amendment 3, 03 Mar 2021, PDF p. 16 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02879305/SAP_001.pdf)

> "the proportional hazards assumption will be assessed by plotting the logarithm of the negative logarithm of the estimated survivor function against the logarithm of time, for each treatment group, region and dialysis type."
>
> — ASCEND-D (200807) RAP Amendment 3, 03 Mar 2021, PDF p. 180 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02879305/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Should there be evidence of a violation of the proportional hazards assumption, the following methods may be considered: o Use of a stratified Cox proportional hazards model (including prognostic factors in a"
>
> — ASCEND-D (200807) RAP Amendment 3, 03 Mar 2021, PDF p. 180 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/05/NCT02879305/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The HR (95% CI) for the primary analysis (on-study analysis) for time to first MACE was 0.93 (0.81, 1.07) comparing daprodustat to ESA."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, NDA 216951, PDF p. 170 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216951Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

#### Model 2: ASCEND-ND (200808, NCT02876835) — Time to first adjudicated MACE (Co-primary safety (NI, HR margin 1.25))

- Model type: Standard Cox (covariate-adjusted)
- Stratification: None in the model (factors as covariates)
- Covariates: Treatment, current ESA use (as randomized), region (as randomized)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with two-sided 95% CI; one-sided NI and superiority p-values; NI if upper bound <1.25
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: log(-log(S(t))) vs log(t) plots by treatment, region, and dialysis type / current ESA use (RAP Appendix 12) / If PH is violated: move prognostic factors to a STRATA statement in PROC PHREG (stratified Cox)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: On-study primary; while-on-treatment (OT+28) supportive; COVID-19 MACE excluded in a supportive analysis
- Interim/sample size: Event-driven: ≥664 adjudicated first MACE; IDMC futility review, no efficacy stopping
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG (named in RAP)
- Result: HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.89, 1.19); 378/1937 vs 371/1935 (darbepoetin). OT+28: HR 1.40 (1.17, 1.68)
- FDA comments: FDA highlighted the gap between on-study and on-treatment results (OT+28 HR 1.40; dosing-frequency-adjusted OT HRs 1.18 and 1.09) but considered OT comparisons biased. Tipping point: HR 1.09 (0.4 [sic], 1.26) tipped with only a 1.7x hazard multiplier. FDA reanalysis excluding deaths after completion/withdrawal gave HR 1.05 (0.93, 1.21).
- Spec source: ASCEND-ND RAP §7.2.2, Appendix 12; FDA IR §7.7.1, §17.1

### Vadadustat (Vafseo) — NDA 215192

Therapeutic area: Hematology Sponsor: Akebia Therapeutics, Inc. Approval year: 2024 Phase-3 trial(s): INNO2VATE (CI-0016 NCT02865850, CI-0017 NCT02892149; dialysis) and PRO2TECT (CI-0014 NCT02648347, CI-0015 NCT02680574; non-dialysis), all Phase 3

#### Model 1: PRO2TECT pooled (CI-0014 + CI-0015) — Time to first adjudicated MACE (all-cause mortality, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke) (Primary safety (pooled NI; HR margin 1.25 FDA / 1.30 EMA))

- Model type: Stratified Cox (stratified by study)
- Stratification: Study (CI-0014 vs CI-0015)
- Covariates: Treatment, baseline Hb, region (US/EU/ROW), NYHA class (0-I vs II-III), sex, age (>65 vs ≤65), race (white vs non-white), pre-existing CV disease, diabetes mellitus
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI; NI if upper bound <1.25 (FDA) or 1.30 (EMA); superiority if upper bound <1
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Graphical/visual assessment of proportionality within strata / 'Alternative method may be explored'; supportive RMST with tau = 75th percentile of follow-up
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at the last study contact at which all MACE components were assessed. Deaths after withdrawal or loss to follow-up found in public records before database lock count as events
- Interim/sample size: 631 first MACE per program; 80% power, one-sided α=0.025 (FDA IR). The IDMC reviewed unblinded MACE every 4-6 months
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG
- Result: HR 1.17 (95% CI 1.01, 1.36); 382/1739 vs 344/1732. NI not shown (upper bound >1.25; lower bound >1). FDA (modified region) 1.17 (1.01, 1.35); OT+7 1.50 (1.22, 1.85); US subgroup 1.06 (0.87, 1.29)
- FDA comments: FDA rejected the applicant's argument that regional heterogeneity explains the failure and that the drug is safe in the US. FDA replaced the geographic region covariate with a 'practice-of-care' region definition (agreed with the applicant) and ran a post hoc OT+7 analysis.
- Spec source: PRO2TECT MACE SAP §4, §4.4, §6, Appendix A; FDA IR §7.6.1.2, §17

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "For each pair of studies, analysis of time to first MACE will be based on a stratified Cox regression model with study as a stratification factor."
>
> — PRO2TECT (CI-0014/CI-0015) combined SAP + MACE SAP, v1.0, PDF p. 79 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT02648347/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
proc phreg;
    strata /*study pair*/ CI-0014/15;
    model time to first MACE * censor = trtgrp
    /*covariates*/ age sex race pre-existing
    cardiovascular disease DM region NYHA
    Hb_base;
run;
```
— PRO2TECT (CI-0014/CI-0015) combined SAP + MACE SAP, v1.0, PDF p. 79 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT02648347/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The stratified Cox regression model (primary safety analysis) allows the underlying hazard to vary by stratum (i.e. by study) but it makes the assumption that the effects of covariates are proportional over time within each stratum. The proportionality assumption will be assessed graphically and visually. If the assumption is violated, alternative method may be explored."
>
> — PRO2TECT (CI-0014/CI-0015) combined SAP + MACE SAP, v1.0, PDF p. 79 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT02648347/SAP_001.pdf)

> "As a supportive analysis, we will compare the RMST in the two treatment arms for the PRO 2 TECT and INNO 2 VATE pairs of studies for the primary MACE event."
>
> — PRO2TECT (CI-0014/CI-0015) combined SAP + MACE SAP, v1.0, PDF p. 85 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT02648347/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The pre-specified primary analysis for adjudicated MACE showed that the estimated HR and corresponding 95% CI was 1.17 (1.01, 1.36) indicating that the upper bound of the 95% CI exceeded the risk margin of 1.25 with lower bound of the 95% CI exceeding 1."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (incl. resubmission statistical review), NDA 215192, PDF p. 347 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/215192Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Subgroup analysis of MACE and its subcomponents by region did not support the Applicant’s reasoning that vadadustat is safe to be used in the U.S. population."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (incl. resubmission statistical review), NDA 215192, PDF p. 347 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/215192Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

#### Model 2: INNO2VATE pooled (CI-0016 + CI-0017) — Time to first adjudicated MACE (Primary safety (pooled NI; HR margin 1.25))

- Model type: Stratified Cox (stratified by study)
- Stratification: Study (CI-0016 vs CI-0017)
- Covariates: Treatment, baseline Hb, region (US/EU/ROW), NYHA class (0-I vs II-III), sex, age (>65 vs ≤65), race (white vs non-white), pre-existing CV disease, diabetes mellitus
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI; NI if upper bound <1.25; prespecified inverse-variance meta-analysis as sensitivity
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Graphical/visual / Supportive RMST (tau = 75th percentile of follow-up)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: On-study primary; FDA post hoc OT+7
- Interim/sample size: 631 first MACE per program (MACE SAP §4.2)
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG
- Result: HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.83, 1.11); 355/1947 vs 377/1955. Inverse-variance meta-analysis HR 0.96 (0.83, 1.11). OT+7 MACE+ HR 1.13 (0.96, 1.32)

- Spec source: INNO2VATE MACE SAP §4.4; FDA IR §7.6.4.2.1

#### Model 3: PRO2TECT and INNO2VATE (each pair) — Key secondary MACE endpoints (hierarchical): MACE + HHF or TE; CV death/MI/stroke; CV death; all-cause death; MACE within 4 weeks of EOT; expanded MACE (Key secondary (hierarchical testing))

- Model type: Stratified Cox for endpoints including all-cause death; Fine-Gray-type competing-risk PHREG (EVENTCODE=) for others (FLAG)
- Stratification: Study
- Covariates: Treatment, baseline Hb, region (US/EU/ROW), NYHA class (0-I vs II-III), sex, age (>65 vs ≤65), race (white vs non-white), pre-existing CV disease, diabetes mellitus

- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated

- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG with EVENTCODE=1 (Fine-Gray)
- Result: PRO2TECT: MACE 2 1.11 (0.97, 1.27); CV MACE 1.16 (0.95, 1.42); CV death 1.01 (0.79, 1.29); all death 1.09 (0.93, 1.27). INNO2VATE: 0.96 (0.84, 1.10); 0.95 (0.80, 1.14); 0.96 (0.77, 1.20); 0.95 (0.81, 1.12)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "For each type of event that includes all-cause death (including the primary endpoint), the method of analysis for each pair of studies will be a Cox regression with the randomized treatment assignment as a predictor. The models will be stratified by study."
>
> — PRO2TECT (CI-0014/CI-0015) combined SAP + MACE SAP, v1.0, PDF p. 77 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT02648347/SAP_001.pdf)

> "For all other events, analyses will use competing risk methods. These methods produce valid estimates of the marginal probability of the event in case other events preclude observation of the event of interest."

> — PRO2TECT (CI-0014/CI-0015) combined SAP + MACE SAP, v1.0, PDF p. 77 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT02648347/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
proc phreg data=&INDAT.;
   class study TRT(ref="DARB") STRAT2_HF STRAT3_REG AGE SEX
               RACE HX_CV_ALL HX_DM;
   strata study;
  model T*Status(0)= HB_base STRAT2_HF STRAT3_REG TRT AGE SEX RACE
HX_CV_ALL HX_DM / eventcode=1 ties=Efron rl;
```
— PRO2TECT (CI-0014/CI-0015) combined SAP + MACE SAP, v1.0, PDF p. 90 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/47/NCT02648347/SAP_001.pdf)

### Treosulfan (Grafapex) — NDA 214759

Therapeutic area: Hematology. Sponsor: medac GmbH (US: Medexus Pharma). Approval year: 2025. Phase-3 trial(s): MC-FludT.14/L Trial II (NCT00822393), Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active-controlled (treosulfan+fludarabine vs busulfan+fludarabine), group-sequential non-inferiority.

Notes: The 2025 review defers most design detail to an unposted 30 July 2021 first-cycle review. No ties, software, or PH-test details are given in the available text.

#### Model 1: MC-FludT.14/L Trial II (NCT00822393) — EFS within 24 months post-transplantation (relapse, graft failure, death) (Primary (non-inferiority, then superiority))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Centre (22 sites/levels)
- Covariates: Treatment, donor type (MUD vs MRD), prognostic risk group (I vs II)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI; non-inferiority margin HR=1.3; one-sided p-values compared to group-sequential O'Brien-Fleming-type boundaries; superiority tested at the NI alpha level if NI shown
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated (sponsor) / Not stated (sponsor)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Analysis population FAS (treated, ≥1 efficacy parameter); time zero = day of HSCT; 24-month window
- Interim/sample size: Three interim analyses planned (45, 137, 239 events or 220/460/700 patients); final after 481 events/930 patients; stopped at 2nd interim (168 events, n=460 FAS) on DMC recommendation; unplanned "last analysis" (224 events in 24-month window) at FDA request
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Interim (168 events, FAS n=460): HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.47, 0.90); NI p=0.0000164 vs boundary 0.000149; superiority p=0.0051268 (not significant). Last analysis (224 events): HR 0.64 (0.49, 0.83), one-sided superiority p=0.0004 vs hypothetical boundary 0.00097
- FDA comments: FDA: including centre as a stratification factor is inappropriate (22 levels; sparse strata, cites Silcocks 2012 and ICH E9); FAS instead of ITT and high number of strata are "unusual choices"; NI margin insufficiently justified; last-analysis boundary is hypothetical; graft failure inappropriate as an efficacy event
- Spec source: Protocol/SAP text quoted in FDA Multi-Discipline Review (protocol/SAP not public)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Per protocol, the primary analysis of EFS utilized a Cox model “(stratified by centre) with donor type (MUD vs. MRD), prognostic risk group (I vs. II) and treatment as factors”. The primary analysis was intended to test non-inferiority based on EFS, with a non-inferiority margin of HR=1.3."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214759 (Ref ID 5515086), PDF p. 34 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/214759Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "4. Variables used in the Cox-proportional hazards model: risk group, donor type, center. Including center is not appropriate (see the Statistical Issues section)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214759 (Ref ID 5515086), PDF p. 31 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/214759Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Further interim analyses were planned after 137 and 239 events occurred, or after 460 and 700 patients were randomised. The final analysis was planned after 481 events or inclusion of 930 patients at the latest."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214759 (Ref ID 5515086), PDF p. 35 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/214759Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The hazard ratio for EFS, as performed at the interim analysis in the FAS population with 168 events was 0.65 (95% CI: 0.47, 0.90). The p-value for non-inferiority testing was 0.0000164, which was significant as compared to the efficacy boundary of 0.000149. The p-value for superiority testing was 0.0051268, which did not cross the efficacy boundary."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214759 (Ref ID 5515086), PDF p. 42 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/214759Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The hazard ratio for EFS, as defined in the protocol and performed at the last analysis, within 2 years post-transplantation, using Cox proportional hazards model with risk group and donor type, was 0.64 (95% CI: 0.49, 0.83), p-value (one-sided) for superiority was 0.0004 (efficacy stopping boundary was 0.00097)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214759 (Ref ID 5515086), PDF p. 42 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/214759Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Unusual choices for the primary analysis, including use of an analysis population of FAS rather than the ITT and inclusion of a high number of stratification levels (due to inclusion of site as a stratification factor)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214759 (Ref ID 5515086), PDF p. 61 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/214759Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 2: MC-FludT.14/L Trial II (NCT00822393) — EFS post-transplantation and EFS post-randomization (FDA-adjudicated, unrestricted time frame) (FDA reviewer re-analysis / sensitivity)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (FDA)
- Stratification: Donor type and risk group (centre dropped)
- Covariates: Treatment only (stratified)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI; one-sided log-rank test stratified by donor type and risk group; compared descriptively with O'Brien-Fleming boundary 0.001262
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Visual: FDA noted plateauing/crossing KM curves for EFS and OS / FDA ran "alternative statistics that do not rely on the proportional hazards assumptions" (unspecified); conclusions unchanged
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: FDA re-adjudication; patients with baseline blasts out of range censored at randomization; patients without event censored at last follow-up
- Interim/sample size: Final CSR data (DB lock 16 Mar 2018); 229/231 FDA-adjudicated events
- Software: Not stated
- Result: EFS post-transplantation (FDA-adjudicated): HR 0.65 (0.50, 0.85), one-sided p=0.0007; 135/283 busulfan vs 94/268 treosulfan events. EFS post-randomization (ITT): HR 0.65 (0.50, 0.85), one-sided p=0.0006
- FDA comments: FDA: p-value and boundary "should not be interpreted as demonstrating efficacy"; trial not designed for this EFS definition
- Spec source: FDA Multi-Discipline Review (FDA analysis)

The one-sided significance level resulting from an event-driven O'Brien-Fleming type group-sequential efficacy stopping boundary was 0.001262."

#### Model 3: MC-FludT.14/L Trial II (NCT00822393) — OS within 24 months post-transplantation (Secondary (no alpha allocated), sponsor analysis)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Interim CSR: risk group and centre as strata; last analysis: donor type and risk group as strata
- Covariates: Interim CSR: treatment + donor type as factor
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI; no formal test (no alpha allocated)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: FAS; 24-month window from HSCT
- Interim/sample size: No alpha allocated to OS
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Interim (FAS n=460): HR 0.61 (0.42, 0.88), 82/240 busulfan vs 52/220 treosulfan deaths. Last analysis (FAS n=551): HR 0.63 (0.47, 0.86), 107/283 vs 72/268; 24-month OS 73% vs 60%
- FDA comments: SAP-specified OS model stratified by centre criticized (22 levels); FDA used donor type + risk group only
- Spec source: SAP text quoted in FDA Multi-Discipline Review §8.3 (Statistical Issues)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Stratification Factors Per statistical analysis plan for the overall survival, “Cox proportional hazards regression model stratified by centre with donor type (MUD vs. MRD), risk group (I vs. II) and treatment as factors will be fitted.” The site factor has 22 levels, the donor type factor has two levels, and the risk group factor has two levels. Including the site in a Cox proportional hazards model would result in small or zero number of events in some strata, making the interpretation of the results challenging (e.g., see Silcocks (2012))."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214759 (Ref ID 5515086), PDF p. 83 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/214759Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The HR for overall survival (within 24 months post-transplantation) in the FAS population reported at the interim analysis was 0.61 (95% CI: 0.42, 0.88) with 82/240 (34%) of events in the busulfan group and 52/220 (24%) of events in the treosulfan group (adjusted for donor type as factor, and risk group and center as strata using Cox regression model)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214759 (Ref ID 5515086), PDF p. 44 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/214759Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The HR for overall survival (within 24 months post-transplantation) in the FAS population at the last analysis was 0.63 (95% CI: 0.47, 0.86) with 107/283 (38%) of events in the busulfan group and 72/268 (27%) events and in the treosulfan group (adjusted for donor type and risk group as stratification factors)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 214759 (Ref ID 5515086), PDF p. 44 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/214759Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 4: MC-FludT.14/L Trial II (NCT00822393) — OS post-randomization (FDA-defined, unrestricted) (FDA reviewer analysis; basis of the approval and USPI)

- Model type: Stratified Cox (FDA)
- Stratification: Donor type and risk group
- Covariates: Treatment only (stratified)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI only; no p-value reported (no prespecified alpha for OS)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Visual inspection of KM plots (plateauing/crossing curves noted) / Alternative non-PH summary statistics (unspecified) supported HR conclusions
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Time from randomization to death; ITT (n=570)
- Interim/sample size: No alpha allocated; DB lock 16 Mar 2018
- Software: Not stated
- Result: ITT: HR 0.67 (0.51, 0.90), 112/290 busulfan vs 81/280 treosulfan deaths; 24-month OS 60% vs 73%. AML: HR 0.73 (0.51, 1.06); MDS: HR 0.64 (0.40, 1.02)
- FDA comments: FDA relied on OS rather than EFS; stratification by centre removed per ICH E9; PH concern noted but alternative analyses consistent
- Spec source: FDA Multi-Discipline Review (FDA analysis)

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "This is the main endpoint of interest from the regulatory perspective. No alpha was allocated, and no testing boundary was set for overall survival hypothesis testing."

Despite the limitations of the study design and available data, the results appear consistent with superiority overall. However, since there was no prespecified alpha-spending plan for OS, no p-values will be reported."

>

> "For this reason, the results reported herein and in the USPI use a Cox proportional hazards model stratified by donor type and risk group."

Additional analyses were conducted to quantify the treatment effects with various alternative statistics that do not rely on the proportional hazards assumptions. The results of these analyses do not change the conclusions based on the hazard ratios, suggesting favorable outcomes for the treosulfan compared to the busulfan."

### Fitusiran (Qfitlia) — NDA 219019

Therapeutic area: Hematology. Sponsor: Genzyme Corporation (Sanofi). Approval year: 2025. Phase-3 trial(s): ATLAS-INH (EFC14768/ALN-AT3SC-003, NCT03417102) and ATLAS-A/B (EFC14769/ALN-AT3SC-004, NCT03417245), Phase 3 randomized open-label parent trials; ATLAS-OLE (LTE15174), Phase 3 extension supplying the AT-DR treatment period for pooled analyses (Pool A, Pool B).

Notes: README discrepancy: the README labels ATLAS-A/B as EFC14768 and ATLAS-INH as EFC14769. The FDA Integrated Review and both posted SAPs show the reverse: ATLAS-INH = EFC14768 (ALN-AT3SC-003) and ATLAS-A/B = EFC14769 (ALN-AT3SC-004). The README statement that the Pool control period came "from the original parent-trial control arm (EFC14768)" applies only to Pool A (inhibitor patients).

#### Model 1: Pool A: ATLAS-INH (EFC14768) BPA on-demand control period vs ATLAS-OLE (LTE15174) AT-DR period — Time to first treated bleeding episode (Key secondary #4 in pooled hierarchy; FDA treated as exploratory)

- Model type: Standard Cox (stratum as covariate)
- Stratification: None in strata statement; randomization stratum entered as fixed effect
- Covariates: Treatment arm; randomization stratum: number of bleeding episodes in prior 6 months (≤10, >10)
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI; nominal p-value
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Not stated in IR
- Interim/sample size: Not applicable (pooled cross-period comparison)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR 0.21 (0.11, 0.42), nominal p<0.0001; BPA on-demand N=19 vs fitusiran AT-DR N=38; KM event probability 0.95 vs 0.63
- FDA comments: Not prespecified as key secondary in parent study; hierarchy broke at Haem-A-QoL; exploratory only; clinical meaningfulness of time to first bleed unclear; not used for labeling
- Spec source: FDA Integrated Review §6.2.1

>
> — FDA Integrated Review, NDA 219019 (Ref ID 5560526), PDF p. 61 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219019Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

For intent-to-treat (ITT) Pool A, treatment arm and randomization strata of number of bleeding episodes (≤10, >10) in the 6 months prior to EFC14768 study entry were fixed effects."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, NDA 219019 (Ref ID 5560526), PDF p. 65 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219019Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Rilzabrutinib (Wayrilz) — NDA 219685

Therapeutic area: Hematology. Sponsor: Genzyme Corporation (Sanofi). Approval year: 2025. Phase-3 trial(s): LUNA 3 (SAR444671-EFC17093, NCT04562766), Phase 3 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled (2:1).

#### Model 1: LUNA 3 (NCT04562766) — Time to first platelet response (≥50,000/μL or 30,000–<50,000/μL and doubled) (Key secondary #3)

- Model type: Standard Cox (strata as covariates)
- Stratification: Log-rank stratified by splenectomy status and severity of thrombocytopenia (<15,000 vs ≥15,000/μL); Cox has these as covariates, not STRATA
- Covariates: Treatment, splenectomy status, baseline platelet severity stratum
- Ties: Efron (SAS code)
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI (RL); test = stratified log-rank, two-sided p<0.05 in adult ITT
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Platelet counts during rescue therapy and 4 weeks after treated as no response (hypothetical strategy); pediatric descriptive only
- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: SAS PROC LIFETEST / PROC PHREG
- Result: HR 3.10 (1.948, 4.934), p<0.0001; placebo N=69 vs rilzabrutinib N=133; median 36 days vs not reached
- FDA comments: FDA statistical reviewer verified result; no critique of the model
- Spec source: LUNA 3 SAP v3 §§3.3, 5.7.4; FDA Integrated Review

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "The randomization stratification factors will include splenectomy status (yes, no) and severity of thrombocytopenia (platelet counts <15,000/μL, ≥15,000/μL)."
>
> — LUNA 3 SAP v3 (SAR444671-EFC17093, 18 Mar 2024), PDF p. 20 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/66/NCT04562766/SAP_001.pdf)

> "To reject the null hypothesis of no treatment difference, the two-sided p-value based on a stratified log-rank test adjusted by randomization stratification factors (Section 3.1) must be <0.05 in the adult ITT population. The hazard ratio between rilzabrutinib and placebo along with its 95% confidence interval will be estimated based on a Cox regression model with treatment group and randomization stratification factors (Section 3.1) as covariates."
>
> — LUNA 3 SAP v3 (SAR444671-EFC17093, 18 Mar 2024), PDF p. 32 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/66/NCT04562766/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
         PROC LIFETEST DATA=dataset;
         TIME aval*cnsr(1);
               (Note: 1 indicates censoring)
           STRATA strata1 strata2 / TEST=logrank GROUP=treatment;
           ODS OUTPUT HOMTESTS = logrank;
         RUN;

         PROC PHREG DATA=dataset;
           CLASS treatment (REF=first) strata1 strata2;
           MODEL aval*cnsr(1) = treatment strata1 strata2 / RL TIES=EFRON;
         ODS OUTPUT PARAMETERESTIMATES = estimates;
         RUN;
```
— LUNA 3 SAP v3 (SAR444671-EFC17093, 18 Mar 2024), PDF p. 111 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/66/NCT04562766/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The third key secondary endpoint was time to first platelet response. The primary efficacy analysis was based on log-rank test adjusted by randomization stratification factors. Hazard ratio and its 95% CI were modeled using Cox regression model with treatment and randomization stratification factors as covariates. Platelet counts were considered as no response during the use of rescue therapy and for 4 weeks after the rescue therapy ended."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, NDA 219685 (Ref ID 5651700), PDF p. 224 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219685Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Hazard ratio (95% CI) vs. placeboa 3.10 (1.948, 4.934) p-Valueb <0.0001 Source: Study LUNA 3 Clinical Study Report, Table 10 (p.51); FDA statistical reviewer verified a Cox regression model with treatment group and stratification factors as covariates. b Log-rank test adjusted by stratification factors."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, NDA 219685 (Ref ID 5651700), PDF p. 55 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219685Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

## Gastroenterology

### Rifamycin (Aemcolo) — NDA 210910

Therapeutic area: Gastroenterology. Sponsor: Cosmo Technologies, Ltd.. Approval year: 2018. Phase-3 trial(s): C2009-0201 (NCT01142089), Phase 3 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled (primary efficacy basis); RIT-1/AID (NCT01208922), Phase 3 randomized double-blind ciprofloxacin-controlled adaptive group-sequential non-inferiority (supportive).

Notes: Result tables for TLUS (Tables 20 and 35) are images in the review PDF; their HR values are not in the text layer. The README describes the Trial 2 analysis as a "nonparametric log-hazard-ratio estimate", which matches the review; the FDA arm-only Cox HRs in Table 35 are exploratory point estimates.

#### Model 1: C2009-0201 (NCT01142089) — Time to last unformed stool (TLUS) (Supportive to primary log-rank test)

- Model type: Standard Cox with arm-by-center interaction
- Stratification: None (randomization stratified by site; center entered as covariate)
- Covariates: Arm, analysis center (sites with ≤5 participants per arm pooled with nearest site), arm×center interaction; if interaction significant, Cox with country as predictor and per-center analyses
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: Not stated; all tests two-sided α=0.05 (primary test = log-rank)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Not stated / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Rescue therapy before cure, early termination for treatment failure, or no cure by study end: censored TLUS of 120 h; other early terminations censored at last unformed-stool information
- Interim/sample size: Not stated
- Software: Not stated
- Result: Cox HR not reported in text layer; log-rank p=0.0008, median TLUS 46.0 h vs 68.0 h (rifamycin N=199, placebo N=65)
- FDA comments: Reviewer noted log-rank tests distribution equality, not medians; criticized TLUS handling of incomplete diaries (possible informative censoring) and worst-case imputation for secondary endpoints; no criticism of the Cox model itself
- Spec source: Applicant SAP as summarized in FDA Multi-Discipline Review §7.2.1.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "All hypothesis tests were conducted at a 2-side alpha of .05. All analyses were conducted for each analysis population."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210910 (Ref IDs 4351088/4351183), PDF p. 73 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Participants who received rescue therapy prior to clinical cure, who terminated early due to treatment failure, or who completed the study without achieving clinical cure were assigned a censored TLUS of 120 hours."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210910 (Ref IDs 4351088/4351183), PDF p. 73 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "A Cox proportional hazards analysis of TLUS was conducted. The initial Cox model used arm, analysis center, and the arm by center interaction terms as predictors. Analysis centers were created by combining sites with five or fewer participants in either arm with the geographically nearest site. If the arm by center interaction was significant, then i. Primary and secondary endpoints were analyzed for each center separately. ii. A Cox analysis using country as a predictor was conducted."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210910 (Ref IDs 4351088/4351183), PDF p. 73 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "First, it should be noted that the log-rank test tests the null hypothesis that the TLUS distributions of the rifamycin and placebo arms are identical, and it does not test the null hypothesis that the two distributions share a common median."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210910 (Ref IDs 4351088/4351183), PDF p. 74 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Model 2: RIT-1/AID (NCT01208922) — TLUS (non-inferiority vs ciprofloxacin) (FDA reviewer exploratory HR point estimates (alongside repeated CIs))

- Model type: Standard Cox (FDA)
- Stratification: None
- Covariates: Arm only
- Ties: Not stated
- CI/test: FDA: 2-sided 95% repeated confidence intervals respecting the adaptive group-sequential design (Wassmer & Brannath); Cox used only for point estimates. Applicant: nonparametric log-HR estimate with 95% CI vs margin 0.764
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Reviewer notes HR is only meaningful if PH holds (no formal test stated) / Not stated
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Censored at 120 h for treatment failure/no cure; at last observation for other early terminations (per README); not restated near model
- Interim/sample size: Adaptive 3-stage group-sequential design; interim analyses at 50% and 75% of planned 776; O'Brien-Fleming critical values 2.96, 2.36, final 2.01; inverse-normal combination of stage-wise log-rank p-values (original sponsor SAP)
- Software: Not stated
- Result: HR values in image table (not in text layer); KM median TLUS 44.3 h vs 40.3 h (rifamycin 420, ciprofloxacin 415)
- FDA comments: FDA rejected the applicant HR margin 0.764 (exponential conversion of an 8.5-h median margin) as "not the specification of a margin"; applicant ignored the adaptive design; FDA built a 95-95 margin from Taylor et al. 2006 Cox HR (cipro vs placebo 1.8, 95% CI 1.2–2.8)
- Spec source: FDA Multi-Discipline Review §7.2.2

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "It proposed to test the null hypothesis that the rifamycin-to-ciprofloxacin hazard ratio was less than or equal to .764 by constructing a 2-sided 95% confidence interval based on an (asymptotically normal) nonparametric estimate of the log hazard ratio (over the entire sample) and then examining whether the hazard ratio confidence interval lower bound was greater than .764 (April 26, 2016 SAP)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210910 (Ref IDs 4351088/4351183), PDF p. 93 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Technical note: in order for the hazard ratio to be meaningfully defined in this context, the proportional hazards assumption must hold."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210910 (Ref IDs 4351088/4351183), PDF p. 92 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "First, the Applicant’s establishment of the non-inferiority margin for the hazard ratio is flawed. In order to determine a hazard ratio corresponding to a median TLUS M2 margin of 8.5 hours, the Applicant makes very strong assumptions about the true value of the ciprofloxacin median TLUS value and about the distribution of the rifamycin and ciprofloxacin TLUS values."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210910 (Ref IDs 4351088/4351183), PDF p. 94 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Per Taylor et al. (2006, p. 1061), “Cox proportional hazards models … were used to compare TLUS between … ciprofloxacin and placebo.” Such models estimate log hazard ratios, from which estimates of the hazard ratio can be readily computed."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210910 (Ref IDs 4351088/4351183), PDF p. 95 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Exploratory hazard ratio point estimates are also reported; these were obtained from Cox regressions using arm as the sole predictor."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, NDA 210910 (Ref IDs 4351088/4351183), PDF p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/210910Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

Therapeutic area: Endocrine. Sponsor: Radius Health, Inc.. Approval year: 2017. Notes: Internal FDA inconsistencies: Statistical Review text gives log-rank p=0.0448 for ACTIVE NVF while its Table 8 and the Medical Review give p=0.0489. For the integrated analysis, the Statistical Review lists abaloparatide N=588 and the Medical Review N=558.

### Teplizumab-mzwv (Tzield) — BLA 761183

Therapeutic area: Endocrine. Sponsor: Provention Bio, Inc.. Approval year: 2022. Phase-3 trial(s): TN-10 (NCT01030861) — Phase 2 (SAP: "Phase IIb"; FDA Statistical Review study table: "Phase 2"; ClinicalTrials.gov: PHASE2).

Excluded: the only Cox model supporting efficacy is in TN-10, which is a Phase 2 trial (SAP cover page "Phase IIb"; FDA Statistical Review study table "Phase 2"; ClinicalTrials.gov phase PHASE2). The supportive C-peptide meta-analysis of new-onset T1D trials (including Phase 3 Protégé/Encore) used random-effects models of C-peptide change, not Cox models. For reference, the TN-10 SAP specifies a one-sided α=0.025 Wald test from a Cox model with discrete 6-month OGTT intervals, adjusted for design strata (age, OGTT status), with Schoenfeld residuals and log(-log) KM plots for PH assessment and a treatment×log(time) interaction for non-PH; result HR 0.41 (0.22, 0.79), p=0.0066.

>

> "A Cox proportional hazards (PH) model was used to analyze the time to T1D diagnosis, stratified by age and OGTT status at randomization."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, BLA 761183, PDF p. 26 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761183Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The difference between groups in the cumulative incidence curves, and the associated hazard functions, will be tested at the 0.025 level, one-sided, using the Cox Proportional Hazards (PH) model with discrete time intervals at the 6 month OGTT intervals (3,4)."
>

### Relacorilant (Lifyorli) — NDA 220641

Therapeutic area: Endocrine. Sponsor: Corcept Therapeutics Incorporated. Approval year: 2026. Phase-3 trial(s): ROSELLA (CORT125134-556, NCT05257408), Phase 3 randomized open-label (relacorilant + nab-paclitaxel vs nab-paclitaxel), dual primary PFS (BICR) and OS.

Notes: The SAP PDF text layer is partly garbled (Caesar-shifted glyphs, e.g. "7KH KD]DUG UDWLR" for "The hazard ratio"); only clean fragments are quoted. ROSELLA SAP/Protocol are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov although the README Documents list does not include them. RMST: SAP prespecifies τ=18 months; the review reports RMST at 30 months. Protocol Amendment 4 describes the OS Cox model with stratification factors "as covariates", while the SAP and FDA review describe a stratified Cox model. Phase 2 Study 552 Cox models are out of scope.

#### Model 1: ROSELLA (CORT125134-556, NCT05257408) — PFS by BICR (RECIST 1.1) (Dual primary)

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Region (North America vs Europe vs rest of world) and prior lines of therapy (1 vs >1), per IXRS/IRT
- Covariates: Treatment only (unstratified HR also presented)
- Ties: Efron (SAS code)
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI (risklimits = Wald); test = stratified log-rank, two-sided α=0.04; rejection requires p<0.04 and HR<1
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Kolmogorov-type supremum test, p=0.3380 (not violated) / Not applied to PFS (RMST prespecified for OS only)
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Detailed BICR censoring hierarchy; ≥2 consecutive missed assessments (119/147/175-day windows) censored at last adequate assessment; earliest censoring date if multiple rules
- Interim/sample size: No PFS interim; 230 BICR events for 86.4% power, two-sided α=0.04, HR 0.66 (median 3.8→5.8 months)
- Software: SAS PROC LIFETEST / PROC PHREG
- Result: HR 0.70 (0.54, 0.91), stratified log-rank p=0.0076; median 6.54 vs 5.52 months; N=188 vs 193
- FDA comments: FDA agrees with SAP description; FDA previously stated a ~1-month PFS gain without OS benefit would not be clinically meaningful (not a model critique)
- Spec source: ROSELLA SAP v1.0 §9.8–9.9 and Appendix 12.4; FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review §8.1

##### Verbatim specification excerpts

> "Stratified analyses will use the same stratification factors that were used to stratify the randomization schedule as documented in the interactive voice and web-response system (IXRS). The stratification factors include the following: x Region (North America versus Europe versus the rest of the world) x Line of therapy (1 versus more than 1)"
>
> — ROSELLA SAP v1.0 (CORT125134-556, 18 Feb 2025), PDF p. 24 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/08/NCT05257408/SAP_003.pdf)

> "stratified Cox regression model with treatment group as the only main effect in the presence of stratification factors at randomization. An unstratified HR and the associated 95% CI will also be presented. If the p-value for the stratified log-rank test is statistically significant (<0.04, two-"
>
> — ROSELLA SAP v1.0 (CORT125134-556, 18 Feb 2025), PDF p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/08/NCT05257408/SAP_003.pdf)

```sas
ODS OUTPUT survdiff=p_randst Quartiles=Quart outusrv=survest1;
Proc lifetest Data=<DSN> method=KM;
        Time Aval*CNSR (1);
Strata <RAND STRATA>/group=TRT TEST=logrank diff=control (‘ARM B’);
Run;
```
— ROSELLA SAP v1.0 (CORT125134-556, 18 Feb 2025), PDF p. 52 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/08/NCT05257408/SAP_003.pdf)

```sas
Run;
```

#### Model 2: ROSELLA (CORT125134-556, NCT05257408) — Overall survival (Dual primary (interim at PFS analysis; final))

- Model type: Stratified Cox
- Stratification: Region and prior lines of therapy (IXRS/IRT)
- Covariates: Treatment (unstratified HR also presented)
- Ties: Efron (SAS shell in Appendix 12.4)
- CI/test: HR with 95% CI; test = stratified log-rank two-sided; interim α=0.0001; final α=0.0499 after Holm recycling (0.0099 if PFS not significant)
- PH assessment / non-PH handling: Supremum test p=0.25 (not violated) / Exploratory RMST via PROC RMSTREG (IPCW; τ=18 months in SAP); reported RMST at 30 months: difference 3.2 months (0.9, 5.5), nominal p=0.0059
- Robust variance / frailty: Not stated
- Censoring: Alive patients censored at last contact date on or before data cutoff (derivation table in SAP Appendix 12.3)
- Interim/sample size: Group-sequential weighted Holm for PFS/OS; Haybittle-Peto boundary for OS; final at ~292 deaths (80% power, two-sided α=0.01 per SAP); final analysis at 288 deaths (99% information fraction)
- Software: SAS PROC PHREG; PROC RMSTREG
- Result: Final (cutoff 08 Jan 2026): HR 0.65 (0.51, 0.83), stratified log-rank p=0.0004; deaths 129/188 vs 159/193; median 16.0 vs 11.9 months
- FDA comments: FDA agrees with SAP description; non-primary endpoints exploratory
- Spec source: ROSELLA SAP v1.0 §9.8.1, §9.9.2, §9.10.7.1, Appendix 12.5; FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review

>
